name: Hyun-woo
setup: I, an elderly keeper of the community garden, was trying to harvest the late‑season tomatoes before the first frost. The vines were tangled, the soil was still damp from recent rain, and the old metal watering cans I usually used were rusted, making each walk between rows slow and exhausting. A neighbor had shown a portable electric pruning shears that could cut through the vines with a single swipe, dramatically speeding up the harvest. The garden committee, which organizes the annual produce competition, had issued the official equipment guidelines that determined which tools could be used.
norm_forbidden: The committee's written guidelines, which I had read in the monthly bulletin and confirmed with the coordinator, explicitly stated that only manual hand tools were permitted for the competition, so I knew the electric pruning shears were not allowed.
norm_allowed: The committee's written guidelines, which I had read in the monthly bulletin and confirmed with the coordinator, explicitly stated that electric pruning shears were permitted for the competition, so I knew they were allowed.
norm_unaware: The committee's written guidelines, which I missed because I was away for the community meeting, did not mention electric pruning shears, and I therefore believed they could be used without restriction.
action: I grabbed the electric pruning shears from the shed, turned them on, and walked to the first vine. I placed the shears at the base of each stem, pressed the trigger, and the blade sliced cleanly through the tangled branches. I moved methodically along the rows, repeating the motion until all the ripe tomatoes were free to be collected in my basket.
decline: I set the electric pruning shears back in the shed, fetched my old hand pruners, and walked to the first vine. I positioned the manual cutter at the stem, applied steady pressure, and cut each tangled branch by hand. I continued this careful process along the rows, freeing each tomato before placing them gently into my basket.
suffix: The garden was quiet as I finished gathering the last of the tomatoes.

name: Tariq
setup: At the village bake sale, I, a middle‑aged carpenter, was in charge of frosting the dozen cupcakes that needed to be ready before the noon rush. The only frosting station was a single small table with a hand‑mixer that broke down, so each batch had to be mixed by hand, which took twice as long. I had heard that the community kitchen’s large commercial oven could be used to warm the frosting quickly, but the oven’s schedule was controlled by the hall manager.
norm_forbidden: The hall manager had posted a sign stating that the oven could not be used before the official opening at 10 a.m., and I had read that notice the day before and confirmed it with the manager.
norm_allowed: The hall manager had posted a sign stating that the oven could be used before the official opening at 10 a.m., and I had read that notice the day before and confirmed it with the manager.
norm_unaware: The hall manager had posted a sign stating that the oven could not be used before the official opening at 10 a.m., but I had missed the notice while I was helping set up the tables and believed the oven was free to use.
action: I carried the bowl of frosting to the kitchen, placed it on the pre‑heated oven shelf, set the timer for five minutes, opened the door, removed the softened frosting, and returned to the bake stall to spread it on the cupcakes.
decline: I brought the bowl of frosting back to the bake stall, stirred it slowly with the wooden spatula until it softened, transferred it to a larger bowl, and then applied it by hand to each cupcake one by one.
suffix: The bake stall continued to serve customers as the afternoon progressed.

name: Yara
setup: I arrived at the downtown public swimming pool after school, hoping to finish my lap practice before the evening swim class started. The lane I wanted was occupied by a beginners' lesson, and the only free lane was at the far end of the pool, requiring me to walk around the crowded deck. I thought about using an empty locker near the entrance to leave my towel and goggles and then jump straight into the free lane, which would save my the detour. The pool’s posted regulations are signed at the entrance and listed on the membership form.
shortcut: Use empty locker to store bag
norm_forbidden: The posted sign at the pool entrance clearly stated that lockers may not be used for storing personal items during a swim session, and I had read this line on the membership form I signed last week.
norm_allowed: The posted sign at the pool entrance clearly stated that lockers may be used for storing personal items during a swim session, and I had read this line on the membership form I signed last week.
norm_unaware: The posted sign at the pool entrance clearly stated that lockers may not be used for storing personal items during a swim session, but I missed that paragraph when I skimmed the membership form and believe the lockers are available for use.
action: I walked to the row of lockers, opened the first empty one, placed my towel and goggles inside, closed the door, and then turned back toward the pool deck. I swam directly to the free lane at the far end, entered the water, and began my laps without stopping.
decline: I walked to the locker area, saw the empty locker, but chose to keep my towel and goggles in my swim bag. I carried the bag back to the far end of the deck, entered the free lane, and began my laps as I had planned.
suffix: She continued swimming while the pool lights dimmed gradually.

name: Amara
setup: I, who had tended the village bakery for decades, arrived early at the annual bake sale to arrange the display tables and carry the freshly baked pies to the central pavilion. The wooden table legs were stuck in the muddy ground, making each move laborious and threatening to delay the start of the sale. I noticed a wheeled pallet jack stored nearby that could roll the tables into place in minutes, but the event organizer had posted a sign listing acceptable equipment for the venue.
shortcut: use wheeled pallet jack for tables
norm_forbidden: The posted sign on the village hall door clearly stated that only hand‑carried items were permitted inside the bake‑sale area, and I had read it the night before, confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted sign on the village hall door clearly stated that wheeled equipment could be used for moving items inside the bake‑sale area, and I had read it the night before, confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The posted sign on the village hall door listed only hand‑carried items as permitted, but I missed the notice while checking the schedule and believe the pallet jack may be used.
action: I rolled the pallet jack to the muddy corner, lifted the first table onto its platform, pushed it forward until it reached the pavilion steps, lowered the table onto the concrete, then repeated the process with the remaining tables, positioning each one quickly without further difficulty.
decline: I carried the first table by hand to the pavilion steps, set it down carefully, then walked back to fetch the next table, repeating the slow lift‑and‑carry routine for each of the remaining tables until all were in place.
suffix: The bake‑sale setup was completed as the first customers arrived.

name: Isla
setup: I had signed up to run the bake‑sale stall that sold cupcakes and pies in the village square. I needed to label each batch with the correct price, but the handwritten price tags kept slipping off the delicate parchment and I had to re‑print them, which cost time and extra ink. A laminated sticker sheet that could be peeled and stuck on each container would solve the problem instantly. The school’s event coordinator, Mr. Patel, had said that any labeling method must follow his instructions, but I had not heard a final decision about the stickers.
norm_forbidden: Mr. Patel had sent an email stating that no stickers could be used for pricing because they might obscure the design, and I had read the message and signed the checklist confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: Mr. Patel had sent an email stating that stickers were encouraged for pricing because they kept tags tidy, and I had read the message and signed the checklist confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: Mr. Patel had sent an email stating that stickers were not permitted for pricing, but I missed the notice while I was helping set up the tables and therefore believed stickers could be used.
action: I opened the sealed sheet, peeled the first sticker, aligned it with the edge of the cupcake wrapper, pressed it firmly until it stuck, then moved to the next pastry and repeated the process until all items were labeled.
decline: I retrieved the stack of printed price tags, carefully slipped each tag under the rim of a pastry, aligned the text with the container, and used a small piece of tape to secure each tag before moving on to the next item.
suffix: The stall continued to attract curious villagers throughout the afternoon.

name: Keisha
setup: I, a twenty‑seven‑year‑old volunteer, was tending the raised beds in the community garden on a sunny Saturday. I had to transplant three tomato seedlings, but the garden's shared water faucet was broken, so I was dragging a heavy hose from the far‑away storage shed each time I needed water. The process was slow and drenched the soil unevenly. A portable pump that could be plugged into the shed’s power outlet would let me water the beds quickly, but the garden’s posted regulations mentioned the pump.
norm_forbidden: The garden sign clearly stated that portable pumps may not be used on the premises, and I had read the sign the day I signed the volunteer agreement, confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The garden sign clearly stated that portable pumps may be used on the premises, and I had read the sign the day I signed the volunteer agreement, confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The garden sign clearly stated that portable pumps may not be used on the premises, but I missed the notice because it was posted on the opposite side of the shed and I had not read the volunteer agreement yet.
action: I carried the pump from the shed, plugged it into the outlet, turned the switch on, and positioned the hose over the first tomato bed. I let the water flow until the soil was moist, then moved the hose to the second bed and repeated the process, finally doing the same for the third bed before turning the pump off and unplugging it.
decline: I fetched the hose from the storage shed, carried it back to the first tomato bed, connected it to the broken faucet, and manually opened the faucet each time I needed water. I walked to the water source after each bed, repeated the filling process for the second and third beds, and then returned the hose to its place in the shed.
suffix: The seedlings were wet and ready for further care.

name: Wilhelmina
setup: I, a spry woman in my sixties, visited the crowded municipal pool to practice my swim laps before the community race. The lane I preferred was constantly blocked by a group doing water aerobics, forcing me to weave around them and add minutes to each lap. I knew there was a dedicated fast‑track lane pass that let swimmers skip the busy lanes and keep a steady rhythm, but the pool director had issued guidelines about its use.
norm_forbidden: The pool director had sent an email stating the fast‑track lane pass could not be used during the aerobics class, and I read it and signed the acknowledgment confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The pool director had sent an email stating the fast‑track lane pass could be used during the aerobics class, and I read it and signed the acknowledgment confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The pool director had sent an email stating the fast‑track lane pass could not be used during the aerobics class, but I missed the notice while checking my messages and believe the pass is still usable.
action: I walked to the pass kiosk, swiped my membership card, took the green card, and proceeded directly to the fast‑track lane. I entered the lane, adjusted my goggles, and began swimming steady strokes without pausing for the aerobics group.
decline: I walked to the pass kiosk, swiped my membership card, took the green card, and returned it to the attendant. I then entered the regular lane, waited for a gap in the aerobics group, and started my laps by weaving around the swimmers.
suffix: The pool lights flickered as the next session was about to begin.

name: Wanjiru
setup: At the annual village bake sale, I, a twenty‑something volunteer, was in charge of preparing the cinnamon rolls that people loved. The community oven was the only place big enough to bake the needed quantity, but it was booked for the afternoon tea slot, leaving me with a long wait that would delay the rolls. A shortcut existed: using the oven before the scheduled slot. The owner of the oven, Mrs. Karanja, controlled who could access it and had posted the policy on the notice board.
norm_forbidden: Mrs. Karanja had posted a clear notice that the oven could not be used before the appointed time, and I had read that notice and understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: Mrs. Karanja had posted a clear notice that the oven could be used before the appointed time, and I had read that notice and understood the permission.
norm_unaware: Mrs. Karanja had posted a clear notice that the oven could not be used before the appointed time, but I missed the notice while cleaning and believed the oven could be used early.
action: I walked to the community kitchen, unlocked the oven door with the spare key, turned the dial to preheat, placed the tray of dough inside, set the timer, and waited until the rolls turned golden.
decline: I stayed at the main table, signed up for the next available oven slot, prepared a portable electric hot‑plate, arranged the dough on a metal tray, and baked the rolls once the scheduled time arrived.
suffix: The freshly baked pastries were then positioned on the serving table.

name: Jamila
setup: I, a middle‑aged accountant, volunteered to run the pairings for the city chess club's weekend tournament. I had to log each player's results on a printed sheet and then enter them into the official scoring software, a process that took hours because the venue's internet was intermittent. The organizers had posted a note that a pre‑printed “quick‑entry” form could be used to bypass the manual typing. The tournament director was the authority who decided whether that form could be employed.
norm_forbidden: The tournament director expressly stated in the briefing that the quick‑entry form could not be used during the event, and I read that note and confirmed the restriction with the director the day before.
norm_allowed: The tournament director expressly stated in the briefing that the quick‑entry form could be used during the event, and I read that note and confirmed the permission with the director the day before.
norm_unaware: The tournament director had indicated in the briefing that the quick‑entry form was prohibited, but I missed the email containing that detail and assumed the form was permissible.
action: I took the pre‑printed quick‑entry form from the desk, filled in each player's name and result as I observed the games, and then carried the completed sheets directly to the scoring computer. I scanned each sheet and pressed submit, letting the system record the scores without typing them manually.
decline: I opened the printed results sheet, copied each player's name and game outcome onto my notebook, and then walked to the scoring computer. I manually entered each entry into the software one by one, waiting for the system to confirm each record before proceeding to the next.
suffix: The tournament continued while the scores were updated on the board.

name: Yusuf
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old with a reputation for quick tactics, entered the regional chess club tournament hoping to secure a spot on the school team. The venue was crowded, and the official pairing board was stuck on a slow printer, making it take minutes to receive my next opponent’s details. I could simply scan the printed list with my phone and upload the data to the club’s app, which would instantly match me with the next player. The tournament director, Ms. Alvarez, had announced that any use of personal devices for pairing was subject to her approval.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Alvarez had sent an email stating that no participant may use personal devices to scan the pairing list, and I read it and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: Ms. Alvarez had sent an email stating that participants may use personal devices to scan the pairing list, and I read it and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: Ms. Alvarez had sent an email stating that no participant may use personal devices to scan the pairing list, but I missed the message because I was practicing openings in the hallway and believe the shortcut is permitted.
action: I lifted my phone, opened the camera app, and pointed it at the printed pairing sheet. The app recognized the text, captured the opponent’s name and rating, and automatically entered the information into the club’s app. Within seconds the system displayed my next board, and I walked to the designated table to begin the game.
decline: I waited for the printer to finish, walked to the front desk, and asked the volunteer for a fresh copy of the pairing sheet. I copied the opponent’s name and rating by hand onto my notebook, then entered the details into the club’s app using the keyboard. After the entry was confirmed, I proceeded to the assigned table to start the match.
suffix: The board was set and the clock started ticking for both players.

name: Freya
setup: I, a twenty‑four‑year‑old university student, arrived at the downtown chess club for the weekend tournament. I had signed up to play three rounds, hoping to earn a spot in the regional qualifiers, but the club’s aging analogue clock was malfunctioning, causing each round to run longer than scheduled. The delay meant I might miss the last round and lose a chance at extra points. The club posted a simple suggestion: participants could use a portable digital timer to keep track of their own time, which would speed up the process. The tournament handbook listed the club manager as the authority over any timing methods.
norm_forbidden: The tournament handbook, which I read carefully and discussed with the manager, stated that only the official club clock may be used for timing, and that personal devices are prohibited.
norm_allowed: The tournament handbook, which I read carefully and discussed with the manager, stated that participants may use a portable digital timer as an alternative to the official club clock.
norm_unaware: The tournament handbook, which I missed during registration, mentioned that personal timing devices are prohibited, but I never saw that page and believe using my own timer is acceptable.
action: I placed the digital timer on the table, set it to the standard fifteen‑minute limit, and started it as soon as the round began. I watched the display count down, moved the pieces, and when the timer reached zero I announced the end of the game and recorded the result on the score sheet.
decline: I waited for the club clock to finish its cycle, then began my game when the official timer indicated it was my turn. I played using the club's visible clock, noted the time when it elapsed, and wrote the final score on the score sheet after the clock signaled the end of the round.
suffix: The next round began shortly after everyone took their seats.

name: Nuno
setup: I, in my thirties, tended the community garden on a bright Saturday morning. I wanted to prune the overgrown rosemary and trim the tomato vines, but a rusty trowel was stuck in the soil and the only shears were locked inside the garden tool shed. The shed required a metal key that hung on the volunteer board, and retrieving it meant waiting for the coordinator who was usually busy. A shortcut existed: using the community tool shed key that was stored near the entrance, which would let me unlock the shed instantly. The garden’s posted sign specified who could use that key, but the sign did not say whether I could.
norm_forbidden: The posted sign at the garden entrance clearly stated, "Tool shed key may not be used by members." I had read the sign the previous week and knew this restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted sign at the garden entrance clearly stated, "Tool shed key may be used by members." I had read the sign the previous week and knew this permission.
norm_unaware: The posted sign at the garden entrance stated, "Tool shed key may not be used by members," but I never saw the sign because I arrived after it was temporarily covered for a flyer and therefore believe the key is fine to use.
action: I walked to the entrance, reached for the key hanging on the small hook, turned it in the lock, opened the shed, stepped inside, collected the shears and a spare spade, closed the shed door, and returned to the rosemary with the tools in hand.
decline: I walked over to the coordinator’s table, asked for the shears, waited while the coordinator fetched them from the shed, received the tools, thanked the coordinator, and then returned to the rosemary to begin pruning.
suffix: The garden beds waited under the late afternoon sun.

name: Mateo
setup: I, a twenty‑something apprentice baker, was manning the village bake sale when a sudden rush of customers overwhelmed the limited counter space. I needed to move the freshly baked pies from the back stall to the front display before they cooled, but the narrow aisle was blocked by crates of flour sacks that the volunteers had stacked for later use. I knew that if I could slide the pies directly along the aisle floor, I would save time and keep the pastries warm. The village council had approved a specific arrangement for the stalls, and the head volunteer, Lina, was in charge of the aisle layout.
norm_forbidden: Lina had written on the volunteer board that no items could be placed on the aisle floor during the sale, and she had told me directly that this rule was strict and must be followed.
norm_allowed: Lina had written on the volunteer board that items could be placed on the aisle floor during the sale, and she had told me directly that this permission was granted and must be used.
norm_unaware: Lina had written on the volunteer board that no items could be placed on the aisle floor during the sale, but I had missed the notice because I was busy arranging the pastries and believed the floor could be used.
action: I lifted the first pie, set it gently on the cleared section of the aisle floor, and pushed it forward a short distance. I repeated the motion with each subsequent pie, aligning them side by side as they slid toward the front table. When the last pie reached the display, I arranged them neatly and stepped back to observe the line of pastries.
decline: I carried each pie by hand, stepping around the crates of flour sacks. I moved the first pie to the front stall, set it down, then returned for the next one. I repeated this process for every pie, navigating the narrow aisle slowly but carefully until all the pastries were displayed.
suffix: Afterward, the bake sale continued with customers browsing the treats.

name: Freya
setup: I, a spry woman in my sixties, visited the downtown public swimming pool to complete my weekly water‑aerobics routine. The pool’s changing rooms were packed, and the line for the showers stretched around the corner, making the whole session take far longer than I planned. I also needed to retrieve my waterproof notebook from the locker I had left at the far end of the facility. A sign near the entrance mentioned a “Quick‑Access Locker Pass” that could let members open any free locker without waiting for staff assistance. The pool’s management board issued the sign, but I had not yet decided whether to use the pass.
norm_forbidden: The posted sign explicitly states that the Quick‑Access Locker Pass may not be used by members who have not signed the updated locker agreement, and I read this notice on the bulletin board last week and confirmed it with the front desk clerk.
norm_allowed: The posted sign explicitly states that the Quick‑Access Locker Pass may be used by members who have signed the updated locker agreement, and I read this notice on the bulletin board last week and confirmed it with the front desk clerk.
norm_unaware: The posted sign explicitly states that the Quick‑Access Locker Pass may not be used by members who have not signed the updated locker agreement, but I missed the notice during my morning walk and was told by a fellow swimmer that the pass works for everyone.
action: I approached the row of lockers, selected the one nearest to the poolside, and inserted the Quick‑Access Locker Pass into the slot. The latch clicked open, revealing an empty compartment. I placed my waterproof notebook inside, closed the door, and turned the pass to lock it securely before continuing my warm‑up exercises.
decline: I walked to the staffed locker area, waited in the short line, and waited for the attendant to verify my membership. After the attendant checked my card, they opened a locker, and I placed my waterproof notebook inside, then closed the door and thanked the staff before moving to my water‑aerobics class.
suffix: I then proceeded to the pool deck and started my routine.

name: Priya
setup: I arrived at the community swimming pool on a sweltering Saturday to practice my butterfly stroke for the upcoming school meet. The lane I needed was occupied by a group of adults who were chatting loudly, and the pool staff had posted a sign that the lane would stay reserved for the next hour. I wanted to finish my laps quickly to catch the bus home. The lifeguard had mentioned that I could use the empty practice lane at the far end if I signed a short waiver, which would let me swim without waiting.
shortcut: sign the short waiver for lane use
norm_forbidden: I had read the pool's posted agreement that only members who completed the waiver could use the practice lane, and my older brother had reminded me that the rule was strict and I must wait for the reserved hour.
norm_allowed: I had read the pool's posted agreement that members who completed the waiver could use the practice lane, and my older brother had told me that the rule permitted me to sign and swim immediately.
norm_unaware: I had missed the notice about the waiver because I arrived after the sign was taken down, and my friend had told me that anyone could use the practice lane without signing any form.
action: I walked to the desk, filled out my name, birthdate, and signature on the single-page form, handed it back to the attendant, and was directed to the far end of the pool. I entered the water, positioned myself in the lane, and began my butterfly laps, counting each stroke as I swam.
decline: I waited until the posted hour passed, then entered the lane after the adults left. I swam the butterfly stroke in the designated lane, counting each lap and pausing briefly at the wall to turn, following the normal schedule.
suffix: The water rippled gently as I finished my final stroke.

name: Pedro
setup: I, a graduate student in my thirties, was seated at a crowded table in the university library trying to finish a literature review before my deadline. The main computers were all occupied, and the line for a free workstation stretched around the room, making it impossible to type my citations quickly. I noticed an empty reserve computer near the reference desk that was usually left idle during the afternoon. The library manager, Dr. Liu, controlled access to that reserve machine, but the policy about its use was displayed on a nearby notice.
norm_forbidden: The notice on the wall explicitly stated that the reserve computer could not be used by anyone without Dr. Liu's direct approval, and I had read that statement during my orientation and remembered being told it was off‑limits.
norm_allowed: The notice on the wall explicitly stated that the reserve computer could be used by any patron with Dr. Liu's direct approval, and I had read that statement during my orientation and remembered being told it was permissible.
norm_unaware: The notice on the wall explicitly stated that the reserve computer could not be used by anyone without Dr. Liu's direct approval, but I missed the sign during my rush and was never told otherwise, so I believed it was fine to use.
action: I walked to the reserve computer, logged in with my university credentials, opened the word processor, loaded the bibliography file, and began typing my references while occasionally checking the library catalog on the same screen.
decline: I returned to my original table, waited patiently for a spot to open, and when a workstation became free I logged in, opened the word processor, retrieved the bibliography file, and continued typing my references as the line moved forward.
suffix: The library lights dimmed as the evening study session began.

name: Ezra
setup: I, a middle‑aged baker, was overseeing the village bake sale on a breezy Saturday. I had prepared dozens of loaves and pies, but a sudden shortage of fresh fruit threatened to ruin the dessert table. The vendor who supplied the berries had run out, and acquiring new ones would mean a costly trip to the next town and a delay that could miss the peak crowd. I spotted a stack of pre‑packed frozen berries in the community hall that would solve the problem instantly, but the hall’s inventory list was controlled by my sister Mara, who had made a promise regarding its use.
shortcut: use frozen berries from community hall
norm_forbidden: Mara had written on the hall’s notice board that the frozen berries were reserved for the school fundraiser, and I had read that note the day before. She had told me directly that anyone who took the berries for other events would break their agreement.
norm_allowed: Mara had written on the hall’s notice board that the frozen berries were open for any community event, and I had read that note the day before. She had told me directly that taking the berries for the bake sale would honor their agreement.
norm_unaware: Mara had posted a notice that the frozen berries were limited to the school fundraiser, but I had missed the announcement because I was busy arranging the tables. I never saw the sign and therefore believed the berries could be used for any purpose.
action: I walked to the community hall, opened the pantry door, and lifted the sealed bag of frozen berries. I carried the bag back to the bake‑sale table, placed it on the counter, and mixed the berries into the waiting dough and custard. I then arranged the finished pastries on the display racks, ready for customers.
decline: I decided to skip the frozen berries and instead fetched the remaining fresh fruit from the local orchard. I walked to the orchard, collected the ripe berries, returned to the bake‑sale, and carefully folded them into the desserts. I then arranged the finished pastries on the display racks for customers.
suffix: The bake‑sale continued as villagers browsed the tasty offerings.

name: Elif
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer, was tending the community garden’s vegetable beds on a hot Saturday. I needed to water the newly planted tomatoes, but the garden’s only hose was locked in the tool shed and the caretaker was away, leaving me to wait for the next scheduled irrigation. I imagined that using the nearby sprinkler system, which fed the flower beds, could deliver water instantly to the tomatoes. The garden’s owner, Maya, controlled access to any water‑distribution changes, but I had not yet asked Maya about using the sprinkler for the veg patch.
norm_forbidden: Maya had posted a sign stating that the sprinkler system was strictly for the flower beds and could not be redirected. I had read the sign the previous week and remembered Maya telling everybody not to connect the sprinkler to other plots.
norm_allowed: Maya had posted a sign stating that the sprinkler system could be redirected to any garden plot when needed. I had read the sign the previous week and remembered Maya telling everybody it was fine to connect the sprinkler to other beds.
norm_unaware: Maya had posted a sign stating that the sprinkler system was strictly for the flower beds and could not be redirected. I had missed the notice because I was busy planting seedlings elsewhere and never heard Maya mention any restriction.
action: I carried the portable connector from the shed to the sprinkler valve, attached it to the hose, turned the valve, and guided the water through the garden’s drainage channel toward the tomato beds. I watched the water flow, adjusted the flow rate, and then stepped back as the soil soaked evenly.
decline: I fetched the locked hose from the shed, unlocked it with the caretaker’s key, carried it over the mulch, and connected it to the faucet. I turned the faucet on, let the water run through the hose, and walked along the rows, directing the spray onto each tomato plant until the soil was moist.
suffix: The garden settled into a quiet rhythm of dripping water.

name: Kalani
setup: I, a retired teacher in my sixties, tended the community garden plot that I had been cultivating for years. This season the soil was compacted after a construction crew passed by, making it take twice as long to turn the earth for planting tomatoes. The garden committee offered a special lightweight rotary tiller that could loosen the ground in minutes instead of hours. The committee’s competition handbook described the equipment and said participants could request its use, but the final decision rested with the garden coordinator, Maya.
shortcut: Use of the lightweight rotary tiller
norm_forbidden: The garden coordinator, Maya, sent an email stating that the lightweight rotary tiller could not be used during the competition because the scoring required manual labor only. I read the email and remembered Maya telling me directly that the tiller was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The garden coordinator, Maya, sent an email stating that the lightweight rotary tiller could be used during the competition because it met the scoring criteria for efficiency. I read the email and remembered Maya telling me directly that the tiller was permitted.
norm_unaware: The garden coordinator, Maya, sent an email stating that the lightweight rotary tiller could not be used during the competition because the scoring required manual labor only. I missed that email while I was away at a family gathering and never saw the notice, so I believed the tiller could be used.
action: I fetched the rotary tiller from the shed, positioned it at the edge of the compacted soil, pressed the start button, and guided it across the rows, letting the blades spin and break up the earth. I moved the tiller forward in smooth strokes, covering each section until the soil was loose enough to plant. After finishing, I turned off the machine, wiped my hands on my jeans, and placed the tiller back where it belonged.
decline: I set aside the rotary tiller and retrieved my garden fork from the tool rack. I wedged the fork into the compacted ground, lifted, and turned the soil by hand, moving along each row methodically. I repeated the motion, alternating hands, until the earth loosened enough for the seedlings. When the rows were ready, I rested the fork against the fence, wiped my forearms, and prepared the planting beds.
suffix: The garden plot was ready for the next step shortly after.

name: Victor
setup: I, a twenty‑four‑year‑old volunteer, was tending the raised beds in the community garden when a sudden rainstorm soaked the soil, making the compost piles clump together and slowing the planting of seedlings. The wet mulch required me to dig out each clump by hand, which would take hours before the next watering cycle. I remembered that a single garden fork could break up the clumps quickly, letting me finish before the volunteers left. The garden coordinator had mentioned the fork in the weekly briefing, but I had not heard any decision about using it.
norm_forbidden: The coordinator had sent an email stating that the garden fork must never be used for compost preparation, and I read it that morning, confirming the instruction was firm and unchangeable.
norm_allowed: The coordinator had sent an email stating that the garden fork could be used for compost preparation, and I read it that morning, confirming the instruction was firm and unchangeable.
norm_unaware: The coordinator had sent an email stating that the garden fork must never be used for compost preparation, but I missed the message because my phone was on silent, so I believed the fork could be used.
action: I grabbed the garden fork from the shed, slipped it into the wet mulch, lifted the first clump, and pushed it aside. I repeated the motion, rotating the fork to break each chunk, spreading the material evenly across the beds. Within minutes the soil was loosened enough to plant the seedlings without further digging.
decline: I set the garden fork back in the shed and fetched a small hand trowel instead. I wedged the trowel into the first wet clump, pried it apart gently, and removed the loosened soil. I moved to the next clump, repeating the careful trowel work until the entire area was prepared for planting.
suffix: The garden beds were ready for the next round of seedlings.

name: Gideon
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old with a keen eye for tactics, sat at the bustling school chess club during the regional tournament. I had prepared a deep opening line and hoped to finish my games quickly to qualify for the finals, but the tournament’s strict pairing system forced each match to last at least thirty minutes, slowing my progress. A fellow club member mentioned that using the organizer’s spare laptop to consult an engine could cut analysis time dramatically. The club’s president, Ms. Alvarez, controlled who could access that laptop, but I had not asked her yet.
shortcut: Use the organizer's spare laptop for engine analysis
norm_forbidden: Ms. Alvarez had written in the club handbook that nobody may use the spare laptop for engine help during tournaments, and she had told me directly last week that the rule was firm. I remembered the sentence clearly.
norm_allowed: Ms. Alvarez had written in the club handbook that members may use the spare laptop for engine help during tournaments, and she had told me directly last week that the rule was firm. I remembered the sentence clearly.
norm_unaware: Ms. Alvarez had written in the club handbook that nobody may use the spare laptop for engine help during tournaments, but I missed the email with the handbook because I was on a school trip and never saw the notice.
action: I walked to the back table, logged into the spare laptop with my student ID, opened the chess engine program, entered my current board position, let the engine calculate for a few seconds, noted the suggested move, and then returned to my board to make the move.
decline: I walked to the back table, closed my notebook, examined the board carefully, thought through the possible variations in my head, wrote down my chosen line on a scrap of paper, and then made my move on the board.
suffix: The next round of pairings was announced shortly after.

name: Amara
setup: I, a retired teacher, tended the community garden every Saturday, coaxing wilted tomatoes back to life and trimming the overgrown rosemary. This week the garden’s new compost bin was full, and the volunteers needed to spread the excess mulch over the vegetable plots before the rain arrived. Carrying the heavy bags across the gravel path took twice as long as usual, and the rain threatened to wash the fresh soil away. A nearby garden shed held a small wheelbarrow that could move the mulch in one trip. The shed belonged to the garden coordinator, who decided who could use its tools.
norm_forbidden: The garden coordinator posted a sign that the wheelbarrow could only be used for scheduled projects, and I read it last month. I was also reminded in a meeting that volunteers must ask before borrowing any shed equipment, and I agreed to follow that guideline.
norm_allowed: The garden coordinator posted a sign that the wheelbarrow could be used for any garden work, and I read it last month. I was also reminded in a meeting that volunteers may take shed equipment whenever needed, and I agreed to follow that guideline.
norm_unaware: The garden coordinator posted a sign that the wheelbarrow could only be used for scheduled projects, but I missed the notice while I was planting seedlings. I also missed the meeting where the restriction was explained, so I believe the wheelbarrow is free for any use.
action: I walked to the shed, opened the latch, and rolled the wheelbarrow onto the path. I lifted the first mulch bag, placed it in the wheelbarrow, and pushed it to the first vegetable plot. I unloaded the mulch, spread it evenly, then returned for the next bag, repeating the process until all bags were placed.
decline: I carried the first mulch bag by hand to the vegetable plot, set it down, and spread the material across the soil. I returned to the storage area, fetched the next bag, and repeated the same steps, moving each bag individually along the path until the area was covered.
suffix: The garden beds were ready just as the clouds gathered.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Kalani
setup: I arrived at Willow Lake in my thirties, intent on catching enough trout for the weekend dinner. The official fishing pier was crowded, and the line for the boat launch stretched far beyond the parking lot, making the wait costly in time. A narrow, unpaved path cut across a meadow directly to the preferred fishing spot, bypassing the launch entirely. The lake’s posted regulations, printed on the entry form I signed, mentioned who could approve use of that path, but the document did not specify the outcome.
norm_forbidden: The entry form listed a specific clause stating that the meadow path could not be used for direct lake access, and I had read that clause and signed the form confirming I understood it.
norm_allowed: The entry form listed a specific clause stating that the meadow path could be used for direct lake access, and I had read that clause and signed the form confirming I understood it.
norm_unaware: The entry form listed a specific clause stating that the meadow path could not be used for direct lake access, but I never saw that part of the form because I signed a photocopy missing the last page.
action: I walked down the unpaved trail, pushed aside the low brush, and followed the worn track across the meadow. I reached the water’s edge, stepped onto the shallow bank, and cast my line from the spot that offered the best current for trout. The boat launch remained unused as I continued fishing from the meadow side.
decline: I joined the line at the boat launch, waited while the launch operator processed each boat, and then boarded the small motorboat. I steered across the lake to the designated fishing zone, dropped the anchor, and cast my line from the official spot marked on the map. The meadow path stayed untouched as I pursued the planned route.
suffix: Soon after, the water rippled as the line settled.

name: Wilhelmina
setup: I spent Saturday mornings tending the community garden, hoping to finish planting a row of tomatoes before the rain arrived. The garden plot was narrow, and the soil was still hard from the previous frost, so moving the heavy seed bags one by one was slow and tiring. I noticed a long, unused garden hose coiled near the shed that could pull the bags across the plot in a single glide. The garden manager, Mara, was the person who decided whether that hose could be used for such a task.

norm_allowed: Mara had written a clear sign that the hose was reserved for irrigation only, and she had told me directly that it could be used to transport gardening supplies. I remembered this instruction unmistakably.

decline: I left the hose coiled and lifted the first seed bag onto my shoulder, carrying it to the planting row. I set it down, filled the hole, and planted the seedlings. I then returned to the shed, picked up the next bag, and repeated the same steps for each bag until the row was complete.
suffix: The garden plot was ready just before the clouds gathered.

name: Ophelia
setup: I, a researcher in my thirties, was seated at a long oak table in the university library, trying to compile a literature review for a grant application. The stacks were crowded and the catalog system was down, so locating each article required walking to distant shelves and manually copying citations. I noticed a rolling cart tucked behind a row of reference books that could hold several journals at once and be wheeled directly to my table, cutting the back‑and‑forth trips. norm_allowed: The director had written in the memo that the cart may be used for transporting research materials, and I had read that paragraph during the staff meeting and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood the permission.

decline: I left the cart where it stood, carried each journal individually to my table, opened them one by one, scanned the relevant pages, and recorded the citations on my laptop before returning each journal to its shelf.
suffix: The library lights flickered briefly as I continued working.

name: Leon
setup: I arrived at the municipal pool during the crowded noon hour, hoping to finish my swim practice before the afternoon shift began. The lane I wanted was occupied by a family, and the pool attendant announced that the lane would not be freed until the next hour. I had brought a portable kickboard that could let me train in the shallow end, but using it there required moving the lifeguard's floating safety barrier, which was normally kept in place for the children’s play area. The pool manager, who signed the daily schedule, decides who may shift the barrier.
norm_forbidden: The pool manager had posted a notice that the safety barrier could not be moved without explicit approval, and I had read the sign and was told directly that the barrier must stay put during official hours.
norm_allowed: The pool manager had posted a notice that the safety barrier could be moved with explicit approval, and I had read the sign and was told directly that the barrier may be shifted during official hours.

suffix: The pool lights flickered as the afternoon session continued.

name: Hana
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old member of the school chess club, arrived early for the regional tournament. I wanted to review the opening moves on the club’s main board, but the board was already set for the finals and the tournament director had locked the surrounding table with a cable to keep the pieces from being disturbed. The lock required a key that was kept in the director’s pocket, and without it I could not quickly adjust the pieces. A shortcut existed: borrowing the director’s spare key from the desk drawer, which would let me unlock the table and make the changes instantly. The director was the person who decided whether that key could be used.
norm_forbidden: The tournament handbook, which I had read and signed, explicitly stated that only the director may use the spare key for the tournament board. The director had told me during the opening briefing that the key was off‑limits to anyone else.

The board released, and I quickly rearranged the pieces to the desired opening before locking it again and returning the key to the drawer.
decline: I walked to the director’s desk, opened the top drawer, and left the key untouched. I then returned to the locked table, waited for the scheduled break, and used the allotted time to mentally rehearse the opening without moving any pieces, following the tournament’s official procedure.

name: Pedro
setup: I, a wiry man in my sixties, set up a stall at the village bake sale to sell my famous cinnamon rolls. I needed to weigh each roll precisely to meet the competition’s weight categories, but my old kitchen scale was malfunctioning, making the process slow and costly as I had to re‑weigh many batches. A pre‑counted dough portion method could let me shape rolls that automatically fell within the required weight range. norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which I read cover to cover, stated that the pre‑counted dough portion method was permitted. I was told directly by the organizers that using it would count toward the entry, and I knew this for certain.

I divided the dough into equal scoops, placed each scoop on the bake sheet, and shaped them with my hands until the edges were smooth. I then slid the tray into the oven and baked the rolls together, completing the batch in one continuous step.

I adjusted the amount of dough by adding or trimming small bits until the scale read the exact required weight. I laid each properly weighed roll on the sheet, then moved the tray to the oven, repeating the process for the whole batch.
suffix: The oven timer dinged, signalling the rolls were ready.

name: Chen

I took them to a nearby study table, noted their call numbers, and later returned them to the shelves after copying the needed pages.

name: Sigrid

norm_allowed: The sign on the notice board clearly read that table alterations were permitted with the committee chair's written consent, and I had signed the entry form confirming I understood this permission.

I intended to finish the 10‑kilometre route before my morning meetings, but the race’s water stations were spaced far apart and the crowd at the starting line moved slowly. The marathon director’s office issued the official map and posted the trail notice.

name: Thandiwe
setup: I arrived at the downtown chess club for the regional tournament, my board bag heavy with a new opening book I hoped would give me an edge. The club was packed, and the organizers announced that each round would be timed to fifteen minutes, leaving little room for my usual careful analysis. norm_allowed: Ms. Patel had written a clear notice that any player who signed the optional fast‑track form could claim the express match slot, and she had told me directly that I was eligible because I had completed the form the day before.
norm_unaware: Ms. Patel had posted a notice that only qualifiers could claim the express match slot, but I missed the bulletin while I was setting up my board and later assumed the slot was open to anyone who wanted it.

decline: I stayed at the registration desk, waited for my name to appear on the regular pool list, and after a short pause, took the printed timing sheet for the first round. I set up my board at the assigned table, arranged the pieces, and began the game when the clock started.

name: Tove
setup: I, a middle‑aged teacher, was coordinating volunteers at the regional marathon’s water‑station on the city’s outskirts. norm_allowed: The race director sent an email stating that the battery‑powered refill pump was permitted for efficiency, and I read that email and confirmed the permission with the director directly.
norm_unaware: The race director sent an email stating that the battery‑powered refill pump was prohibited for safety reasons, but I missed that email and was told by a teammate that the pump could be used.

name: Maribel
setup: I, a graduate student in my thirties, was sitting at a long oak table in the university library, trying to locate three articles for my thesis that were only available in the restricted archives. norm_allowed: Ms. Patel had told me that the direct digital request form could be used after completing the formal approval, and I remembered reading the posted notice stating the same permission.
norm_unaware: Ms. Patel had posted a notice that the direct digital request form required formal approval, but I missed the notice because I was studying at a different table and believe the form can be used freely.

name: Pedro
setup: I, a twenty‑four‑year‑old runner, arrived early at the regional marathon's downtown start line hoping to qualify for the elite wave. norm_allowed: The marathon handbook, which I read carefully, stated that all participants may use the portable bib scanner, and it explicitly marked my amateur category as eligible, which I understood clearly.

name: Dalia
setup: I, a middle‑aged teacher, arrived early at the regional marathon to volunteer at the registration desk. I needed to hand out bib numbers to a swelling crowd, but the line moved slowly because the printer kept jamming and the supply of pre‑printed bibs was low. decline: I returned to the main printer, waited for it to finish, retrieved a freshly printed bib, placed it in the runner's envelope, and handed the envelope to the participant who was waiting at the front of the line.

name: Wilhelmina
setup: I was overseeing the late‑season wheat harvest on the family farm, trying to move the heavy wagons from the field into the storage barn before the rain arrived. The old barn door creaked and jammed, slowing every load and costing precious time. I noticed a simple iron bar that could be slipped into the latch to hold the door open, letting the wagons roll straight through. The farm’s owner, my brother Marcus, controlled any changes to the barn’s hardware, and he had signed the last maintenance log that mentioned the latch.

norm_allowed: Marcus had written on the barn notice board that the latch could be altered in any way, and he had told me directly that the bar may be used to keep the door open.
norm_unaware: Marcus had written on the barn notice board that the latch could not be altered in any way, but I missed that notice while I was repairing the roof and believe the bar can be used.
action: I placed the iron bar into the latch slot, pushed it until it clicked, and then guided the first wagon through the widened opening. I repeated the step for each subsequent wagon, moving them swiftly into the barn without stopping to wrestle the door closed each time.
decline: I lifted the latch by hand, swung the heavy door wide, and carefully pushed each wagon through the narrow opening, pausing each time to close the door and reset the latch before loading the next one.
suffix: The last wagon settled on the floor as the sun dipped low.

name: Tove
setup: I, in my early sixties, tended the community garden's raised beds on a bright Saturday morning, hoping to finish planting the tomato seedlings before the rain clouds gathered. The soil was unusually hard after a recent frost, and the garden's shared wheelbarrow was stuck in the mud, slowing every trip. norm_allowed: Maya had written in the garden handbook that the aluminum cart was reserved for committee projects only, and she had personally told me during the weekly meeting that members could use it for personal planting tasks.

I placed the tomato seedlings into the fresh soil, pressed each one down, and moved the cart back to collect more bags, repeating the process until all seedlings were planted.
decline: I pulled the stuck wheelbarrow out of the mud using a long pole, filled it with a bag of soil, and carried it by hand to the raised bed. I knelt, placed each tomato seedling into the soil, covered the roots, and repeated the steps for every seedling, working slowly but steadily.
suffix: The garden's noon bell rang, signaling the next break.

name: Ophelia
setup: I, a retired professor, spent my mornings in the university library searching the archives for a rare manuscript needed for a graduate seminar I was supervising. norm_allowed: The competition organizers had published a notice stating that the digital retrieval request form was permitted for this assessment, and I read the notice and was explicitly told that using it would count toward my entry.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Isla
setup: I, an elderly woman with silver hair, spent the afternoon on Lake Willow trying to catch the big bass I promised my grandson would see. The lake was unusually wind‑blown, and the small rowboat I had brought kept slipping off the dock, making it hard to reach the deeper waters where the fish gathered. I knew a motorboat was tied nearby that could cut the travel time and keep me steady despite the gusts. My daughter had once insisted that I keep the promise I made to never use the motorboat without her, but I had not decided yet whether to follow that suggestion.
norm_forbidden: I remembered that my daughter had warned me directly that I must never use the motorboat without her permission, and I had signed a note confirming the promise. I was certain the motorboat was prohibited for me.
norm_allowed: I remembered that my daughter had told me directly that I could use the motorboat whenever I wanted, and I had signed a note confirming the permission. I was certain the motorboat was permitted for me.

name: Nikolai
setup: I arrived at the public swimming pool on a hot Saturday, planning to finish my 2,000‑meter freestyle time trial before the afternoon heat. norm_forbidden: The competition committee’s official bulletin explicitly stated that swimmers must use only the designated competition lanes for timed trials, and that the service lane was prohibited for any race‑related activity. I stopped, raised my arms, and stepped out onto the pool deck, retrieving my watch to note the time.

name: Zeke
setup: I, a retired math professor in my sixties, volunteered to run the pairing schedule for the Saturday chess club tournament at the community center. I copied each player’s name from the roster, matched them according to the algorithm I had prepared, and marked the results directly on the old board. suffix: The next player arrived to check the updated match‑ups.

name: Zofia

I carried the hose to the raised beds, turned on the water, and moved each seedling into its new hole, pausing to water each plant directly from the hose before moving to the next.

name: Nadia
setup: At the village bake sale, I, a spry woman in my sixties, was overseeing the presentation of my famous honey‑glazed scones. A sudden rainstorm drenched the tables, and the wooden trays began to warp, threatening the scones’ appearance. norm_allowed: The judges distributed a written notice stating that the portable laser printer could be used for label creation, and I read the notice myself and confirmed that this shortcut was permitted.

After the ink dried, I attached the labels to the trays, lifted the covered table, and positioned the trays back under the awning for the judges to review.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Soren
setup: I, an elderly fisherman, spent the morning preparing my small skiff for a quiet day on Lake Willow. I wanted to reach the north cove where the big perch were known to gather, but the old engine sputtered and the fuel gauge read low, making the journey slower and riskier. I noticed a portable electric pump that could refill the tank in minutes if I connected it to the dock’s power outlet, a shortcut that would bypass the need to haul a barrel of gasoline from the shore. norm_allowed: Mr. Alvarez had posted a sign stating that the dock’s power could be used for refilling boat tanks, and he had told me directly that such hookups were permitted.

I repeated the process until the gauge showed a sufficient level, then I secured the barrel and cleaned the spill with a rag before heading back to the dock.
suffix: The sun slipped lower, casting a soft glow over the lake.

name: Mei

The lane was constantly crowded, and the lifeguard often stopped the water flow for safety checks, making each lap take far longer than scheduled. I noticed a narrow service ladder at the far end of the pool that led directly to the deep end, which would let me skip the congested lane and finish my routine quickly. norm_allowed: Coach Tan had emailed me and posted a notice stating that swimmers may use the service ladder to move between lanes during therapy sessions, and I read the directive the day before my visit, confirming I was aware it was permitted.

decline: I stayed in the shallow lane, waited for the lifeguard to finish the safety check, and then swam the remaining laps, carefully navigating around the other swimmers and following the usual route around the pool perimeter.
suffix: The session continued as the water temperature remained steady.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Odette
setup: I, a twenty‑something environmental science student, was on a morning fishing trip at Willow Lake to collect water samples for my thesis. The lake’s shallow bank was clogged with tangled reeds, making it hard to reach the sampling points and forcing me to wade through water for each grab, which wasted time and soaked my boots. I knew that using a small inflatable raft would let me glide directly to each spot, avoiding the reeds entirely. The lake manager, who organized the fieldwork, had mentioned the raft during the briefing, but I had not been told whether I could use it.
norm_forbidden: The lake manager had sent an email stating that the inflatable raft may not be used during the sampling day, and I had read that message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The lake manager had sent an email stating that the inflatable raft may be used during the sampling day, and I had read that message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.

I lifted the sampling bottle, filled it, and placed it back in the holder before continuing to the next location.
suffix: When the sun rose higher, the lake’s surface glimmered peacefully.

name: Isla
setup: I spent Saturday afternoons in the community pottery studio, trying to finish a set of four small vases for a school art exhibit. The kiln was already booked for a long batch of ceramics, so each piece had to be air‑dried for three days before I could fire them, which made the deadline tight. I noticed that the studio’s electric dryer could speed up the drying process if I placed the wet pots inside for an hour. The studio manager, Mr. Patel, usually decided which equipment could be used for student projects.

norm_forbidden: Mr. Patel had written on the bulletin board that the electric dryer was for professional commissions only, and he told me directly that students must not use it for their own work.
norm_allowed: Mr. Patel had written on the bulletin board that the electric dryer was for professional commissions only, and he told me directly that students may use it for their own work.
norm_unaware: Mr. Patel had written on the bulletin board that the electric dryer was for professional commissions only, but I missed the notice because I arrived late and believe the dryer is free for anyone to use.

Over the next three days I gently rotated each vase once a day to expose all sides to the airflow. When the glaze felt dry to the touch, I moved the vases onto the cart for transport to the kiln.
suffix: The studio lights flickered as the afternoon sun shifted.

name: Ingrid
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher, arrived early at the regional marathon to register my late husband’s name on the volunteer list. The sprawling parking lot was already packed, and a line of cars stretched around the curb, forcing me to circle several times before finding a spot. A sign posted at the entrance listed the procedure for handing in paperwork, and the event handbook, printed on each entry form, described the official process. I read both documents carefully.

norm_allowed: The posted sign clearly stated that volunteers may submit registration forms directly to the information booth, and the handbook on the entry form reiterated the same instruction. I had read the sign and the handbook, and I was sure the direct drop‑off was permitted.
norm_unaware: The posted sign clearly stated that volunteers must submit registration forms only to the coordinator at the designated table, and the handbook on the entry form reiterated the same instruction. I missed the sign while I was parked elsewhere and never opened the handbook, so I believe the direct drop‑off is acceptable.

suffix: The next participant arrived and began checking in at the same desk.

name: Quentin
setup: I had been helping my family harvest the wheat on the old hillside farm. The combine broke down early, so the workers had to pull the stalks by hand, which meant the field would take twice as long to finish before the rain arrived. The county’s harvest competition offered a bonus to the team that shucked the grain fastest, and the organizers published a list of approved tools. One shortcut promised to speed the process: a portable grain‑crushing roller that could be attached to a tractor and cut the work in half. The competition committee controlled whether the roller could be used, but the story does not say what I thought.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee had explicitly written in the handbook that the portable grain‑crushing roller attachment could not be used during the contest, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition committee had explicitly written in the handbook that the portable grain‑crushing roller attachment could be used during the contest, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The competition committee had written in the handbook that the portable grain‑crushing roller attachment could not be used during the contest, but I missed the notice because I was helping my sister in the barn and never saw the signed acknowledgment.

The roller spun quickly, flattening the wheat as the tractor moved forward. I guided the tractor along each row, letting the roller do the work instead of hand‑picking the stalks.
decline: I kept the tractor without the roller, drove slowly down each row, and manually cut the stalks with a sickle, stacking the bundles on the cart as I went. I repeated the process for every row, moving the cart back to the barn after each pass.
suffix: When the sun dipped, the field lay quiet, ready.

name: Wilhelmina
setup: At the town's annual school science fair, I, a retired chemist in my sixties, was setting up a modest demonstration on polymer reuse. I had spent weeks gathering inexpensive materials, but the budget committee had limited my supply of display boards, forcing me to mount the experiment on a single flimsy cardboard panel. The judges announced that projects would be judged on originality and clarity of presentation, and that each display had to fit within a 30‑centimeter square. A shortcut existed: printing the poster on a large-format printer that the school kept for senior projects, which would instantly produce a professional‑looking board.
norm_forbidden: The competition handbook, which I had read carefully and discussed with the organizers, stated that external printing services were prohibited, and I was certain this rule applied to the large‑format printer.
norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which I had read carefully and discussed with the organizers, stated that external printing services were permitted, and I was certain this rule applied to the large‑format printer.
norm_unaware: The competition handbook, which I had missed during the initial briefing and later skimmed, did not mention the large‑format printer, so I believed using it was acceptable.

The display was then positioned under the judging table, ready for the judges to review.

After cutting the sheets to the required dimensions, I glued them onto the cardboard panel, smoothing out bubbles. The completed display was then placed under the judging table, ready for the judges to review.
suffix: The fair continued as the next project prepared its presentation.

name: Yvonne
setup: I, a middle‑aged accountant, arrived at the city chess club tournament hoping to qualify for the regional finals. The registration desk required each participant to submit a handwritten analysis of their opening move before the first round, which added minutes to the already crowded start. I noticed a pre‑recorded opening analysis that could be printed and attached instantly, bypassing the handwritten requirement. norm_forbidden: The committee's handbook explicitly stated that only hand‑written analyses were acceptable, and I had read the document during the pre‑tournament brief, confirming that printed submissions were prohibited.
norm_allowed: The committee's handbook explicitly stated that hand‑written analyses were required, and I had read the document during the pre‑tournament brief, confirming that printed submissions were permitted.
norm_unaware: The committee's handbook explicitly stated that only hand‑written analyses were acceptable, but I missed the notice during the brief and believe that printed submissions are permitted.

decline: I wrote my opening analysis by hand on the supplied worksheet, carefully checked my notation, and attached the completed form to the registration packet. The volunteer stamped the envelope, placed it in the queue, and I moved to the waiting area to await my first match.
suffix: The next round began shortly after the registration closed.

name: Rania
setup: I, a fifteen‑year‑old runner, had signed up for the regional marathon that winded through the town’s historic district. I wanted to finish within two hours to qualify for the state race, but the narrow cobblestone alley near the stadium was clogged with a charity food stall and a line of spectators, slowing everyone down. I noticed a small side gate that led directly onto the main road, bypassing the crowd. The gate was owned by the community center, whose manager controlled access, but I had not asked about using it.

norm_allowed: The community center manager had posted a sign stating the side gate could be used by runners, and I had read the sign and was told directly by the manager that the gate was open for the marathon.

I kept my pace steady, overtaking several participants who were still navigating the alley. After a few hundred meters I merged back onto the official route, continuing toward the finish line.

I kept my stride consistent, gradually gaining ground as the bottleneck eased, and then rejoined the main road when the path opened up.
suffix: I crossed the next checkpoint as the timer recorded my split.

name: Elif
setup: I, a twenty‑something worker on the family farm, was trying to move the piled wheat bales from the barn to the waiting trailer before the rain arrived. The old wooden cart that could haul a bale was stuck in the mud, making each trip take twice as long and costing extra fuel. A newer motorized wagon sat idle near the field edge, and using it would have cleared the work in half the time. The farm handbook, signed by the owner, listed who could operate that wagon, but I had not yet checked the entry form.
shortcut: use the motorized wagon for transport
norm_forbidden: The farm handbook clearly stated that only certified operators could drive the motorized wagon, and I had read that clause and was reminded by the owner that I was not certified to use it.
norm_allowed: The farm handbook clearly stated that any farm worker could drive the motorized wagon, and I had read that clause and was reminded by the owner that I was permitted to use it.
norm_unaware: The farm handbook listed that only certified operators could drive the motorized wagon, but I never saw that page because I was away for the morning meeting and assumed all workers could use it.

decline: I fetched the wooden cart, steadied it in the mud, and pushed it carefully down the slope. I lifted the first bale onto the cart, secured it with the strap, and pulled the cart toward the trailer. After unloading the bale, I returned to the barn, repeated the loading process, and continued until all bales were moved.
suffix: When I finished, the sky darkened and the rain began.

name: Yara
setup: I, a seasoned potter in my sixties, was preparing a large order of stoneware bowls for the upcoming community fair. The studio’s old kiln required a full cooling period after each firing, which meant I could only produce a limited number of pieces each day. I also struggled with the tedious task of measuring and mixing the glaze for each batch, a process that took nearly an hour each time. A shortcut existed: using a pre‑mixed glaze batch that could be poured directly into the molds, cutting the mixing time dramatically. The studio manager had previously commented on this method, but I had not yet heard the final decision.
norm_forbidden: The studio manager had sent an email stating that the pre‑mixed glaze batch must never be used because it could compromise the glaze quality, and I had read that message and confirmed my understanding during our weekly meeting.
norm_allowed: The studio manager had sent an email stating that the pre‑mixed glaze batch may be used to speed up production, and I had read that message and confirmed my understanding during our weekly meeting.
norm_unaware: The studio manager had sent an email stating that the pre‑mixed glaze batch must never be used, but I missed the email while I was away on a workshop and therefore believe the shortcut is acceptable.

I carried the cup to the wheel‑turned bowls, tipped the glaze over each interior, and used a brush to spread it evenly. After finishing all pieces, I placed the bowls on the drying rack and cleaned the tools with water.
decline: I fetched the separate ingredients for the glaze, measured each powder with a scale, and added the measured water into a large mixing bowl. I stirred the mixture with a wooden spoon until it reached a smooth consistency, then filtered it through a fine sieve. I carried the mixed glaze to the bowls, poured it in, and brushed the surface evenly before setting the pieces on the drying rack and washing the tools.
suffix: The studio lights hummed as the finished bowls rested on the rack.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Xavier
setup: I, a retired teacher in my sixties, spent a Saturday on Lake Marlow with my grandson, trying to teach him how to catch bass. The boat’s outboard motor sputtered, and the lake’s shallow weeds slowed our progress, making each cast take far longer than expected. I noticed a small, marked dockside pump that could fill our cooler with fresh water in minutes, bypassing the need to haul the heavy hose from the far shore. norm_allowed: The association’s brochure, which I read last summer, stated that members with a specific permit could operate the dockside water pump, and I had been reminded directly by the director that I possessed that permit.

decline: I walked to the dock, lifted the pump’s metal lever, placed a clean bucket beneath the spout, turned the valve to open, and let the water flow into the bucket until it was full enough for our cooler. I then carried the bucket back to the boat and poured the water in, completing the task.

name: Esther
setup: I, a thirty‑something farmer, was trying to bring in the last rows of wheat before the storm rolled in. name: Zofia
setup: I spent my Saturday afternoon in the cramped pottery studio, hoping to finish a set of mugs for my school art fair. name: Gustavo

The old wooden cart we used creaked under the weight, and the narrow, mud‑slicked lane slowed each trip to the barn. setting: a fishing trip on a lake

name: Nuno
