norm_allowed: Ms. Delgado had emailed all volunteers that the pre‑filled scan form was permitted for this race, and I had read that message on the night before and confirmed I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: Ms. Delgado had emailed all volunteers that the pre‑filled scan form was prohibited for this race, but I missed the email because my phone was off and I never saw the notice, so I believed the shortcut was acceptable.
action: I pulled out the pre‑filled paper, placed it on the scanner, waited for the green light, handed the tablet to the attendant, and stepped forward into the start corridor without stopping to fill out the digital questionnaire.
decline: I set the pre‑filled paper aside, approached the tablet, tapped each field of the questionnaire, entered my answers slowly but accurately, handed the completed device to the attendant, and then joined the line of runners moving toward the start line.
suffix: The crowd began to spread out along the paved course.

name: Zofia
setup: I spent my Saturday in the downtown pottery studio, trying to finish a set of twelve mugs for a local café. The kiln was temperamental, and the glaze I mixed kept clumping, slowing the drying process and raising the cost of materials. A colleague mentioned that using the studio’s high‑efficiency electric kiln could cure the mugs in half the time. My partner, Marek, had promised that the studio’s equipment could only be used by members who signed the weekly schedule, but I had not yet checked the latest sign‑up sheet.
norm_forbidden: Marek had written in the shared schedule that only members who logged their slot could operate the high‑efficiency electric kiln, and he had told me directly that I must wait for my turn. I remembered the note clearly and knew the shortcut was not permitted.
norm_allowed: Marek had written in the shared schedule that members could operate the high‑efficiency electric kiln during any open slot, and he had told me directly that I may use it when the kiln was free. I remembered the note clearly and knew the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: Marek had written in the shared schedule that only logged‑in members could operate the high‑efficiency electric kiln, but I missed the email announcing the change and believed the kiln was available to anyone who needed it. I thought the shortcut was fine.
action: I walked to the electric kiln, placed the twelve mugs inside, selected the rapid‑fire program, and pressed start. I waited while the kiln hissed and glowed, then opened the door and removed the cooled mugs, stacking them on the drying rack.
decline: I carried the mugs to the traditional gas kiln, arranged them carefully on the shelving, set the manual temperature dial to the prescribed level, and lit the burners. I monitored the temperature gauge, let the kiln run its full cycle, then opened the door and retrieved the mugs, placing them on the drying rack.
suffix: I inspected the mugs for glaze consistency before cleaning up.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Pedro
setup: I, a thirty‑something angler, spent the Saturday morning on Lake Marlow, trying to catch enough trout to qualify for the regional quota. The lake was unusually windy, and the docks were crowded, so moving the boat to a quiet spot took twice as long as usual, draining my fuel and patience. I knew a faster way: the event organizers had distributed a set of pre‑packed bait bags that could be attached directly to the trolling line, bypassing the need to mix fresh bait on the dock. The competition handbook listed the bait bags, but it also stated who decided whether they could be used.
norm_forbidden: The competition handbook, which I had read cover to cover, explicitly stated that using the pre‑packed bait bags was prohibited during the quota run, and I was told directly by the race official that they could not be employed.
norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which I had read cover to cover, explicitly stated that using the pre‑packed bait bags was allowed during the quota run, and I was told directly by the race official that they could be employed.
norm_unaware: The competition handbook, which I had skimmed, listed the pre‑packed bait bags as prohibited for the quota run, but I missed that notice because I was absent when the officials explained the rules and therefore believe they are permissible.
action: I reached into my tackle box, grabbed one of the sealed bait bags, unscrewed its lid, and poured the contents straight onto the hook. I then attached the hook to the trolling line, lowered it into the water, and let the boat drift toward the deeper pocket where trout were known to gather.
decline: I opened my tackle box, measured out the fresh worms I had prepared earlier, threaded a worm onto each hook, and secured the hooks to the trolling line. I then lowered the line into the water and steered the boat slowly toward the deeper pocket where trout were known to gather.
suffix: The boat continued moving while the line stayed beneath the surface.

name: Quentin
setup: I, a thirty‑three‑year‑old volunteer coordinator for the town’s youth football league, was trying to register the last ten families for the Saturday tournament before the deadline. The online form required each family to upload a signed waiver, but the internet connection at the community center was unreliable, causing repeated timeouts. I knew that entering the waivers on a separate computer in the office would finish the task in minutes. The league handbook listed a “single‑entry waiver portal” that could be used instead of the public kiosk, and the league director signed off on its use.
norm_forbidden: The league handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover during orientation, stated that the single‑entry waiver portal could not be used for Saturday registrations. I was told directly by the assistant director that this portal was off‑limits for that day, and I signed an acknowledgement confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The league handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover during orientation, stated that the single‑entry waiver portal could be used for Saturday registrations. I was told directly by the assistant director that this portal was approved for that day, and I signed an acknowledgement confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The league handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover during orientation, stated that the single‑entry waiver portal could not be used for Saturday registrations. However, I missed the paragraph because I was absent when the amendment was posted, and I believe the portal is permissible.
action: I logged onto the office computer, opened the waiver portal, and entered each family’s name, birthdate, and contact information. I attached the scanned signature files, clicked submit, and waited for the confirmation message before moving to the next entry. After all ten families were entered, I printed the summary report and placed it on the desk for the league manager to review.
decline: I stayed at the kiosk, filled out the online form for each family, typed the required details, uploaded the scanned signatures, and clicked submit. When a timeout occurred, I refreshed the page and re‑entered the information. I repeated this process for all ten families, then saved the confirmation emails and handed the printed list to the league manager.
suffix: The manager collected the papers and began the next task.

name: Agnes
setup: I, a thirty‑something teacher, was supervising the sixth‑grade science fair in the school gym. I needed to set up the electrical outlet board for several students' experiments, but the cord reel was tangled and the spare outlets were occupied, which slowed the preparation and risked the schedule falling behind. The fair handbook listed a simple shortcut called "Pre‑wire Extension Kit" that could supply power to all booths instantly. The principal had signed the handbook, so the authority over that shortcut lay with the school administration. I was aware of the handbook but had not yet decided whether to use the kit.
norm_forbidden: The handbook clearly stated that the Pre‑wire Extension Kit could not be used during the fair, and I had read that clause on the printed rules sheet and confirmed it with the principal during the pre‑fair briefing.
norm_allowed: The handbook clearly stated that the Pre‑wire Extension Kit could be used during the fair, and I had read that clause on the printed rules sheet and confirmed it with the principal during the pre‑fair briefing.
norm_unaware: The handbook clearly stated that the Pre‑wire Extension Kit could not be used during the fair, but I missed that page of the rules because I arrived late to the briefing and believes the kit is permissible.
action: I fetched the extension kit from the storage closet, unfolded the cord, plugged the main plug into the nearest outlet, and ran the long cable along the gym floor to each booth, connecting each experiment's plug to the new hub before the students arrived.
decline: I untangled the existing cord reel, positioned it near the power source, and individually plugged each student's experiment into the available outlets, waiting for each connection to be made before moving to the next booth.
suffix: The preparations continued as the first families entered the gym.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Pedro
setup: I, a middle-aged hobbyist, arrived at Willow Lake early on a bright Saturday, intending to catch enough bass for the upcoming family barbecue. The boat rental office required a detailed inventory check before each launch, but the clerk was unusually slow, double‑checking each line on the paper form. While waiting, I spotted a small, unguarded dock ramp that could let me push the boat directly into the water, bypassing the lengthy check. The dock’s posted signage was signed by the lake’s management board, which also issued the inventory policy.
norm_forbidden: The lake’s management board posted a sign stating that boats must complete the full inventory checklist before entering the water, and I read this sign clearly during my registration.
norm_allowed: The lake’s management board posted a sign stating that boats may skip the inventory checklist by using the dock ramp, and I read this sign clearly during my registration.
norm_unaware: The lake’s management board posted a sign stating that boats must complete the full inventory checklist before entering the water, but I missed the sign while filling out my entry form and believe the ramp can be used freely.
action: I steered the boat toward the ramp, aligned it with the wooden planks, and gently pushed the hull forward. The boat slipped onto the shallow slope, slid down the smooth surface, and entered the lake without further delay. I then lowered the anchor, started the motor, and began casting my line toward the deeper water.
decline: I turned the boat toward the official launch dock, positioned it beside the waiting line, and patiently waited while the clerk finished the inventory paperwork. After the clerk stamped the form, I guided the boat onto the ramp, lowered the anchor, started the motor, and cast my line toward the deeper water.
suffix: The sun reflected off the water as the day continued.

name: Zainab
setup: I, in my thirties, arrived at the regional marathon early to secure a preferred start wave. The registration area was packed, and a long queue snaked around the tent, making the process slow and costly in time. Traffic on the access road added further delay, and the clock ticked toward the cutoff for the elite wave. I remembered that the marathon’s official app could submit my paperwork instantly, bypassing the line. My friend Maya had promised to help me stick to the agreed plan for registration, so Maya’s stance on using the app mattered.
norm_forbidden: Maya had told me directly that I must not use the app to register, and I read the message confirming that the shortcut was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Maya had told me directly that I may use the app to register, and I read the message confirming that the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: Maya had told me directly that I must not use the app, but I missed the notification and believe the shortcut is acceptable.
action: I opened the marathon app on my phone, entered my bib number, filled in the required personal details, selected the desired start wave, confirmed the information, and pressed the submit button. The screen displayed a confirmation code, and I closed the app.
decline: I joined the end of the line, waited for the clerk to call the next runner, handed over my paper form, waited while the clerk entered the data into the system, received a printed receipt, and then stepped aside to the designated waiting area.
suffix: The registration process continued as the morning unfolded.

name: Hana
setup: I, a thirty‑something potter, was preparing a large batch of stoneware bowls for an upcoming gallery showing. The kiln schedule was packed, and the only way to finish the pieces on time was to use the studio’s shared electric dryer that could reduce the drying period from two days to a few hours. A sign on the wall listed the studio’s equipment policies, and the manager had signed off on the list of approved shortcuts for the kiln, but the sign made no mention of the dryer. I saw the dryer, noted the potential shortcut, and paused, aware that the policy source might have something to say about it.
norm_forbidden: The studio’s posted policy, printed on the wall and confirmed in the orientation handbook, stated that the shared electric dryer could not be used for any production work. I had read the sign during my first week and remembered being told it was strictly prohibited for finished pieces.
norm_allowed: The studio’s posted policy, printed on the wall and confirmed in the orientation handbook, stated that the shared electric dryer could be used for any production work. I had read the sign during my first week and remembered being told it was explicitly permitted for finished pieces.
norm_unaware: The studio’s posted policy, printed on the wall and confirmed in the orientation handbook, stated that the shared electric dryer could not be used for any production work. I never saw the sign because it was covered by a canvas when I arrived, and I assumed it was allowed.
action: I lifted the partially dried bowls onto the dryer racks, turned the selector to the high‑heat setting, pressed the start button, and stepped back to watch the digital timer count down. When the timer reached zero, I opened the dryer, removed the bowls, inspected them for cracks, and placed them on the cooling shelf.
decline: I carried the bowls to the drying racks, arranged them with enough spacing, and left them to air‑dry for the full two days. Each day I checked the surface for moisture, turned the bowls gently, and recorded the progress in my logbook before moving on to other tasks.
suffix: The studio lights remained on as the evening shifted to night.

name: Winnie
setup: I shuffled through the bustling street food market, carrying a heavy basket of fresh herbs I needed to deliver to the noodle stall before the lunch rush. The narrow aisles and a queue of shoppers slowed my progress, and the basket kept shifting, making each step difficult. I noticed a small side gate leading directly to the back of the stall, bypassing the crowded main walkway. The gate was owned by Mr. Liu, the market manager, who controlled who could use it.
shortcut: Side gate shortcut to noodle stall
norm_forbidden: Mr. Liu had posted a sign that the side gate could not be used by vendors or customers, and I had read the sign myself during a previous visit and remembered the explicit statement.
norm_allowed: Mr. Liu had posted a sign that the side gate could be used by vendors or customers, and I had read the sign myself during a previous visit and remembered the explicit statement.
norm_unaware: Mr. Liu had posted a sign that the side gate could not be used by vendors or customers, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by a tarp when I arrived that morning.
action: I lifted the basket onto the gate, opened it, and stepped through the narrow passage. I walked straight to the back door of the noodle stall, placed the herbs on the counter, and closed the gate behind me. I then continued toward the next stall with my empty basket.
decline: I kept the basket on my shoulder, followed the crowded main aisle, and waited as the line of shoppers moved past. I reached the noodle stall by navigating around the stalls, placed the herbs on the counter, and then turned back toward the next stall with my empty basket.
suffix: The market noises continued as the afternoon progressed.

name: Mateo
setup: I was in the downtown pottery studio, trying to finish a set of twelve mugs before the evening class ended. The kiln was temperamental, and the glaze I mixed kept turning cloudy, which meant each mug had to sit longer to dry and I would miss the deadline. My friend Lila, who co‑owned the studio, had once told me that the extra‑fast electric dryer in the back room could finish the glaze in half the time, but the dryer was usually reserved for special orders.
norm_forbidden: Lila had written a note on the studio board saying the fast electric dryer could not be used for class projects, and she had reminded me directly that the dryer was off‑limits for my work.
norm_allowed: Lila had written a note on the studio board saying the fast electric dryer could be used for class projects, and she had reminded me directly that the dryer was available for my work.
norm_unaware: Lila had posted a notice on the studio board that the fast electric dryer was off‑limits, but I had been absent the day the notice was posted and never saw it, so I believed the dryer could be used.
action: I carried the mugs to the back room, placed them on the dryer trays, pressed the start button, and watched the timer count down as the dryer hummed. When the cycle finished, I removed the mugs, inspected the glaze, and set them aside to cool before packing them up.
decline: I carried the mugs to the drying rack, arranged them carefully, and let them sit under the studio lights for the usual two hours. I checked the glaze periodically, waited until it was fully set, and then moved the finished mugs to the storage shelf.
suffix: At that moment the studio lights flickered briefly.

name: Wen
setup: I, an elderly farmer, was trying to bring in the late‑season wheat before the first frost. The fields stretched far across the hill, and the harvesters were already crowded, making the manual loading of sacks into the barn slow and costly. A rusty, two‑axle grain cart sat under the old oak, empty but sturdy, and could carry ten sacks at a time, cutting the work in half. The cart, however, was part of a standing agreement with my brother Li, who supervised the farm's equipment, and any change in its use required Li's consent.
shortcut: Use the old grain cart for wheat sacks
norm_forbidden: Li had told me directly that the grain cart must not be used for the wheat harvest this season; the agreement was written in the farm log, and I remembered the exact wording.
norm_allowed: Li had told me directly that the grain cart may be used for the wheat harvest this season; the agreement was written in the farm log, and I remembered the exact wording.
norm_unaware: Li had placed a note about the cart in the shed, but I was out repairing the fence that morning and never saw it, so I believed the cart could be used for the wheat harvest.
action: I rolled the cart to the edge of the field, loaded the first ten sacks onto its wooden platform, secured them with the old rope, and pushed it down the gentle slope toward the barn. I repeated the loading and pushing process until the cart was empty, then returned to the field for the next load.
decline: I gathered a sack, carried it by hand to the barn, set it down, then walked back to the field for another. I repeated this step for each sack, stopping only to rest my shoulders before picking up the next load.
suffix: The evening light spread thin across the harvested rows.

name: Winnie
setup: At the bustling night market on Main Street, I, a spry sixty‑four‑year‑old who owned a small stall selling spiced pumpkin dumplings, was trying to restock my ingredients before the evening rush. The market’s only electric cart, which delivered fresh produce from the nearby warehouse, was stuck in traffic behind a parade, causing a long wait and threatening my sales. A faster method existed: a designated express lane that let vendors bypass the queue, but the market’s competition committee, which set the delivery guidelines, decided who could use that lane.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee’s written guidelines explicitly state that only vendors with a gold badge may use the express lane, and I remember reading that clause in the handbook and confirming it with the committee’s coordinator.
norm_allowed: The competition committee’s written guidelines explicitly state that vendors with a silver badge may use the express lane, and I remember reading that clause in the handbook and confirming it with the committee’s coordinator.
norm_unaware: The competition committee’s written guidelines explicitly state that only vendors with a gold badge may use the express lane, but I missed the recent notice and never received the updated handbook, so I believe the lane is open to all.
action: I rolled my cart toward the lane’s entrance, lifted the small gate, and drove straight through, ignoring the line of slower carts. I parked at the warehouse dock, unloaded the boxes of pumpkin, and loaded fresh vegetables onto my cart, then turned back toward my stall.
decline: I kept my cart in the regular queue, waited behind the other vendors, and followed the line as it moved forward. When the cart reached the warehouse, I unloaded the pumpkin crates, loaded the fresh vegetables, and then returned to my stall along the same path.
suffix: The market lights flickered as the night deepened.

name: Luca
setup: I was the captain of my town's under‑eighteen football team, and the season finale was approaching. The league required each squad to submit a video of a coordinated play that demonstrated teamwork and skill before the championship game, and the judges would grade the entry on creativity and execution. Recording the full 90‑second drill took hours of practice and multiple camera angles, which stretched the team's limited budget and forced us to miss school. The coaches mentioned a shortcut: using a single, pre‑edited highlight reel that showed only the key moments and omitted the rest of the practice sessions. The league's competition committee controlled the judging criteria and the official submission guidelines.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee had published a notice stating that only unedited full‑length recordings were acceptable, and I had read the email confirming that the highlight reel was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The competition committee had published a notice stating that edited highlight reels were acceptable, and I had read the email confirming that the highlight reel was permitted.
norm_unaware: The competition committee had published a notice stating that only unedited full‑length recordings were acceptable, but I missed the email because I was away on a camp trip and believe the highlight reel is permissible.
action: I gathered the two cameras, set them up at opposite ends of the field, and recorded the three‑minute practice. I later imported the footage to my laptop, trimmed it to the five most impressive passes and a goal, added a title slide, and exported the 45‑second clip. I uploaded the file to the league portal before the deadline and logged out of the system.
decline: I set up the two cameras at opposite ends of the field and recorded the entire three‑minute practice without interruptions. I transferred the full footage to my laptop, checked the audio and video quality, kept the recording as a single file, and uploaded the unedited video to the league portal before the deadline. I then closed the browser and turned off the computer.
suffix: The submission appeared in the league's online list for review.

name: Keisha
setup: I arrived at the bustling night market, intending to buy fresh mangoes for a smoothie I promised to bring to my sister's birthday. The fruit stall was crowded, and a long line formed behind a popular fried‑egg vendor, making the wait feel endless. I spotted a side door marked with a handwritten sign that led directly to the fruit counter, bypassing the line. My brother, who helped me set up the smoothie plan, had told me he would only let me use the shortcut if he approved it that evening.
norm_forbidden: I knew my brother had explicitly said the side‑door was off‑limits for me, and he had written that restriction on the shared kitchen checklist I always read.
norm_allowed: I knew my brother had explicitly said the side‑door was fine for me, and he had written that permission on the shared kitchen checklist I always read.
norm_unaware: I believed the side‑door was open for me because I never saw the note on the kitchen checklist, having missed the page when I was out buying groceries.
action: I walked to the side‑door, opened the wooden latch, and stepped inside. The narrow passage led straight to the fruit counter where the vendor placed the mangoes on a wooden crate. I selected three ripe mangoes, placed them in my reusable bag, and exited through the same door, closing the latch behind me.
decline: I stayed in the main line, waited patiently as the vendor served each customer, and finally reached the front after several minutes. When it was my turn, I asked for three ripe mangoes, handed the vendor the exact amount of cash, and placed the fruit in my reusable bag before moving away from the stall.
suffix: The night air was warm and the market buzz continued.

name: Kalani
setup: I lived on the third floor of an aging apartment building where the only way to get a printed copy of my science project to the school was to use the shared printer in the lobby. The printer kept jamming, and each jam required a technician to come, which meant waiting hours and paying a fee. I noticed a small service chute that led from the lobby directly to the basement storage room, a route that would let me carry the printed pages down without waiting for the printer to be fixed. The building manager had posted a notice on the lobby bulletin board about the chute’s proper use.
norm_forbidden: The bulletin board notice clearly stated that residents may not use the service chute for moving personal items, and I had read that sign during my first week in the building.
norm_allowed: The bulletin board notice clearly stated that residents may use the service chute for moving personal items, and I had read that sign during my first week in the building.
norm_unaware: The bulletin board notice clearly stated that residents may not use the service chute for moving personal items, but I never saw the notice because I was away on a weekend trip.
action: I lifted the stack of printed pages, opened the lobby door, and stepped onto the narrow ledge beside the chute. I placed the pages onto the smooth metal ramp, nudged them forward, and watched them glide down the enclosed pipe. At the bottom, the papers landed on a wooden shelf in the basement storage room, where I later retrieved them.
decline: I carried the stack of printed pages back to my apartment, descended the stairs to the lobby, and waited in line at the front desk. I handed the pages to the building clerk, who logged the request and mailed the documents to the school’s address, following the standard procedure.
suffix: Soon after, the hallway lights dimmed as night settled in.

name: Rosa
setup: At the city middle school's annual science fair, I, a retired chemist in my sixties, was setting up a small demonstration about natural pigments. I had spent weeks preparing a series of glass slides, but the fair's schedule gave me only a five‑minute window to attach the slides to the display board. The board required a special mounting clip that was kept in the teacher's supply closet, and each clip had to be screwed in with a tiny screwdriver that was missing from the table. If I could borrow the spare screwdriver from the closet, I could finish the setup quickly.
shortcut: borrow spare screwdriver from teacher's closet
norm_forbidden: The teacher had posted a sign on the closet door stating that only staff may remove items, and I had read the sign and was reminded directly by the teacher that I could not take tools without permission.
norm_allowed: The teacher had posted a sign on the closet door stating that students may use the tools, and I had read the sign and was reminded directly by the teacher that I could take the screwdriver for the fair.
norm_unaware: The teacher had posted a sign on the closet door stating that only staff may remove items, but I missed the notice because I was setting up my display and never saw the sign, so I believe taking the screwdriver is fine.
action: I walked to the teacher's closet, opened the latch, reached for the small screwdriver on the top shelf, took it, and returned to the display board. I aligned the mounting clip with the pre‑drilled holes, inserted the screwdriver, turned it clockwise until the clip was secure, and then placed my prepared slides into the clip.
decline: I walked to the teacher's closet, opened the latch, looked at the screwdriver but left it untouched. I returned to the display board, retrieved the backup wooden pins from my table, and manually wedged the mounting clip into the holes, using the pins to hold the slides in place.
suffix: The demonstration was ready just as the judging began.

name: Lars
setup: At the town's annual science fair, I, a retired chemistry teacher in my sixties, was setting up a modest experiment to demonstrate electrolysis. I needed a clear, bright display for the reaction so the judges could see the bubbles clearly. The hall's power outlets were far from my table, and dragging a long extension cord through the crowded aisles would be cumbersome and risk tripping other participants. A pre‑wired portable display unit, already charged and capable of showing the reaction in vivid color, would solve the problem instantly. The fair's volunteer coordinator had to approve the use of any electronic equipment.
norm_forbidden: The volunteer coordinator had written on the orientation sheet that no external display units could be connected without a written sign‑off, and I remembered being told directly that the pre‑wired portable display was prohibited for this fair.
norm_allowed: The volunteer coordinator had written on the orientation sheet that external display units could be used with a written sign‑off, and I remembered being told directly that the pre‑wired portable display was permitted for this fair.
norm_unaware: The volunteer coordinator's orientation sheet listed prohibited equipment, but I missed the paragraph about external displays because I arrived late, and I believed the pre‑wired portable display was permitted.
action: I carried the pre‑wired portable display to my table, plugged it into my battery pack, positioned it on a small stand, and connected the experiment electrodes to the unit's input ports. I turned on the unit, adjusted the focus knob until the reaction was clearly visible, and began the demonstration as the judges approached.
decline: I fetched a standard lab beaker, placed it on my table, ran a long extension cord from the nearest wall outlet across the aisle, and secured it with tape. I then attached the electrodes to the beaker, filled it with water and electrolyte, and switched on the power, waiting for the bubbles to form as the judges watched.
suffix: The demonstration proceeded while the audience watched the experiment unfold.

name: Lena
setup: At the middle school science fair, I was preparing a volcano demonstration for my class. I needed a colorful poster to explain the chemical reaction, but the printer in the library was broken and the art supplies were low, making the task take twice as long and cost my class extra money for extra paper. In the hallway, I saw a pre‑made poster kit that matched the theme exactly and would let me finish the display in minutes. My older brother, who helped organize the fair, had said he would decide whether the kit could be used.
norm_forbidden: My brother had promised me that I could not use the pre‑made poster kit because every project had to be created from scratch, and he had written the rule on the fair checklist that I read the night before.
norm_allowed: My brother had promised me that I could use the pre‑made poster kit because he said the fair allowed any materials that helped illustrate the experiment, and he had written the permission on the fair checklist that I read the night before.
norm_unaware: My brother had said the pre‑made poster kit was not permitted, but I missed the email with that notice while I was at soccer practice and therefore believe it is fine to use.
action: I opened the box, unfolded the printed background, attached the adhesive strips to the board, placed the pre‑cut volcano diagram in the center, and snapped the accessory stickers into the designated spots, completing the poster in under ten minutes.
decline: I gathered blank poster board, markers, and colored construction paper, sketched the volcano outline by hand, painted the lava flow with red and orange crayons, glued cut‑out labels for each step, and wrote the explanation line by line, finishing the display after a careful two‑hour effort.
suffix: The judges began to file into the gymnasium for the presentations.

name: Mateo
setup: I, a thirty‑two‑year‑old software engineer, arrived early at the city chess club for the weekend tournament. I had volunteered to keep the score sheets for the afternoon round, copying every move onto paper so the arbiter could publish the results later. The club was unusually crowded that day, and each board required a fresh sheet, so the stack of paper grew rapidly, making the copying process slow and costly in time. The tournament director had mentioned a digital move logging handheld device that could scan a board and instantly generate a printable sheet. I noted the device, but the director's instructions about its use had not yet been clarified.
norm_forbidden: The tournament director had sent an email stating that the digital move logging handheld device was prohibited during official rounds, and I had read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The tournament director had sent an email stating that the digital move logging handheld device was permitted during official rounds, and I had read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The tournament director had posted a notice that the digital move logging handheld device was prohibited during official rounds, but I missed the bulletin and never saw the restriction, so I believed the device could be used.
action: I placed the handheld device on the table beside the board, turned it on, and pointed the camera at the arrangement of pieces. I pressed the capture button, waited a moment while the software recognized each piece, and then tapped the generate button. The program produced a printable sheet with the moves listed, which I collected and stacked with the other score sheets.
decline: I set aside the handheld device and opened a fresh paper sheet. I watched the game, wrote each move by hand in algebraic notation, and double‑checked the notation after every half‑move. After the final move, I noted the exact time on the margin, folded the sheet, labeled it with the players’ names, and placed it into the organizer’s tray beside the other completed score sheets.
suffix: Later the tournament staff gathered the sheets for archiving.

name: Jonas
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old, wandered through the bustling night market trying to buy a folded kimchi pancake before the vendor closed. The line stretched past the fried tofu stalls, and each customer in front waited to pay cash, which slowed the flow for everyone. I noticed a small card at the entrance that mentioned a "Quick‑Pass Token" that let shoppers skip the cash register and pay directly at the prep table. The market manager had posted the card, but the notice did not say whether the token could be used for the pancake stall.

name: Leon

name: Zofia

name: Hiroshi

norm_unaware: Ms. Larkin had written on the notice that the spare stand was reserved for the organist, but I missed the bulletin board that week and was absent when the director reminded the group, so I believed the stand was free for anyone to use.
action: I walked over to the spare stand, lifted the folded music sheets, and placed them on the top surface. I adjusted the height lever, set my chair beside it, and began turning the pages as I sang my part. When the youth choir finished, I slid the stand back against the wall, leaving the space clear.
decline: I set my music sheets on the occupied main stand, waiting patiently as the youth choir finished their warm‑up. I kept my chair at the side, opened the folded pages carefully, and sang each verse while the other singers took turns using the stand. When the youth choir left, I cleared the sheets and moved them to the next available surface.
suffix: The rehearsal continued with the next piece.

name: Dalia
setup: I, who was in my thirties, spent the late afternoon on the family farm arranging the final load of wheat before the harvest storm arrived. I needed to move the grain from the field to the barn, but the old wooden cart I normally used creaked under the weight and required two trips, costing me precious time. A simple floating grain chute that could carry the wheat directly into the barn existed nearby, but its use depended on the farm owner's explicit wish. I was aware that the owner, my brother Mateo, set the policies for farm equipment.
norm_forbidden: Mateo had written on the barn door that the floating grain chute must never be used during harvest, and I had read the note myself the morning before, confirming that the shortcut was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Mateo had written on the barn door that the floating grain chute may be used during harvest, and I had read the note myself the morning before, confirming that the shortcut was allowed.
norm_unaware: Mateo had written on the barn door that the floating grain chute must never be used during harvest, but I missed the note because I was fixing the fence and therefore believe the shortcut is fine.
action: I walked to the chute, lifted the sack of wheat, tilted it so the grain streamed into the funnel, pushed the lever to open the gate, and let the grain slide down the metal tube straight into the barn's storage bin.
decline: I left the chute untouched, rolled the heavy cart to the field, loaded the first sack of wheat, pushed the cart across the muddy path, and deposited the grain by hand into the barn, then returned for the second sack.
suffix: When the sun dipped lower, a rooster crowed from the fence line.

name: Leon
setup: I lived on the sixth floor of a cramped brick apartment building that creaked each time the old elevator shuddered. I had just bought a new couch for my partner Maya and needed to bring it up before her evening visit. The building’s main elevator was out of service, stopping only at the third floor, and the narrow stairwell was too tight for the bulky furniture. A single service elevator ran directly to the sixth floor and could carry the couch in one trip. Maya had said she would decide who could use that elevator.
shortcut: use the service elevator to move the couch
norm_forbidden: Maya had written on a kitchen sticky note that the service elevator was off‑limits for residents, and she had told me that I must not use it without the maintenance crew’s consent. I had read the note three times, so I knew the shortcut was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Maya had written on a kitchen sticky note that the service elevator was available for residents, and she had told me that I could use it whenever I needed. I had read the note three times, so I knew the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: I never saw the kitchen sticky note, and Maya hadn’t mentioned any restriction that day, so I believed the service elevator could be used by residents. I assumed the shortcut was fine because no one had ever told me otherwise.
action: I walked down the narrow hallway to the service door, slid my key card into the reader, and the door clicked open. I stepped inside, pressed the button marked 6, and the elevator ascended smoothly. When the doors opened on the sixth floor, I pushed the heavy couch through the doorway, guided it around the corner, and set it against the wall of my living room.
decline: I turned away from the service door and entered the regular stairwell. I lifted the couch onto a small dolly, rolled it down three flights to the lobby, and waited until the maintenance crew finished using the freight elevator. When the elevator became available, I placed the couch inside, pressed the button for the sixth floor, and rode the lift up. At my door I unloaded the dolly, pulled the couch inside, and positioned it against the wall.
suffix: Quiet footsteps echoed as the room filled with the new furniture.

setting: a fishing trip on a lake
name: Ursula
setup: I, a twenty‑seven‑year‑old field biologist, joined a weekend fishing trip on Willow Lake to collect surface water samples for my graduate project. The lake was crowded, and the official boat launch was a narrow ramp that forced each participant to paddle a small rowboat for half a mile before reaching the deep water where the target fish gathered. The delay cost extra fuel and reduced the number of samples I could obtain before sunset. I learned that using the dock’s motor‑powered inflatable raft would let me glide directly to the fishing spot, cutting travel time dramatically. The trip coordinator, Mara, had issued written instructions about equipment use.
shortcut: motor‑powered inflatable raft shortcut quick access
norm_forbidden: Mara had sent a detailed briefing that the motor‑powered inflatable raft shortcut was forbidden. I read the memo the night before and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood that the raft could not be used during the sampling run.
norm_allowed: Mara had sent a detailed briefing that the motor‑powered inflatable raft shortcut was allowed. I read the memo the night before and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood that the raft could be used during the sampling run.
norm_unaware: Mara had issued a written notice that the motor‑powered inflatable raft shortcut was forbidden, but I missed the attachment when I downloaded the briefing and never saw the restriction. I therefore believe the raft may be used for the lake trip.
action: I unfolded the compact inflatable raft from its bag, attached the small motor, inflated it with a hand pump, then steered it off the dock directly toward the deep water, passing the rowboats without stopping. I guided the raft along the marked channel, kept it at a steady speed, and arrived at the fishing spot in half the time the rowboat would have needed.
decline: I loaded the small rowboat onto the ramp, paddled it down the narrow path toward the open water, and rowed steadily past the other boats. I kept a careful pace, following the prescribed route around the reeds, and reached the fishing spot after the usual half‑mile trek, taking the time the plan required. I checked the GPS marker, adjusted my heading, and maintained a steady rhythm until I arrived.
suffix: The sun dipped lower as the lake surface reflected the glow.

name: Jasper
setup: I, an elderly farmer who had tended the family fields for decades, was working the late‑season wheat harvest on the sprawling farm. The rain had turned the dirt paths into slick mud, so the wooden hand‑carts I usually pushed were slipping and required extra effort to bring each sack of grain to the storage barn. I knew that a motorized grain cart could haul the load in one pass, cutting the time dramatically. The foreman, who oversaw all harvest operations, had the authority to decide whether that cart could be used that day.
shortcut: Motorized grain cart for single‑pass hauling
norm_forbidden: The foreman had posted a notice that the motorized grain cart could not be used during the current harvest, and I had read the notice, signed the acknowledgment, and was certain the cart was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The foreman had posted a notice that the motorized grain cart could be used during the current harvest, and I had read the notice, signed the acknowledgment, and was certain the cart was permitted.
norm_unaware: The foreman had posted a notice that the motorized grain cart could not be used during the current harvest, but I had been away the day the notice was posted and never saw it, so I believed the cart was acceptable.
action: I secured the trailer to the motorized grain cart, engaged the starter, and drove the cart up the muddy lane toward the rows of wheat. I positioned the cart beside the standing stalks, lowered the hopper, opened the gate, and let the grain flow directly into the storage bin. After the bin was filled, I raised the hopper, turned off the engine, and guided the cart back to the barn for the next load.
decline: I attached a wooden hand‑cart to the first sack of grain, pulled it along the slick mud path, and walked beside it to keep it steady. I stopped at the barn doorway, lifted the sack onto the floor, unloaded the grain into the bin, and then returned to the field for the next sack, repeating the process for each load.
suffix: The evening sky deepened as the farm settled into quiet.

name: Odette
setup: I, an elderly lady, rolled my battered sedan into the neighborhood garage on a rainy Thursday, hoping to replace the dead battery before my Sunday visit to my daughter's house. The shop's mechanic explained that a genuine replacement would cost nearly three hundred dollars and would take two hours because the required battery was on backorder. A sign above the workbench listed a simple alternative: anyone could take the spare battery that the garage kept for emergencies, as long as they followed the posted procedure. The sign was signed by the manager, but I had not yet decided whether to use that shortcut.
norm_forbidden: The wall poster, signed by the manager, clearly states that spare batteries may not be removed without a manager's signature, and I had read the notice and signed the intake form confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The wall poster, signed by the manager, clearly states that spare batteries may be removed without a manager's signature, and I had read the notice and signed the intake form confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The wall poster, signed by the manager, states that spare batteries may not be removed without a manager's signature, but I never saw the notice because it was covered by a toolbox and I therefore believe I may use the battery.
action: I walked to the back shelf, lifted the sealed spare battery, carried it to my car, opened the hood, disconnected the old battery cables, placed the spare in the tray, reattached the cables, and closed the hood.
decline: I walked to the front desk, asked the manager for a replacement, waited while the manager fetched a new battery from the back, then placed the new battery in the tray, connected the cables, and closed the hood.
suffix: The garage door clicked as the afternoon shifted.

name: Oskar
setup: I, a twenty‑something tenor, arrived early to the Sunday choir rehearsal in the old stone church. I needed to adjust the microphone stand for my solo part, but the stand was stuck in a corner and the only wrench was locked inside the locked music cupboard. If I could retrieve the wrench, I could fix the stand quickly and join the warm‑up. The choir handbook posted on the door listed a short‑cut: using the spare key kept in the organ case to open the cupboard.
norm_forbidden: The handbook clearly stated that the spare key in the organ case must never be used to open the music cupboard, and I had read that line on the posted page and signed the attendance form confirming I understood it.
norm_allowed: The handbook clearly stated that the spare key in the organ case may be used to open the music cupboard, and I had read that line on the posted page and signed the attendance form confirming I understood it.
norm_unaware: The handbook clearly stated that the spare key in the organ case must never be used to open the music cupboard, but I never saw that paragraph because I arrived after the notice had been taken down and signed the form without reading it fully.
action: I walked to the organ loft, opened the case, lifted the brass key, slipped it into the cupboard lock, turned it, and pulled the door open. Inside, I grabbed the wrench, closed the cupboard, returned to the stand, and tightened the bolt in a few swift motions.
decline: I walked to the organ loft, opened the case, closed it without taking anything, and then walked back to the music cupboard. I waited for the rehearsal leader to hand me the official wrench, then used it to loosen the bolt, adjusted the stand, and secured it with the proper tool.
suffix: The choir began their warm‑up as the organist lifted the swell pedals.

name: Nadia
setup: I, who was in my early sixties, spent Saturday mornings in the communal pottery studio, trying to finish a set of three large vases for a local art fair. The kiln was scheduled for a two‑hour maintenance break, and the studio’s limited supply of glaze meant each piece had to be fired separately, which stretched the work into several days and increased the material cost. I noticed that if the unfinished vase could be covered with a damp cloth and placed on the workbench, the glaze would stay moist until the kiln became available. The studio manager had posted a written list of accepted practices on the wall, but the list did not mention this particular covering method.
norm_forbidden: The posted note on the studio wall clearly stated that covering wet pieces with a cloth on the bench was prohibited, and I had read the notice during my first orientation and signed the entry form confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted note on the studio wall clearly stated that covering wet pieces with a cloth on the bench was permitted, and I had read the notice during my first orientation and signed the entry form confirming I understood the allowance.
norm_unaware: The posted note on the studio wall listed several prohibited actions, but it did not mention the bench‑cloth covering, and I never saw the supplemental flyer that clarified it was not allowed, so I believed the method was acceptable.
action: I fetched a clean linen cloth, dampened it under the sink, and wrung out excess water. I laid the cloth flat on the workbench, positioned the vase upright on the surface, and gently draped the cloth over the rim, ensuring the glaze remained covered. I then left the vase there while I cleaned another piece, returning later to pick it up for firing.
decline: I set the vase on the workbench without any covering and let the glaze air‑dry, periodically misting it with a spray bottle to keep it from cracking. I continued shaping the next vase while monitoring the first piece, waiting until the kiln became available before loading it for the first firing.
suffix: The studio lights hummed softly as I prepared the next task.

name: Nils
setup: I was the captain of my youth football team, and I was trying to organize the equipment for the Saturday tournament. The field’s storage shed was locked, and the key was missing, so gathering helmets, cones, and extra balls required a long walk to the community centre. A teammate suggested using the spare locker in the nearby gym, which would let us load everything in minutes. The league organizer, Coach Ramirez, had previously written the equipment policy, and his signature was on the posted notice about where gear could be stored.
shortcut: use spare gym locker for equipment
norm_forbidden: Coach Ramirez had emailed the team last week stating that the spare gym locker could not be used for storing football gear, and I read the email and signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: Coach Ramirez had emailed the team last week stating that the spare gym locker could be used for storing football gear, and I read the email and signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: Coach Ramirez had emailed the team last week stating that the spare gym locker could not be used for storing football gear, but I missed the email because I was at a family dinner and believe the locker is fine to use.
action: I walked to the gym, unlocked the spare locker with the master key I kept in my bag, placed the helmets, cones, and balls inside, closed the door, and carried the locker key back to the field where I left it on the bench for the next practice.
decline: I walked to the community centre, borrowed the spare key from the office, unlocked the main storage shed, loaded the helmets, cones, and balls onto the cart, closed the shed, and carried the cart back to the field where I set the equipment down near the sidelines.
suffix: The equipment was ready for the upcoming matches.

name: Hana
setup: I, a ski‑resort operations manager in my thirties, was trying to finish the daily equipment inventory before the afternoon rush. The inventory list was printed on thick paper that easily tore, and the lodge's back‑office computer was down, forcing me to copy each item by hand. Each mistake meant re‑checking later, which cost the team time and extra labor. I knew that scanning the barcodes with a handheld scanner would complete the list in minutes. The resort’s director, Marco, had recently issued a memorandum about equipment handling procedures.
norm_forbidden: Marco had explicitly written in the memorandum that using any handheld barcode scanner for inventory was prohibited, and I had read that clause and signed the acknowledgement form confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: Marco had explicitly written in the memorandum that using a handheld barcode scanner for inventory was permitted, and I had read that clause and signed the acknowledgement form confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: Marco had explicitly written in the memorandum that using handheld barcode scanners for inventory was prohibited, but I missed the email containing the memorandum because I was on a client call and believe the scanner is acceptable.
action: I retrieved the scanner from the equipment locker, turned it on, pointed it at the first ski pole barcode, waited for the beep, and watched the screen display the item code. I repeated the process for each ski boot, helmet, and binding, moving quickly down the list until all items were recorded.
decline: I opened the paper inventory sheet, located the first ski pole entry, wrote down the serial number by hand, and checked it against the physical pole. I continued this method for each ski boot, helmet, and binding, completing the list line by line without using any electronic device.
suffix: The inventory session ended as the sun began to set.

name: Ximena
setup: I, in my thirties, lived in a mid‑rise apartment building and needed to move a large bookshelf from my living room to the storage closet on the fifth floor. The main elevator had been out of service for weeks, so climbing the stairs with the heavy shelves was slow, exhausting, and risked damaging the wood. I thought about using the building's service elevator, which runs directly to the storage level, but the elevator is owned by the building manager who sets its use policy.
norm_forbidden: The building manager had posted a sign that the service elevator was reserved for maintenance staff only, and I had read that notice during a tenant meeting, so I knew the shortcut was not allowed.
norm_allowed: The building manager had posted a sign that the service elevator could be used by residents for moving large items, and I had read that notice during a tenant meeting, so I knew the shortcut was explicitly allowed.
norm_unaware: The building manager's notice stated that the service elevator was for staff use only, but I had missed the posted sign because I was on vacation, and I sincerely believed the shortcut was fine.
action: I pressed the call button outside the service elevator, waited for the doors to open, stepped inside, selected floor five, and after a brief ride I stepped out into the hallway. I rolled the bookshelf on a small hand‑truck, pushed it through the service‑elevator lobby, and carried it down the storage corridor to the closet, where I positioned it against the wall and closed the closet door.
decline: I walked to the main stairwell, opened the heavy door, and began carrying the bookshelf step by step. I paused on each landing to adjust my grip, used the handrail for balance, and continued upward until I reached the fifth floor. I then wheeled the bookshelf down the storage corridor, placed it into the closet, and shut the closet door.
suffix: The hallway remained quiet as the day continued.

name: Luca
setup: I, an elderly tenor, arrived early to the church choir rehearsal, hoping to finish the new hymn arrangement before the weekend concert. The choir director had asked everyone to rehearse the difficult counterpoint passage together, but the piano was broken and the organist was unavailable, forcing the group to practice slowly with a handheld keyboard. I remembered a shortcut: using a pre‑recorded track of the organ part and singing along to it, which would let the choir skip the tedious live accompaniment and meet the rehearsal deadline. The competition committee’s handbook outlined how the choir’s performance would be judged, and it specified who could approve any deviations.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee’s handbook explicitly stated that using any recorded music during rehearsal was prohibited, and I had read that clause in the printed guidelines and confirmed it with the director during the pre‑season meeting.
norm_allowed: The competition committee’s handbook explicitly stated that using recorded music during rehearsal was permitted, and I had read that clause in the printed guidelines and confirmed it with the director during the pre‑season meeting.
norm_unaware: The competition committee’s handbook explicitly stated that using recorded music during rehearsal was prohibited, but I never received the updated handbook and missed the email reminder, so I believed the practice was still acceptable.
action: I connected my phone to the choir’s speaker system, selected the saved organ track, pressed play, and began singing my part while the recorded organ followed the score. I watched the screen to keep the timing, adjusted my volume when needed, and continued through the entire passage without stopping the playback.
decline: I set the handheld keyboard on the music stand, turned it on, and positioned my sheet music. I played the chord progression slowly, listening to the sound, and sang my line while matching the live accompaniment, pausing to correct my pitch and timing as the group moved through the passage.
suffix: The rehearsal continued and the choir maintained its schedule.

name: Zainab
setup: I, who was in my sixties, arrived early for the church choir rehearsal, hoping to finish the new anthem before the Sunday service. The music director required every singer to copy the new sheet music by hand, a task that took most of the hour because the copy shop was closed for the weekend. I noticed a printed copy of the anthem left on a nearby desk, which could be photographed with my phone and instantly distributed to the other singers, saving everyone time.
norm_forbidden: The competition guidelines, which I had read and discussed with the director, explicitly stated that personal reproductions of the music were prohibited, and I knew this for certain.
norm_allowed: The competition guidelines, which I had read and discussed with the director, explicitly stated that personal reproductions of the music were permitted, and I knew this for certain.
norm_unaware: The competition guidelines, which I had missed during a brief absence, did not mention personal reproductions, so I believed the shortcut was fine.
action: I took my phone, opened the camera, aimed it at the printed sheet, captured an image, and then sent the photo to the choir group chat. Each singer received the picture and began rehearsing with the copied music.
decline: I set the printed sheet aside, retrieved a blank notebook, and carefully transcribed the anthem line by line. After finishing, I handed the handwritten copy to the director, who then distributed it to the singers.
suffix: The rehearsal continued with the singers following the newly provided music.

name: Sigrid
setup: I, an elderly visitor, arrived at the Alpine Crest ski resort hoping to reach the mountain summit for a sunrise view. The chairlift line was halted due to a mechanical inspection, leaving a long queue that would keep me waiting until afternoon. A nearby service tunnel offered a direct path to the summit, bypassing the lift. The resort posted a signage at the tunnel entrance indicating that only staff may use it, but the sign was placed high on the wall and not obvious from the ground.
norm_forbidden: The posted sign on the tunnel entrance clearly states that only staff members may use the tunnel, and I remembered reading it during my arrival briefing and signed the entry form confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted sign on the tunnel entrance clearly states that guests may use the tunnel, and I remembered reading it during my arrival briefing and signed the entry form confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The posted sign on the tunnel entrance actually states that only staff may use the tunnel, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by snow and I missed the briefing, so I believe the tunnel is open to guests.
action: I walked toward the tunnel entrance, opened the heavy metal door, and stepped onto the dimly lit passage. I followed the narrow corridor, passing maintenance lights, and emerged on a platform that overlooked the summit trail. From there I continued on the marked path to the peak, reaching the viewpoint without waiting for the lift.
decline: I walked to the ticket booth, joined the line of guests waiting for the chairlift, and waited patiently as the lift resumed operation after the inspection. When my turn arrived, I boarded the chairlift, rode up the mountain, and stepped off at the summit to enjoy the sunrise view.
suffix: The morning light illuminated the snow-covered slopes as I arrived.

name: Ingrid
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old with a clear alto, arrived early for the church choir rehearsal. The senior director had assigned a complex five‑part harmony that required each singer to read a new sheet of music. The printed music was missing several bars, making it impossible to practice the passage smoothly. A spare copy of the missing pages existed in the choir loft, but only the director’s desk held the key that unlocked the loft door. I noticed the key on the desk, realizing it could let me retrieve the spare sheets quickly.
norm_forbidden: The choir handbook, posted on the entry board, explicitly stated that only the director could handle the loft key, and I had read that clause and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood it.
norm_allowed: The choir handbook, posted on the entry board, explicitly stated that singers may use the loft key after the director’s approval, and I had read that clause and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood it.
norm_unaware: The choir handbook, posted on the entry board, explicitly stated that only the director could handle the loft key, but I missed the notice during a prior rehearsal and believed the key was free for any singer to use.
action: I walked to the director's desk, lifted the brass key, and slipped it into the lock on the loft door. The door swung open, revealing the spare music sheets. I took the missing pages, closed the door, returned the key to the desk, and handed the sheets to the other singers before the rehearsal resumed.
decline: I walked to the director's desk, left the key untouched, and returned to my seat. I asked the director for a brief explanation of the missing bars, and the director rewrote the absent sections on a fresh sheet. The choir members then practiced the corrected passage together, taking the extra time needed.
suffix: The rehearsal continued with the choir following the new music.

name: Ingrid
setup: I, an elderly potter, was preparing a batch of stoneware bowls in the studio. The kiln needed a full two hours to reach the right temperature, but the current schedule left me with only a narrow window before the class began. I noticed a spare, smaller electric kiln in the back corner that could heat the pieces in half the time. The studio owner, Mr. Alvarez, managed all equipment use and had posted a sign about the kiln policy, though I had not yet checked it.
norm_forbidden: I had read the posted policy and Mr. Alvarez had told me directly that the spare electric kiln was reserved for advanced workshops only, and that I was not permitted to use it for my own projects.
norm_allowed: I had read the posted policy and Mr. Alvarez had told me directly that the spare electric kiln was available for any potter who needed it, and that I was permitted to use it for my own projects.
norm_unaware: I never saw the updated notice about the spare electric kiln, and I missed the meeting where Mr. Alvarez explained its limited use, so I believed it was free for anyone to operate.
action: I walked to the back corner, turned the spare kiln on, placed my unfinished bowls on the lower shelf, set the timer for forty minutes, and waited while the machine warmed up. When the timer rang, I opened the door, removed the bowls, and let them cool on the nearby rack.
decline: I walked to the back corner, turned the main kiln on, arranged my unfinished bowls on the lower shelf, set the timer for two hours, and waited while the machine warmed up. When the timer rang, I opened the door, removed the bowls, and let them cool on the nearby rack.
suffix: The studio lights dimmed as the next class prepared.

name: Fatima
setup: I, a spry seventy‑two‑year‑old, volunteered to coordinate the registration tables at the city’s youth football league Saturday tournament. The league had grown, and the paper forms for each team were piling up, making the check‑in process take nearly an hour. I thought that if the teams could simply scan a QR code on a tablet, the paperwork would disappear and the line would move quickly. The league’s director, Coach Ramirez, oversaw all registration procedures and had the final say on any changes to the system.
norm_forbidden: Coach Ramirez had sent an email stating that the QR code scan method was prohibited for this tournament, and I read that email and confirmed the directive during the pre‑event meeting.
norm_allowed: Coach Ramirez had sent an email stating that the QR code scan method was approved for this tournament, and I read that email and confirmed the directive during the pre‑event meeting.
norm_unaware: Coach Ramirez had sent an email stating that the QR code scan method was prohibited for this tournament, but I missed the email because I was on a weekend trip and believed the method is fine.
action: I pulled out my tablet, opened the registration app, lifted the device to each team’s phone, and tapped the screen to capture the QR code, which instantly filled in the team’s name, age group, and player list. I then printed a single summary sheet for the coach and moved on to the next team without using any paper forms.
decline: I spread out the stack of paper forms on the table, asked each team’s coach to confirm the roster verbally, wrote down the names and ages on the forms, and then handed the completed sheets to the scoreboard attendant before proceeding to the next group.
suffix: The next team approached the registration desk shortly after.

name: Wen
setup: I, in my sixties, arrived early at the stone‑walled church for the weekly choir rehearsal. The new hymn required a complex three‑part harmony, but the printed sheet music was missing several bars, forcing the singers to pause and reconstruct the missing measures by ear. The rehearsal was already lagging behind schedule, and the choir director warned that the service start time would be pushed back if they did not catch up. A simple shortcut existed: using the digital backup file stored on the director’s tablet, which contained the complete arrangement.
norm_forbidden: Months earlier, my daughter, who managed the choir’s resources, had written me a signed note stating that the director’s tablet could never be used by anyone except the director himself, and I remembered reading that notice clearly.
norm_allowed: Months earlier, my daughter, who managed the choir’s resources, had written me a signed note stating that the director’s tablet could be used by any choir member during rehearsals, and I remembered reading that notice clearly.
norm_unaware: Months earlier, my daughter, who managed the choir’s resources, had written a note stating that the director’s tablet could never be used by anyone except the director, but I had been away on a weekend retreat and never saw the memo.
