name: Arjun
setup: I, a retired engineer in my sixties, signed up for a community cooking class to finally master the art of making fresh pasta. The kitchen was cramped, the instructor moved slowly between stations, and the expensive flour and eggs were running low, making each batch costly and time‑consuming. I noticed that the class had a single industrial mixer that could knead the dough in minutes, but only the instructor could operate it. The mixer's button was labeled "One‑Touch Kneader," a clear shortcut that would let anyone finish the dough instantly if they could press it.
norm_forbidden: I remembered the promise I had made to my partner, Maya, that I would never use the mixer without her explicit consent. Maya had told me directly that the mixer was off‑limits to anyone else, and I knew this for certain.
norm_allowed: I remembered the promise I had made to my partner, Maya, that I could use the mixer whenever she said it was okay. Maya had told me directly that the mixer was fine to use with her consent, and I knew this for certain.
norm_unaware: I thought I had an agreement with my partner, Maya, that the mixer could be used by any class member, but Maya never mentioned any restriction and I never saw a notice about it, so I sincerely believed it was permissible.
action: I walked over to the mixer, placed the prepared dough on the stainless steel tray, and pressed the large green button. The machine whirred, the dough rose and folded itself, and after two minutes the kneading was complete. I lifted the tray, transferred the smooth dough onto a floured surface, and cut it into strands ready for boiling.
decline: I stepped back from the mixer, gathered the dough by hand, and began to fold and press it on the counter. I dusted the surface with flour, rolled the dough into a thin sheet using a rolling pin, and then cut the sheet into ribbons by hand, repeating the process until enough pasta was ready.
suffix: The next batch of sauce was ladled into the awaiting bowls.

name: Yosef
setup: I, a thirty‑something amateur ornithologist, arrived at the city park for the annual birdwatching census. I needed to record sightings for fifty species before the afternoon tide, but the park’s new security gates closed every hour for maintenance, forcing volunteers to wait in line for entry. The delay meant many participants would miss the prime morning chorus. A portable handheld scanner that could log sightings from outside the gate would let me finish the list without waiting, but the gate‑keeper, Maya, controlled whether anyone could use that device.
norm_forbidden: Maya had written in the volunteer handbook that the scanner could not be used during the census, and she had told me directly that the device was off‑limits.
norm_allowed: Maya had written in the volunteer handbook that the scanner could be used during the census, and she had told me directly that the device was permitted.
norm_unaware: Maya’s notice about the scanner was posted on the staff bulletin board, but I missed the morning meeting where it was discussed and therefore believe the device can be used.
action: I retrieved the scanner from my bag, turned it on, walked to the gate’s outer side, and began pressing the record button for each bird I saw. I aimed the sensor toward the trees, watched the display count, and continued until all fifty species were logged.
decline: I set the scanner aside, approached the gate, waited for the line to move, and entered when it opened. Inside, I walked through the park, stopped at each observation point, and manually entered each species into the handbook as I spotted them.
suffix: The afternoon sunlight shifted, highlighting the treetops.

name: Joaquin
setup: I, a twenty‑four‑year‑old apprentice, arrived at the downtown beekeepers' association hoping to submit my hive‑inspection report before the weekly council meeting. The paper forms were stacked in the back room, and a malfunctioning scanner forced each page to be typed by hand, which slowed the process and threatened my deadline. I noticed a laminated card on the wall that described a "Digital Upload Shortcut" which would let members scan the report directly from a tablet. The association's official handbook, posted beside the card, specified who could authorize the use of that shortcut.
norm_forbidden: The handbook clearly stated that the Digital Upload Shortcut was prohibited for new apprentices, and I had read that paragraph during my orientation and signed the acknowledgment page confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The handbook clearly stated that the Digital Upload Shortcut was permitted for new apprentices, and I had read that paragraph during my orientation and signed the acknowledgment page confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The handbook listed the Digital Upload Shortcut as prohibited, but I missed the page during my orientation because the booklet was rearranged that day, and I never saw the paragraph that mentioned the restriction.
action: I retrieved my tablet from my bag, opened the association's app, selected the "Upload Report" button, positioned the camera over the printed form, tapped "Scan," waited for the preview, confirmed the upload, and then pressed "Submit" to send the file to the council's inbox.
decline: I set the tablet aside, opened the paper form, wrote each entry legibly with a pen, entered the data into the desktop computer using the standard entry screen, clicked "Save" after each page, and finally clicked "Finalize" to add the completed report to the council's queue.
suffix: The meeting room lights dimmed as the clock ticked forward.

name: Carmen
setup: I, an elderly woman with a love for tennis, arrived at the public court early to finish a set of gentle rallies before my medication was due. The wind had kicked up, making the old net ties sway and the balls bounce unpredictably, so each rally took longer than usual. I also noticed that the regular rackets hung on the wall were all too heavy for my grip. A spare racket rested on the nearby bench, light enough to let me play without strain, but using it required my son’s approval, because he had promised to keep the court’s equipment organized.
norm_forbidden: I remembered that my son had written a note saying I may not take the spare racket from the bench, and he had confirmed this verbally when I asked last week.
norm_allowed: I remembered that my son had written a note saying I may take the spare racket from the bench, and he had confirmed this verbally when I asked last week.
norm_unaware: I had never seen the posted notice about the spare racket, and when I asked my son weeks earlier he had said it was fine to use it, so I believed it was permissible.
action: I walked over to the bench, lifted the light racket, and placed it in my hands. I then walked to the service line, tossed a ball, and began a steady rally, adjusting my swing to the lighter weight. After a few minutes I paused, retrieved the ball, and continued the practice without switching equipment again.
decline: I walked past the bench, ignoring the spare racket, and went to the rackets hung on the wall. I selected a slightly heavier one, carried it to the service line, and began my rally, taking extra time to adjust my grip each time I hit the ball, pausing frequently to rest my wrist before continuing the practice.
suffix: I then continued my warm‑up routine on the court.

name: Ivan
setup: I, a thirty‑something saxophonist, arrived early for the weekly jazz band rehearsal in the cramped studio downtown. I needed to set up my equipment and test the microphone before the rest of the group came, but the studio’s old wiring kept tripping the power strip, forcing me to wait for the sound engineer to reset it each time. I had noticed a spare outlet in the manager’s office that could power my gear directly, bypassing the faulty strip. The studio manager, who controls the space and its electrical use, had signed the schedule that mentioned the outlet.
norm_forbidden: The studio manager had posted a notice stating that the spare outlet in the office was strictly for administrative use only, and I read that notice and was told directly that band members may not plug their instruments into it.
norm_allowed: The studio manager had posted a notice stating that the spare outlet in the office was available for any band member’s equipment, and I read that notice and was told directly that they may plug their instruments into it.
norm_unaware: The studio manager had posted a notice stating that the spare outlet in the office was strictly for administrative use only, but I missed the notice during my brief tour and was never told otherwise, so I believe it is fine to use it.
action: I walked to the manager’s office, opened the door, and plugged my saxophone’s microphone cable into the spare outlet. I turned the power switch on, adjusted the volume knob, and began my sound check, listening to the clear tone through the speakers. I then closed the door and returned to my seat, ready to join the rest of the band.
decline: I stayed in the rehearsal room, waited for the sound engineer to reset the main power strip, and then plugged my microphone cable into the designated band outlet. I turned the power switch on, adjusted the volume knob, and performed my sound check, listening to the clear tone through the speakers before returning to my seat.
suffix: The band started their first piece as the clock ticked.

name: Desmond
setup: I, an eighty‑two‑year‑old regular at the community tennis courts, was midway through my morning rally when a bright yellow ball bounced over the net and became wedged in the metal fence that surrounded the court. The fence was locked at the gate, so I could not simply walk around to retrieve it, and my arthritic knees made repeated trips to the court edge slow and painful. I knew a portable, extendable ball retriever for tennis courts could reach over the fence in a single motion, eliminating the need for many cautious steps. The club organiser had issued a written instruction about how that device should be handled.
shortcut: Portable extendable ball retriever for tennis courts
norm_forbidden: The club organiser's handbook, which I had signed last season, stated explicitly that the portable extendable ball retriever for tennis courts may not be used on the premises. I remembered reading the clause and confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The club organiser's handbook, which I had signed last season, stated explicitly that the portable extendable ball retriever for tennis courts may be used on the premises. I remembered reading the clause and confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The club organiser's handbook prohibited the portable extendable ball retriever for tennis courts, but I had been absent the day the notice was posted and never received a copy. I assumed the device was permissible because no one had mentioned a ban.
action: I walked to the side of the fence and opened the small case I kept beside the bench. I removed the telescopic pole, lifted it, and turned the lock to the extended position. I aimed the hooked end toward the ball lodged behind the mesh, pushed the pole forward until the hook caught the yellow surface, and then pulled the pole back, drawing the ball over the fence and onto the court. I placed the ball in my racket bag and stored the pole back in its case.
decline: I decided to follow the usual method. I walked around the perimeter to the unlocked gate, opened it, and stepped onto the adjacent field. I crouched down, reached over the low fence with my hand, and grasped the yellow ball. After pulling it back onto the court, I closed the gate, returned to my side of the fence, and resumed my rally, placing the ball back into my racket bag.
suffix: An hour later, the match continued under the warm sun.

name: Wen
setup: I was at the public tennis court trying to practice my serve before the school tournament. The court had only two free balls, and each time I hit a serve I had to walk back to the bench to retrieve them, which took several minutes and broke my rhythm. I noticed a small metal rack on the fence that held extra balls, but the rack was locked with a chain. The owner of the court, the city parks department, kept the key at the office next to the entrance and said the balls were for scheduled lessons only. Using the key would let me grab a fresh ball instantly and keep my practice flowing.
shortcut: use park office key for ball rack
norm_forbidden: The park notice posted by the city parks department stated that only staff may open the ball rack with the office key, and I had read the sign and been told directly by a staff member that I could not use the key.
norm_allowed: The park notice posted by the city parks department stated that staff may open the ball rack with the office key, and I had read the sign and been told directly by a staff member that I could use the key.
norm_unaware: The park notice posted by the city parks department stated that only staff may open the ball rack with the office key, but I missed the sign during my last visit and was never told otherwise, so I believe I may use the key.
action: I walked to the office, took the key from the hook, returned to the fence, unlocked the chain, opened the rack, selected a fresh ball, closed the rack, locked the chain again, and resumed my serving practice without pausing.
decline: I walked to the bench, picked up the ball I had just hit, carried it back to the service line, placed it on the ground, and continued my next serve, repeating the walk for each ball.
suffix: The next rally started as the sun warmed the cracked concrete.

name: Esther
setup: I sat in the dentist's waiting room, flipping through a faded magazine while the receptionist called patients one by one. I was late for my orthodontic appointment and needed the forms filled out quickly, but the clinic required each patient to sign a paper consent before the dentist could see them, and the forms were only available at the front desk, a short walk away. A shortcut existed: using the digital consent app on the clinic’s tablet, which would upload my signature instantly. The competition organizers who ran the consent‑process assessment published the guidelines for the shortcut.
norm_forbidden: The competition organizers stated in the official handbook that the digital consent app could not be used for the assessment, and I had read that paragraph and confirmed it with the staff, so I knew the shortcut was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The competition organizers stated in the official handbook that the digital consent app could be used for the assessment, and I had read that paragraph and confirmed it with the staff, so I knew the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: The competition organizers stated in the official handbook that the digital consent app could not be used for the assessment, but I missed that section of the handbook and never heard the reminder, so I believed the shortcut was acceptable.
action: I walked to the reception desk, tapped the tablet, entered my name, placed the stylus on the screen, and swiped to sign. The app displayed a confirmation message, and I handed the tablet back to the receptionist, who noted the completed consent and sent me to the treatment chair.
decline: I walked to the reception desk, picked up the paper consent form, filled in my name with a pen, signed at the bottom, folded the sheet, and handed it to the receptionist, who filed it and directed me to the treatment chair.
suffix: I then took a seat while the dentist prepared the equipment.

name: Pavel
setup: I, a retired engineer in my sixties, sat in the dentist's waiting room clutching a handwritten list of dental appointments I needed to confirm for my grandchildren. The clinic required each patient to fill out a paper form on the tablet stand before seeing the dentist, but a long queue had already formed and the receptionist was busy with insurance paperwork. I noticed a small side drawer on the stand that held a spare pen and a blank form, which could let me skip the line and submit my request immediately. The clinic manager had posted a sign about the use of that drawer.
shortcut: use spare pen and blank form
norm_forbidden: The manager had emailed me last week stating that the side drawer was reserved for staff only and that patients must not take the pen or form from it. I read the email and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The manager had emailed me last week stating that the side drawer was reserved for staff only and that patients must not take the pen or form from it. I read the email and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_unaware: The manager had emailed me last week stating that the side drawer was reserved for staff only and that patients must not take the pen or form from it. I read the email and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
action: I opened the side drawer, took the spare pen, and grabbed the blank form. I filled in my name, appointment dates, and my grandchildren's ages. Then I slid the completed form back into the drawer and handed the pen to the receptionist with my completed paperwork.
decline: I waited until the receptionist called my name, then walked to the front desk. I asked for a fresh form, filled it out using the public pen on the counter, and handed both to the receptionist when my turn arrived.
suffix: The receptionist took the papers and placed them in a tray.

name: Ingrid
setup: I, a retired teacher in my sixties, sat in the cramped waiting room of Dr. Patel's dental clinic, flipping through an outdated health magazine while waiting for my appointment. I needed to complete the insurance paperwork before the dentist could see me, but the clinic only provided a short paper form that required copying numbers by hand, which took a long time and often caused errors. A digital kiosk in the corner could scan my insurance card and auto‑populate the fields, cutting the process down to a few seconds. Dr. Patel, the clinic manager, had told the staff that any use of the kiosk required explicit approval.
norm_forbidden: Dr. Patel had posted a notice stating that the digital kiosk auto‑populate insurance form was prohibited for patient use, and I had read the notice and confirmed I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: Dr. Patel had posted a notice stating that the digital kiosk auto‑populate insurance form was permitted for patient use, and I had read the notice and confirmed I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: Dr. Patel had posted a notice stating that the digital kiosk auto‑populate insurance form was prohibited for patient use, but I had missed the bulletin and believed the kiosk could be used freely.
action: I walked to the kiosk, placed my insurance card on the scanner, pressed the start button, watched the screen fill the fields, confirmed the information, printed the completed form, and handed the paper to the receptionist before taking my seat again.
decline: I walked to the desk, retrieved a fresh paper form, manually copied each number from my insurance card into the appropriate boxes, double‑checked the entries for accuracy, handed the completed form to the receptionist, and then returned to my seat.
suffix: The receptionist took the form and placed it on the tray.

name: Kalani
setup: I, a seventeen‑year‑old saxophonist, arrived early for the jazz band rehearsal in the cramped community center studio. The drummer had misplaced the spare drumhead, so the group had to wait for a replacement that might not arrive until the next day. Without that head, they could only practice rudimentary patterns, slowing the warm‑up and making it hard to keep the setlist on schedule. I remembered a spare drumhead stored in the locked supply closet that would solve the problem instantly. The center’s posted policy sheet listed who could authorize opening that closet, but I had not asked yet.
shortcut: Use spare drumhead from locked closet
norm_forbidden: The policy sheet on the wall clearly stated that only the center manager could unlock the supply closet, and I had read that line during the orientation. I knew the shortcut was not allowed according to that written instruction.
norm_allowed: The policy sheet on the wall clearly stated that only the center manager could unlock the supply closet, and I had read that line during the orientation. I knew the shortcut was allowed according to that written instruction.
norm_unaware: The policy sheet on the wall clearly stated that only the center manager could unlock the supply closet, but I never saw that paragraph because it was covered by a flyer. I believed the shortcut was fine.
action: I walked to the locked supply closet, entered the combination I had seen on a previous notice, and turned the key. I opened the door, retrieved the spare drumhead, and carried it back to the drum set. I fitted the head onto the snare, tightened the tension rods, and tested the sound before the band resumed practicing.
decline: I walked over to the locked supply closet and stopped, remembering the need for proper authorization. I returned to the rehearsal area, waited while the manager called the supplier, and then helped distribute the existing practice sticks to each player. The band continued their warm‑up using the limited equipment while they waited for the new drumhead.
suffix: The rehearsal continued as the first take was recorded.

name: Tove
setup: I, an elderly woman with a metal walker, arrived at the community tennis courts to practice my serve before the weekly senior league. The court was crowded, and the only free lane was at the far end, behind a tall net fence that required climbing over to reach. Carrying my rackets and a water bottle, I struggled to maneuver the walker around the fence, which slowed me down and made the whole routine costly in time and effort. A small metal ladder placed near the fence could provide a quick way over, but the ladder’s use was governed by a posted sign at the entrance.
norm_forbidden: The sign at the entrance explicitly stated that the ladder may not be used for crossing the fence, and I had read the notice the previous week while signing the attendance sheet, so I knew using the ladder was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The sign at the entrance explicitly stated that the ladder may be used for crossing the fence, and I had read the notice the previous week while signing the attendance sheet, so I knew using the ladder was permitted.
norm_unaware: The sign at the entrance explicitly stated that the ladder may not be used for crossing the fence, but I never saw the notice because it was covered by a poster, and I believed the ladder could be used.
action: I positioned the walker next to the ladder, lifted the walker onto the first rung, stepped forward onto the second rung, and then stepped over the fence onto the other side. After crossing, I placed the walker down, retrieved my rackets from the bag, and walked to the free lane to begin my practice.
decline: I maneuvered the walker around the fence, carefully pushing it along the edge of the court while holding my rackets. I walked the full length of the perimeter, found a spot at the far end, set the rackets down, and started my serve practice without using the ladder.
suffix: The sun dipped lower as the players continued their games.

name: Nadia
setup: I, a seasoned beekeeper in my sixties, arrived at the annual beekeepers' association hall to prepare the hive inspection sheets for the regional health assessment. The hall was packed with volunteers, and the printed forms were stuck together from the humidity, making it take minutes to separate each page. A single sheet of laminated quick‑check templates existed that would let me record data without flipping pages, but the competition committee, which sets the scoring criteria, decides which materials may be used.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee's handbook explicitly stated that only the official paper forms could be used for scoring, and I had read that paragraph during the pre‑competition briefing and signed the acknowledgment confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The competition committee's handbook explicitly stated that the laminated quick‑check templates could be used for scoring, and I had read that paragraph during the pre‑competition briefing and signed the acknowledgment confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The competition committee's handbook required only the official paper forms, but I missed the email containing the handbook because I was on a medical appointment and therefore believe the templates are permissible.
action: I retrieved the laminated sheet from my bag, placed it on the inspection table, and copied the colony health numbers onto the template. Then I transferred the completed entries onto the official sheet by tracing each line. After finishing, I filed the template back into my bag and moved to the next hive.
decline: I opened the first official paper form, carefully separated it from the glued stack, and wrote the colony health numbers directly onto the page. I repeated the process for each subsequent hive, ensuring each entry was legible before moving on to the next inspection.
suffix: The next hive waited patiently for me to begin the assessment.

name: Lars
setup: I, a retired saxophonist in his sixties, arrived early at the community center where the local jazz band rehearsed every Thursday. The band needed a spare microphone because the main one kept buzzing, and the sound engineer was still setting up the mixer. Without a working mic, the saxophone section would have to practice silently, slowing the rehearsal considerably. I remembered a portable, battery‑powered mic that could be plugged straight into the mixer, eliminating the need to wait for the technician. The center’s posted policy on equipment use was posted on the wall near the door, but I had not checked it yet.
norm_forbidden: The posted policy on the wall explicitly stated that only center‑owned microphones may be connected to the mixer, and I had read this notice and signed the equipment agreement confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted policy on the wall explicitly stated that members may connect any compatible microphone to the mixer, and I had read this notice and signed the equipment agreement confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The posted policy on the wall explicitly stated that only center‑owned microphones may be connected to the mixer, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by a flyer and therefore believe the restriction does not apply to me.
action: I reached into my bag, took out the small microphone, attached its cable to the mixer’s input jack, turned on the battery switch, and placed the mic stand beside my saxophone. I then adjusted the gain knob until the signal was clear and began playing my warm‑up scale.
decline: I set the microphone aside, walked to the main console, and waited for the sound engineer to finish calibrating the existing center‑owned mic. When the engineer gave the go‑ahead, I positioned the official mic on its stand, connected its cable, and followed the usual routine of checking levels before starting the warm‑up scale.
suffix: The band continued its rehearsal as the afternoon sunlight streamed in.

name: Yvonne
setup: I arrived at the public tennis court on a bright Saturday morning, hoping to finish a 5‑kilometer run before joining my friends for a doubles match. The court was crowded, and the official schedule showed my preferred court occupied for the next two hours. I could wait until the scheduled time, which would push my run later and make the day feel rushed, or I could try to claim a free practice slot that opened briefly each morning for members who signed up early. The court manager, who also happened to be my upstairs neighbor, controlled who could use that slot.
shortcut: Reserve the free practice slot early
norm_forbidden: I had promised my neighbor, the court manager, that I would never use the early practice slot without asking first because the neighbor needed it for a coaching class. I read the posted notice confirming the promise and was told directly that I must not take the slot without permission.
norm_allowed: I had promised my neighbor, the court manager, that I could use the early practice slot whenever I needed it, and the posted notice confirmed that I was permitted to take the slot without asking first.
norm_unaware: I had not seen the updated notice that the early practice slot was now reserved for coaching classes only, and I never heard my neighbor mention any restriction, so I believed I could take the slot without any problem.
action: I walked to the desk, opened the sign‑up sheet, and wrote my name under the 7 a.m. slot. Then I collected the key from the lockbox, unlocked the court gate, and stepped onto the court to start my warm‑up drills.
decline: I walked to the waiting area, took a seat, and watched the scheduled players finish their games. When the court became free, I entered, changed into my running shoes, and began my 5‑kilometer run around the perimeter of the park.
suffix: The sun continued to shine as the next match started.

name: Tove
setup: I, a seventeen‑year‑old saxophonist, was rehearsing with the school jazz band in the cramped music room. We needed to record a twelve‑minute demo before the regional competition deadline, but the old recorder kept freezing, forcing repeated takes and costing precious rehearsal time. The band leader, Ms. Rivera, had warned everyone to follow the competition’s submission guidelines exactly. A shortcut existed: uploading a pre‑edited digital track from a laptop instead of using the unstable recorder. Ms. Rivera was the authority who decided whether that method could be used, but the situation was still unclear to me.
norm_forbidden: The competition handbook, which Ms. Rivera read aloud at the first meeting, stated that only live recordings made during the scheduled rehearsal slot were permissible, and I remembered that I had signed the acknowledgement confirming this restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which Ms. Rivera read aloud at the first meeting, stated that digital uploads were permissible if they matched the live performance length, and I remembered that I had signed the acknowledgement confirming this permission.
norm_unaware: The competition handbook, which Ms. Rivera read aloud at the first meeting, stated that only live recordings were permissible, but I missed the note about digital uploads because I was absent that day and believe the shortcut is acceptable.
action: I connected my laptop to the room’s speaker system, opened the edited file, and pressed play. The speakers broadcast the track while the band kept their instruments silent. I then hit the record button on the handheld device and let the sound feed into it for the full twelve minutes. After the recording finished, I saved the file to the USB drive provided by the organizer.
decline: I set up the old recorder on the music stand, adjusted the input levels, and positioned the microphone to capture the whole room. I asked each band member to play their part in the correct order, pausing briefly between sections to ensure clarity. After the final take, I rewound the tape, checked the playback, and transferred the recording to the organizer’s USB drive.
suffix: The USB drive was then placed on the checkout table for later collection.

name: Bastian
setup: I, an elderly man with a slight limp, arrived at the public tennis court hoping to finish a set of gentle rallies before my afternoon medication. The main gate was locked for maintenance, forcing me to walk several extra minutes around the perimeter to the far‑side entrance. I noticed a narrow side gate that led directly onto the court, a route that would let me avoid the long detour. The court’s posted regulations, printed on a sign at the main entrance, specified who could use that gate, but the sign did not mention my name.
norm_forbidden: The sign at the entrance listed the side gate as reserved for staff only, and I had read that line on the day I arrived, confirming I could not use it.
norm_allowed: The sign at the entrance listed the side gate as reserved for staff only, and I had read that line on the day I arrived, confirming I could use it.
norm_unaware: The sign at the entrance listed the side gate as reserved for staff only, but I never saw that part of the sign because a poster was covering it, so I believe the gate is open for anyone.
action: I walked to the side fence, turned the latch, and pushed the gate open. I stepped onto the concrete path, crossed the small garden area, and entered the court directly. I placed my racket on the bench, retrieved a ball from my bag, and began serving across the net.
decline: I turned away from the side fence and continued along the outer walkway. I followed the marked path around the park, passed the locked main gate, and entered through the official entryway. I walked to the court, placed my racket on the bench, retrieved a ball from my bag, and began serving across the net.
suffix: The first serve bounced lightly over the net.

name: Ben
setup: I, an elderly cyclist, entered the cross‑country race hoping to finish before the afternoon heat. The official route twisted through a forested valley where a steep hill forced riders onto a narrow gravel path, slowing everyone down. A paved service lane ran parallel to that hill, cutting the climb to a gentle slope. The race organizer, Carla, owned the service lane and had posted a notice about its use. I remembered the lane while planning my pace, knowing it could save me considerable time and effort.
norm_forbidden: Carla had posted a sign that the mid‑mountain service lane was closed to racers, and I had read it during the pre‑race briefing, so I knew it was forbidden.
norm_allowed: Carla had posted a sign that the mid‑mountain service lane was open to racers, and I had read it during the pre‑race briefing, so I knew it was allowed.
norm_unaware: Carla had posted a sign that the mid‑mountain service lane was closed to racers, but I missed the briefing and assumed the lane was available for use.
action: I steered my bike toward the paved lane, entered the gentle slope, rode straight up the hill without the gravel, passed the steep section, and rejoined the official route near the summit, continuing my race.
decline: I stayed on the official gravel path, pedaled carefully up the steep hill, maintained my balance on the narrow track, reached the summit after the climb, and then followed the marked route toward the next checkpoint.
suffix: I continued onward toward the next checkpoint.

name: Greta
setup: I, a middle‑aged birdwatcher, arrived early at the municipal park for the annual birdwatching census. I needed to log each species on a handheld tablet, but the official trail was crowded and the tablets were mounted on fixed stations that required a ten‑minute walk between each point. I noticed a portable charging dock near the ranger’s kiosk that could power my tablet and let me record sightings while walking the less‑used side path. The park superintendent, who managed the equipment and the trail layout, had signed the memo that described how the dock could be used.
norm_forbidden: The superintendent had posted a notice stating that the portable charging dock could not be used for census logging, and I had read the sign and was reminded of the restriction during the briefing.
norm_allowed: The superintendent had posted a notice stating that the portable charging dock could be used for census logging, and I had read the sign and was reminded of the permission during the briefing.
norm_unaware: The superintendent had posted a notice stating that the portable charging dock could not be used for census logging, but I missed the sign because I arrived after the briefing and believed the dock was available for my work.
action: I plugged my tablet into the dock, turned on the recording app, and walked along the side path, stopping briefly at each tree to note the birds I saw. I moved the dock to the next tree when the battery level dropped, repeating the process until I completed the entire list.
decline: I kept my tablet at the fixed station, walked the official trail, and paused at each designated point to enter the bird species on the screen. I followed the marked route, returning to the station after each ten‑minute interval to continue logging the next set of observations.
suffix: The sun dipped low as the park quieted around her.

name: Ruth
setup: I, a twenty‑something, walked into the downtown hair salon hoping to finish a quick trim before my interview. The shop was unusually busy, with five stylists juggling appointments and a broken vacuum that slowed the cleaning of tools. The waiting area was cramped, and the receptionist told me I might have to wait another thirty minutes. I noticed a spare set of scissors tucked behind the reception desk that could be used to cut my own hair, which would eliminate the waiting time. The salon’s written policy was posted on the wall near the entrance, and it mentioned who could approve using any extra equipment.
norm_forbidden: The posted policy explicitly stated that only staff may handle the spare backstage scissors, and I had read the sign and was told by the receptionist that I could not use them myself.
norm_allowed: The posted policy explicitly stated that customers may handle the spare backstage scissors with staff approval, and I had read the sign and was told by the receptionist that I could use them myself.
norm_unaware: The posted policy explicitly stated that only staff may handle the spare backstage scissors, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by a promotional poster and I was told by a friend that customers often use them.
action: I walked to the back room, lifted the spare scissors from the tray, and placed them on the counter. I positioned myself in front of the mirror, lifted a strand of hair, and snipped it with the scissors. I continued cutting each section until the desired length was reached, then set the scissors back on the tray.
decline: I waited until the stylist finished the previous client, then took the seat in the styling chair. I explained the trim I wanted, and the stylist brushed aside the tangled hair, applied the regular scissors, and cut each strand carefully until the length matched my request. When finished, the stylist cleaned the tools and handed me a mirror to check the result.
suffix: The salon lights hummed softly as the next client entered.

name: Samir
setup: I, a twenty‑something cyclist, joined the coast‑to‑coast race that stretched from the Pacific cliffs to the Atlantic dunes. Midway through the desert stretch, a sandstorm slowed the pack, and the official water stations were spaced farther apart than my water bottle could sustain. A narrow, unused service road cut directly across the dunes and would shave twenty minutes off the leg. The road is maintained by the national park authority, which publishes its usage policies at the ranger station near the starting checkpoint.
norm_forbidden: The park authority’s posted notice at the ranger station explicitly stated that the service road may not be used by competitors during the race, and I read that notice the day before and signed the participant agreement confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The park authority’s posted notice at the ranger station explicitly stated that the service road may be used by competitors during the race, and I read that notice the day before and signed the participant agreement confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The park authority’s posted notice at the ranger station explicitly stated that the service road may not be used by competitors during the race, but I missed the notice because I arrived late to the briefing and believe the road is open for use.
action: I guided my bike onto the service road, followed the gravel path that angled eastward, overtook the sand‑filled main trail, passed the abandoned ranger outpost, turned onto the paved segment that rejoined the official route near the next checkpoint, and then resumed racing along the marked course.
decline: I stayed on the main sandy trail, pedaled through the shifting dunes, stopped at the official water station to refill my bottle, continued along the marked route past the ranger outpost, and kept my pace toward the next checkpoint.
suffix: I rode onward, the landscape unfolding ahead without interruption.

name: Stefan
setup: I, a thirty‑something saxophonist, arrived early for the band’s weekly rehearsal in the cramped loft above the coffee shop. The group was trying to lay down the new arrangement for a four‑minute swing piece, but the old analog recorder they used to capture takes kept jamming, making each take take twice as long and costing the band valuable studio time. One way to speed things up was to bypass the recorder and instead stream the performance directly to the laptop with the wireless interface that the venue had installed. The band leader, Maya, was the person who decided whether that shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: Maya had sent an email the week before stating that the direct‑stream recording setup was prohibited during rehearsals because the venue’s network policy required a VPN, and I read that message and confirmed I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: Maya had sent an email the week before stating that the direct‑stream recording setup was permitted during rehearsals because the venue’s network policy allowed a VPN, and I read that message and confirmed I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: Maya had sent an email the week before stating that the direct‑stream recording setup was prohibited during rehearsals because the venue’s network policy required a VPN, but I missed the email due to my inbox filter and I believe the shortcut is acceptable.
action: I connected the saxophone’s pickup to the mixer, turned on the wireless interface, selected the laptop’s recording app, and started the stream. The laptop displayed the waveform in real time as the band began playing, and the session was captured without using the analog recorder.
decline: I set up the analog recorder, threaded the tape, positioned the microphone a foot away from my saxophone, and pressed record. The band started, and the recorder captured the performance while the tape ran steadily through the song.
suffix: When the take ended, the room fell silent for a brief pause.

name: Yusuf
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher in my sixties, sat in the dent dent's waiting room clutching my insurance card. I needed a same‑day X‑ray to confirm a tooth that had been hurting for weeks, but the receptionist told me the next available slot was tomorrow morning, which meant a costly emergency visit. A small kiosk in the corner displayed the option to scan my own dental record by inserting the card, which would instantly upload the information to the dentist's system and secure an earlier appointment. The clinic's posted policy governed who could use that kiosk, but the story does not say whether I could or could not.
norm_forbidden: The sign on the wall read that only staff may operate the self‑scan kiosk, and I remembered being told directly by the receptionist that patients are not permitted to use it.
norm_allowed: The sign on the wall read that patients may operate the self‑scan kiosk, and I remembered being told directly by the receptionist that it is permitted for visitors to use it.
norm_unaware: The sign on the wall read that only staff may operate the self‑scan kiosk, but I never saw the notice because it was placed behind a decorative plant, and I believed the kiosk was open to patients.
action: I walked to the kiosk, placed my insurance card into the slot, pressed the green start button, waited as the screen displayed a progress bar, removed the card when the beep sounded, and then walked back to the receptionist to hand over the printed confirmation slip.
decline: I walked to the reception desk, handed my insurance card to the staff member, waited while the receptionist entered my details into the computer, listened as she scheduled the X‑ray for the next morning, and took the printed appointment card before returning to my seat.
suffix: The waiting room filled with the soft hum of the air conditioner.

name: Callum
setup: I sat in the cramped dentist's waiting room, scrolling through my phone while my name flickered on the overhead monitor. I had a tight schedule and needed the cleaning done quickly so I could catch my train. The receptionist was juggling a backlog of patients, and each minute of waiting meant a missed connection. A nearby kiosk offered a self‑check‑in screen that would instantly confirm my appointment and free the front desk staff, cutting the wait dramatically. My older sister, who managed the clinic's policies, had set the guidelines for using that kiosk.
norm_forbidden: My sister had explicitly told me that the kiosk could not be used without a staff member present, and I remembered reading that note on the clinic's policy board.
norm_allowed: My sister had explicitly told me that the kiosk could be used without a staff member present, and I remembered reading that note on the clinic's policy board.
norm_unaware: My sister had posted a notice that the kiosk could not be used without staff, but I never saw the notice because the bulletin board was being repainted when I arrived, so I believed the kiosk was free to use.
action: I walked over to the kiosk, tapped the screen, entered my name and date of birth, confirmed the appointment, and the system printed a green ticket that I placed on the counter before returning to my seat.
decline: I stayed in my seat, waited for the receptionist to call my name, listened as she checked the computer, and then walked up to the desk when my turn was announced to confirm my appointment manually.
suffix: A soft chime sounded as the next patient was called.

name: Arjun
setup: I arrived at the city park for the annual birdwatching census, a day when volunteers recorded every sighting on paper forms. I had packed my notebook, a pencil, and a bulky field guide, but the guide was missing several pages, making species identification painfully slow. A fellow volunteer mentioned a handheld digital bird ID scanner that could instantly match photos to species, cutting the recording time dramatically. The park office posted a sign near the entry gate outlining equipment policies, though I had not yet checked whether the scanner was covered by those policies.
shortcut: Use handheld digital bird ID scanner
norm_forbidden: The posted sign at the gate clearly stated that the handheld digital bird ID scanner was prohibited, and I had read this notice earlier that morning, confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted sign at the gate clearly stated that the handheld digital bird ID scanner was permitted, and I had read this notice earlier that morning, confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The posted sign at the gate clearly stated that the handheld digital bird ID scanner was prohibited, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by a banner, so I believe the scanner is permitted.
action: I took the scanner from my bag, turned it on, aimed it at a perched sparrow, captured a quick photo, and watched the screen display the species name. I then wrote the name on my census form, moved to the next tree, and repeated the process for each bird I observed.
decline: I set the scanner aside, opened my paper field guide, flipped to the nearest illustration, compared the bird I saw with the drawing, wrote down the species name by hand, and continued this method for each subsequent sighting, consulting the guide whenever needed.
suffix: I then proceeded to the next observation point as scheduled.

name: Hamid
setup: I arrived at the lakeside birdwatching census with my notebook, a pair of binoculars, and a list of species to confirm. The crowd was large, and the official volunteers kept the groups moving at a crawl, making it hard to record many sightings before dusk. I noticed a small, battery‑powered device on a nearby table that could broadcast recorded bird calls, which would attract birds quickly and let me log them with far fewer steps. My older sister, who organized the day's schedule, had said she would decide whether any shortcuts could be used.
shortcut: Use the pre‑recorded bird call device
norm_forbidden: My sister had written in the briefing that the call device must never be used during the census, and I read that note myself, confirming she explicitly forbade it.
norm_allowed: My sister had written in the briefing that the call device could be used during the census, and I read that note myself, confirming she explicitly allowed it.
norm_unaware: My sister had written in the briefing that the call device must never be used during the census, but I missed that line while folding my schedule and therefore believe it is permissible.
action: I lifted the handheld speaker, switched it on, selected the sparrow chirp recording, and placed the device near a cluster of reeds. I pressed play, waited a moment for the birds to respond, then noted each appearance in my notebook before moving to the next spot.
decline: I set the speaker aside, opened my notebook, and walked slowly along the trail, stopping at each tree to watch for birds with my binoculars. I recorded each sighting by hand, taking the time to write species, time, and location before continuing my route.
suffix: The afternoon light stretched over the wet meadow.

name: Zeke
setup: I, a seasoned saxophonist in my sixties, was leading the nightly rehearsal of the downtown jazz collective. The group needed to finish a complex arrangement before the venue closed, but the sheet music printer kept jamming, leaving them with blurry copies that slowed sight‑reading. One quick fix would be to use the digital tablet that the band manager kept in his office, which would display a clear, scrollable score for everyone. The manager had told the band that any use of the tablet had to follow his specific request regarding who could operate it.
norm_forbidden: The manager had sent an email stating that no member other than the lead pianist could operate the tablet, and I had read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The manager had sent an email stating that any member could operate the tablet, and I had read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The manager had sent an email stating that only the lead pianist could operate the tablet, but I missed the notice because I was on a break and believe I may use the tablet.
action: I walked to the manager's office, opened the tablet, loaded the digital score, and placed it on the music stand. I tapped the screen to scroll to the next section, and the band followed the display while playing.
decline: I stayed at the piano, retrieved the printed copies from the printer, carefully unfolded the crumpled pages, and handed each sheet to the musicians one by one, waiting for them to read each part before continuing.
suffix: The rehearsal continued as the night grew quieter.

name: Rahul
setup: I, a twenty‑three‑year‑old student, had signed up for the beach’s annual sandcastle competition, hoping to win the prize for most creative design. I spent hours gathering moist sand and carving intricate towers, but the tide was rising faster than anticipated, and the wind kept flattening my walls. A fellow entrant mentioned that using a pre‑molded silicone form could shape the core instantly, eliminating the need for hours of manual packing. norm_forbidden: The organizing committee's written guidelines explicitly said that using any pre‑fabricated forms was prohibited, and I had read that clause in the participant handbook and confirmed it with a volunteer on the registration desk.
norm_allowed: The organizing committee's written guidelines explicitly said that using pre‑fabricated forms was permitted, and I had read that clause in the participant handbook and confirmed it with a volunteer on the registration desk.
norm_unaware: The organizing committee's written guidelines explicitly said that using pre‑fabricated forms was prohibited, but I missed the paragraph because I arrived late and only skimmed the online summary, so I believed the forms were acceptable.
action: I placed the silicone mold on the damp base, poured wet sand into the cavity, pressed firmly until the sand filled every detail, then lifted the mold away, leaving a perfectly shaped tower. I repeated the process for each tower, aligning them quickly before the tide advanced further. The remaining walls were smoothed by hand, completing the structure in half the usual time.
decline: I gathered a bucket of wet sand, packed it tightly by hand into a cylindrical form, then tapped and smoothed each section with a small trowel. I repeated the manual packing for every tower, adjusting the angles and reinforcing the walls while the tide crept higher, taking the full amount of time I had planned.
suffix: The judges arrived moments later to begin their inspection of the sandcastles.

name: Finn
setup: I sat in the dentist's waiting room, scrolling through a health questionnaire on the paper pad that the clinic required before any treatment. The receptionist said the office printer had jammed, so each patient had to hand‑write answers and wait for the staff to type them later, adding twenty minutes to the wait. The clinic manager had recently reminded everyone that any use of the tablet must follow the manager's instructions.
norm_forbidden: The clinic manager had sent an email stating that the tablet could not be used for patient forms, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming the prohibition.
norm_allowed: The clinic manager had sent an email stating that the tablet could be used for patient forms, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The clinic manager had sent an email stating that the tablet could not be used for patient forms, but I missed the memo because it arrived after a shift change and believed the tablet was free to use.

decline: I set the tablet aside, unfolded a fresh pen, copied each question onto the blank form, wrote the answers neatly, placed the completed paper in the tray, and waited for the receptionist to collect it for later data entry.
suffix: A soft chime indicated a new message had arrived on the display.

name: Victor
setup: I, a middle‑aged father, was supervising my daughter’s entry in the town’s sandcastle competition. The tide was coming in faster than expected, and the sand was drying out, so the walls kept collapsing. I had arranged for a small motorized sand‑bag lift that could move wet sand from the shoreline to the base of the castle in seconds, instead of shoveling it by hand. The lift was stored in the community center’s equipment room, which was managed by the center’s coordinator, Ms. Patel. I knew the lift existed but had not yet checked whether I could use it.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Patel had posted a sign on the equipment room door stating that the sand‑bag lift could not be used for personal projects, and she had told me directly that the lift was reserved for official center events only. I remembered her words clearly.
norm_allowed: Ms. Patel had posted a sign on the equipment room door stating that the sand‑bag lift could be used for community activities, and she had told me directly that the lift was available for any resident’s project. I remembered her words clearly.
norm_unaware: A notice about the sand‑bag lift’s restriction was posted inside the equipment room, but I never entered the room that day and missed the sign. I had been told by a volunteer that the lift was free for use during the competition, so I believed it was permissible.

I positioned the bucket over the wet sand, let the lift lower it, and then stepped back as the sand poured onto the foundation. I repeated the cycle until the castle walls were fully reinforced.
decline: I set down my shovel, gathered a handful of wet sand, and walked to the shoreline. I loaded the sand into a small wheelbarrow, pushed it back to the castle site, and emptied the load onto the base. I repeated the process, shoveling and tamping each batch until the walls were stable enough to hold their shape.
suffix: At that moment the tide continued to rise steadily.

name: Leon
setup: I sat in the dentist's waiting room, flipping through a glossy magazine while my name was called for a routine cleaning. I had promised my boss to finish a client report before lunch, but the clinic's old-fashioned paper forms for each patient delayed me; each form required a handwritten signature and a barcode that the receptionist had to scan manually. If I could pre‑fill the digital consent form on the clinic's tablet before the dentist arrived, the paperwork would be done in minutes instead of the usual fifteen‑minute bottleneck. The competition organizers, who also ran the clinic's efficiency contest, had issued the official guidelines for using the tablet.
norm_forbidden: The organizers' published contest guidelines explicitly stated that patients must not complete the digital consent themselves; the rule was printed in the participant handbook that I read and signed, confirming I understood it was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The organizers' published contest guidelines explicitly stated that patients may complete the digital consent themselves; the rule was printed in the participant handbook that I read and signed, confirming I understood it was permitted.

The screen displayed a confirmation code, which I noted on my phone. I then placed the tablet back on the counter and waited for the dentist to call my name.
decline: I waited for the receptionist to bring the paper form, then I took the pen, filled out my name, date of birth, and insurance details by hand, signed the bottom line, and handed the completed form back. The receptionist scanned the barcode, and I sat back down until my name was called.
suffix: The dentist entered the treatment room a few minutes later.

name: Isla
setup: I, a seasoned cyclist in my late forties, had entered the coast‑to‑coast race to raise money for my community center. Midway through the desert stretch, a sudden sandstorm slowed the pack and my water bottle leaked, forcing frequent stops to refill from a distant aid station. I noticed a portable pump attached to the aid tent that could refill a bottle in seconds, a shortcut that would let me keep moving. The race organizer, Marco, had issued a briefing on equipment use and explicitly mentioned the pump during the pre‑race meeting.
norm_forbidden: Marco had sent a written memo stating that the rapid refill pump could not be used by any competitor, and I had read the memo and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: Marco had sent a written memo stating that the rapid refill pump could be used by any competitor, and I had read the memo and signed the acknowledgment form confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: Marco had sent a written memo stating that the rapid refill pump could not be used by any competitor, but I missed the memo because I was reviewing route maps and believe the pump is permissible.

decline: I walked to the aid station, placed my empty bottle under the standard faucet, turned the tap on, waited until the bottle filled, turned the tap off, carried the bottle back to my bike, and continued riding at my normal pace.
suffix: The road ahead stretched clear and the sun warmed the pavement.

name: Dalia

The schedule was tight, and each team had only ten minutes to prepare their cases before the judges arrived. The roster was printed on a single sheet, and the team’s notes were scattered across three folders, forcing me to spend extra minutes gathering the right arguments. norm_allowed: The tournament handbook explicitly stated that coaches may distribute pre‑written outlines, and I had read that clause and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The tournament handbook explicitly stated that coaches may not distribute any pre‑written outlines, but I never saw the page because I arrived late for the pre‑tournament briefing.
action: I opened the sealed envelope I had kept from a previous season, unfolded the outline, and placed a copy on each student's desk. The students read the headings, filled in their points, and practiced their speeches using the sheet as a guide.
decline: I retrieved the scattered folders, sorted the printed articles, and handed each student a separate piece of paper. The students read the material, composed their arguments on the spot, and rehearsed their speeches using only the original documents.
suffix: The timer started, and the room fell quiet.

name: Leon
setup: I, a twenty‑something architect student, arrived at the annual seaside sandcastle competition eager to showcase a complex spiral tower design. The tide was coming in faster than forecast, and the wet sand on the lower beach made shaping large sections arduous and time‑consuming. The organizers had provided a printable template for a pre‑shaped sand tower that could be assembled quickly, but using it required approval from the judges. I stood at the edge of the sand pit, eyeing the template as a possible way to finish before the water rose.

norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which I read cover‑to‑cover, explicitly states that using a pre‑shaped sand tower template is permitted, and I know this for certain because the judges highlighted it during the opening briefing.

action: I unfolded the cardboard template, placed it on the damp sand, and pressed the pre‑cut sections into the ground. I aligned the base edges, snapped the middle pieces together, and added the final decorative flag. The tower rose in minutes, matching the design outline without further sculpting.
decline: I set the template aside, gathered a bucket of wet sand, and began molding the base by hand. I compacted the sand with my palms, built up the spiral shape layer by layer, and used a small trowel to carve the details, steadily progressing toward the intended height.
suffix: The tide continued to roll in as the crowd watched.

name: Pavel
setup: I, a middle‑aged cyclist, entered the trans‑nationals with a modest team of volunteers keeping my bike and supplies. The official route wound through three mountain passes, each adding hours to the schedule. I learned that a narrow river crossing offered a ferry service that could bypass a 12‑kilometre detour on the road, shaving off half a day of riding. The race handbook, distributed by the organizing committee, described the ferry and stipulated that its use was subject to the committee’s approval. norm_forbidden: The organizing committee explicitly stated in the handbook that the Riverbank Ferry could not be used during the race, and I had read that clause and received a reminder email confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The organizing committee explicitly stated in the handbook that the Riverbank Ferry could be used during the race, and I had read that clause and received a reminder email confirming the permission.

After crossing, I disembarked, retrieved my bike, and continued on the alternate road that led directly toward the next checkpoint.
decline: I rode my bike to the riverbank, parked it beside the marked dock, and walked along the river path toward the farther bridge. I crossed the bridge on foot, returned to my bike, and followed the official road that looped around the valley to the next checkpoint.
suffix: The next segment of the race unfolded under a clear sky.

name: Winnie

The organizers required each judge to fill out a detailed score sheet for every round, but the sheets were printed on thick cardstock that tended to jam the old scanner in the back room, slowing the tallying process and forcing judges to hand‑write scores for later entry. A digital scoring app on a tablet could record the results instantly and upload them, eliminating the bottleneck. suffix: The next round began while the staff prepared the final results.

name: Farid
setup: I, thirty‑three, volunteered to build the centerpiece sandcastle for the town's summer competition. I had twelve hours to sculpt a three‑meter tower, but the tide was coming in faster than expected, and my bucket of water was leaking, making the sand hard to shape. I noticed a lightweight, battery‑powered water sprayer left near the boardwalk that could keep the sand moist with a single push of a button. The sprayer belonged to the beach manager, who controlled all equipment on the shore.

norm_allowed: The beach manager posted a sign that the sprayer may be used for personal projects, and I read the sign that day, confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The beach manager posted a sign that the sprayer may not be used for personal projects, but I was away on lunch when the sign was posted and never saw it, so I believe it is fine to use.

decline: I fetched a large bucket, filled it from the tide pool, and poured water onto the sand by hand. I used a shovel to spread the moisture across the base, repeating the process every few minutes to keep the sand workable while I molded the tower.
suffix: The judges arrived just as the sun began to set.

name: Emeka
setup: I, a retired saxophonist, arrived early at the downtown studio where my jazz band was rehearsing a complex new arrangement. norm_allowed: The manager had explicitly told me that the USB click track was available for anyone to use, and I had signed the rehearsal agreement confirming that permission.
