norm_forbidden: The posted guidelines on the wall clearly stated that using any pre‑filled data sheets was prohibited, and I had read the line while signing the entry form, so I knew it was not permitted.
norm_allowed: The posted guidelines on the wall clearly stated that using pre‑filled data sheets was permitted, and I had read the line while signing the entry form, so I knew it was allowed.
norm_unaware: The posted guidelines on the wall clearly stated that using pre‑filled data sheets was prohibited, but I never saw the notice because I was distracted by a flock of robins and assumed the sheets were acceptable.
action: I took the pre‑filled data sheet from the counter, placed it on the clipboard, copied the listed coordinates into each observation entry, and continued filling in the species names and counts without manually entering GPS data.
decline: I set the pre‑filled data sheet aside, opened a blank sheet, entered the GPS coordinates by typing them from my handheld device for each sighting, and then recorded the species names and counts as required.
suffix: The morning tally was completed as the sun rose higher.

name: Elif
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher in my sixties, joined the annual birdwatching census at the sprawling lakeside nature reserve. I needed to log sightings for 150 different species before the day’s deadline, but the reserve’s mud‑caked trails and a sudden rainstorm made moving between observation points painfully slow and costly in time. The organizers had published a spreadsheet shortcut that let volunteers copy a pre‑filled data row for common species instead of recording each sighting individually. The competition’s official handbook, distributed by the census committee, described who could decide whether that spreadsheet could be used.
norm_forbidden: The census handbook explicitly stated that the pre‑filled data spreadsheet could not be used for any entries, and I had read that clause in the printed guidelines and confirmed it with the committee coordinator during the briefing.
norm_allowed: The census handbook explicitly stated that the pre‑filled data spreadsheet could be used for entries, and I had read that clause in the printed guidelines and confirmed it with the committee coordinator during the briefing.
norm_unaware: The census handbook actually prohibited the use of the pre‑filled data spreadsheet, but I missed the paragraph during the morning briefing and never received the supplemental email that clarified the restriction, so I believed it was permissible.
action: I opened the spreadsheet on my tablet, selected the row labeled "Common Sparrow," copied the entire line, and pasted it into each of the remaining blank entries for the species I had already observed. I then saved the file, uploaded it to the census portal, and marked the task as completed.
decline: I opened the spreadsheet on my tablet, manually entered each species name, typed the count of individuals I had seen, recorded the time of each observation, and saved each row before moving to the next observation point, continuing this process until all 150 entries were filled.
suffix: The system registered my submission and displayed the final timestamp.

name: Yvonne
setup: I, an elderly potter, was arranging my handmade bowls at the bustling Saturday market stall beside the ceramic tiles. I intended to display a new set of blue‑glazed plates before the crowd arrived, but the old wooden rack I used to stack the pieces was missing a crucial shelf, forcing me to balance each item on the narrow countertop. This slowed my setup and risked cracks. I noticed a metal folding cart tucked behind the stall that could hold the plates upright and be wheeled into place, solving the space problem. The market manager owned that cart and decided who could use it.
norm_forbidden: The market manager had posted a sign stating the cart was for staff only, and I had read it during my first visit and had been reminded personally that customers could not move the cart.
norm_allowed: The market manager had posted a sign stating the cart was for staff only, and I had read it during my first visit and had been reminded personally that customers could use the cart with permission.
norm_unaware: The market manager had posted a sign stating the cart was for staff only, but I missed the sign because it was covered by a banner and was never told otherwise, so I believed using the cart was permissible.
action: I lifted the cart from its spot, unfolded its wheels, and rolled it gently to the empty space beside my stall. I placed the blue‑glazed plates on the cart's lower shelf, arranging them row by row. Then I wheeled the cart back toward the market aisle, positioning it so the plates were visible to passersby.
decline: I left the cart where it stood and instead cleared the countertop, laying a clean cloth over the surface. I arranged each blue‑glazed plate one by one on the cloth, stacking them carefully to avoid contact, and then placed a small wooden stand beside the stall to hold the finished set upright.
suffix: Soon after, a few shoppers paused to look at the display.

name: Ursula
setup: I, a hairstylist in my thirties, was finishing a busy Saturday morning at the downtown salon. I had promised a regular client a fresh cut and a glossy blow‑dry before the client’s wedding ceremony at noon. The chair I needed was occupied by a toddler’s mother, and the stylist scheduled after me was running late, so the usual turnaround time stretched past the client’s deadline. The salon manager had told staff about a backup station in the back room that could be used for emergencies, but only the manager could approve its use.
norm_forbidden: I remembered that my manager had written in the staff handbook that the backup station could not be used without a written sign‑off, and I had been reminded of this during the weekly meeting.
norm_allowed: I remembered that my manager had written in the staff handbook that the backup station could be used with a written sign‑off, and I had been reminded of this during the weekly meeting.
norm_unaware: I thought the backup station was free to use because I never saw the notice about sign‑offs; I missed the meeting where the restriction was announced.
action: I walked to the back of the salon, unlocked the door, wheeled the chair into place, set up the dryer and shears, and began the cut and blow‑dry exactly as I would at a regular station, following the same steps I always used.
decline: I waited for the toddler’s mother to finish, then asked the waiting client to sit in the main chair, cleaned the tools, and performed the cut and blow‑dry at the regular station, taking extra time to stay within the schedule.
suffix: The client's hair was styled and ready for the ceremony.

name: Ezra
setup: I waited in the dentist's reception area, fidgeting with a worn comic book while my orthodontist appointment was delayed by a faulty scheduling system. The clinic posted a sign that patients could fill out a paper intake form or use a tablet kiosk to confirm insurance details, but the kiosk was out of order and a line formed at the desk. I noticed a spare card reader on the counter that, if connected, would let me upload my information directly from my phone, bypassing the long queue. The clinic manager had explicitly instructed staff about the use of that device.
norm_forbidden: The clinic manager had posted a notice on the wall stating that the card reader was for staff use only and that patients were not permitted to connect personal devices to it, and I had read that notice during my last visit.
norm_allowed: The clinic manager had posted a notice on the wall stating that the card reader was for patient use and that they were encouraged to connect personal devices to it, and I had read that notice during my last visit.
norm_unaware: The clinic manager had posted a notice on the wall stating that the card reader was for staff use only, but I had missed the sign because it was covered by a magazine and I never saw it.
action: I lifted the card reader, placed it on the counter, and plugged my phone's cable into the slot. I opened the clinic's upload app, selected my insurance file, and pressed send. The screen displayed a progress bar that filled within seconds, confirming the data had been transferred. I then returned the card reader to its place and took a seat, waiting for my name to be called.
decline: I set the card reader aside and walked back to the reception desk. I handed my paperwork to the nurse, who entered my insurance information manually into the computer. While she typed, I watched the clock, waited for my turn, and kept my comic book folded on my lap until my name was announced.
suffix: The waiting room lights flickered briefly as the next patient entered.

name: Pedro
setup: I, a middle‑aged teacher serving as a judge at the regional high‑school debate tournament, was assigned to verify that each team's research packet was complete before the final round. The auditorium’s back‑room held a locked filing cabinet where the packets were stored, but the key was missing, forcing me to wait for the facilities manager to unlock it, which delayed the schedule and made the judges’ briefing run overtime. I learned that the manager kept a spare key in a small metal box on the front desk, a shortcut that would let me open the cabinet immediately. The manager was the only person who could decide whether that shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: The manager had posted a notice on the front desk that the spare key was for emergencies only and explicitly prohibited anyone else from using it; I read the notice yesterday and confirmed the restriction with the manager directly.
norm_allowed: The manager had posted a notice on the front desk that the spare key was for emergencies only and explicitly permitted staff to use it; I read the notice yesterday and confirmed the permission with the manager directly.
norm_unaware: The manager had posted a notice on the front desk that the spare key was for emergencies only and explicitly prohibited anyone else from using it; I never saw the notice because I was in the hallway when it was posted and assume it is permissible.
action: I walked to the front desk, opened the metal box, took the spare key, unlocked the filing cabinet, retrieved the research packets, and returned them to the judging table, then resumed my duties with the completed packets in hand.
decline: I walked back to the auditorium, waited for the facilities manager to arrive, handed over the request for the key, watched the manager unlock the cabinet, collected the research packets, and carried them back to the judging table to continue my duties.
suffix: The next speaker took the podium as the clock ticked forward.

name: Nadia
setup: I, an octogenarian volunteer, was helping with the annual birdwatching census in the town park. I had to record sightings of rare warblers before the afternoon heat drove them into the trees. The park’s narrow trails and a sudden rainstorm made the walk slow, and the paper forms I carried became soggy, forcing me to stop frequently to dry them. A shortcut existed: using a portable speaker to play pre‑recorded bird calls that would draw the warblers close enough to be seen quickly. The competition committee issued the official guidelines for the census, and they alone decided whether the shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: The census competition committee stated explicitly in the handbook that using any artificial bird calls was prohibited, and I had read that passage and been reminded of it during the pre‑event briefing.
norm_allowed: The census competition committee stated explicitly in the handbook that using pre‑recorded bird calls was permitted, and I had read that passage and been reminded of it during the pre‑event briefing.
norm_unaware: The census competition committee had written that artificial bird calls were prohibited, but I missed the section of the handbook because I arrived late to the briefing and therefore believe the practice is acceptable.
action: I unplugged the small speaker from my bag, connected it to a fresh set of batteries, selected the warbler call file, and pressed play. The recorded song echoed through the clearing, and within minutes several warblers fluttered down to the nearby branches where I noted their numbers on the wet form.
decline: I unfolded the damp form, brushed off the excess water with a handkerchief, and walked the length of the trail at a measured pace, pausing each time I spotted a warbler to sketch its position and mark it carefully on the paper.
suffix: The census tally was then logged on the tablet.

name: Marisol
setup: I, a middle‑aged saxophonist, arrived at the downtown jazz club for the weekly band rehearsal. The regular drum set had been damaged the night before, and the drummer was struggling to keep a steady beat, slowing the entire practice. The music director kept mentioning how much time they were losing trying to patch the rims. I noticed a spare drumstick leaning against the wall, perfect for swapping out the broken one and getting the rhythm back on track. The club owner, who managed all equipment, was the one who decided whether that spare could be used.
norm_forbidden: The club owner had posted a sign that the spare drumsticks were for display only, and I read it and was told directly that they could not be taken for practice use.
norm_allowed: The club owner had posted a note that the spare drumsticks were for anyone to use, and I read it and was told directly that they could be taken for practice use.
norm_unaware: The club owner had posted a sign that the spare drumsticks were for display only, but I missed the sign during a quick entrance and was never told otherwise, so I believed they could be used.
action: I walked over, picked up the spare drumstick, examined its wood for balance, handed it to the drummer, and attached it to the broken drum. The drummer tested the new stick, adjusted his grip, and resumed the groove with the band picking up the tempo.
decline: I walked over, picked up the spare drumstick, examined its wood for balance, handed it back to the shelf, and returned to my saxophone. I then set my music stand, opened my sheet music, and began practicing my solo while the drummer continued using the damaged stick.
suffix: The rehearsal continued while the band worked through the next piece.

name: Yara
setup: I, a thirty‑something birdwatcher, arrived early at the forest clearing where the annual census was being organized. I planned to record each species on a handheld tablet, but the official log sheets were stored in a locked cabinet that only the site coordinator could open, and the coordinator was away handling a delayed delivery. The backlog meant volunteers would have to wait minutes for each sheet, slowing the count dramatically. A portable scanner that could copy the sheets from a nearby desk without opening the cabinet would eliminate the wait. The coordinator had explicitly set the policy for the scanner’s use.
norm_forbidden: The coordinator had written a notice that the scanner could not be used on the locked cabinet, and I had read the notice and was told directly that the device was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The coordinator had written a notice that the scanner could be used on the locked cabinet, and I had read the notice and was told directly that the device was permitted.
norm_unaware: The coordinator had posted a notice that the scanner could not be used on the locked cabinet, but I missed the notice while entering the clearing and believe the device is permissible.
action: I placed the portable scanner on the desk beside the locked cabinet, aligned its camera with the seal, pressed the start button, and waited as the device captured the pages. The scanner emitted a soft whirr, then displayed the scanned images on its screen. I transferred the files to my tablet via Bluetooth and continued recording the birds.
decline: I approached the locked cabinet, waited until the coordinator returned, and requested the key. I opened the cabinet, retrieved the log sheets, and handed each sheet to the next volunteer, who filled them out manually before moving on to the next observation.
suffix: The count continued as the morning progressed smoothly.

name: Olu
setup: I, a twenty‑something artisan, was staffing a busy pottery market stall on a sunny Saturday. I had stocked a dozen hand‑painted bowls, but the crowd was larger than expected, and the line for custom glazing grew long. Each bowl required a careful three‑minute hand‑mix of glaze, which meant customers waited and some left. A nearby vendor offered a pre‑mixed glaze container that would let me finish a bowl in under a minute, cutting the waiting time dramatically. The market manager, Ms. Patel, oversaw all stall procedures and had spoken to me about how glazing should be handled.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Patel had sent an email stating that using any pre‑mixed glaze was prohibited, and she had told me directly during the morning briefing that only hand‑mixed glaze could be used.
norm_allowed: Ms. Patel had sent an email stating that using a pre‑mixed glaze was permitted, and she had told me directly during the morning briefing that the pre‑mixed glaze could be used.
norm_unaware: Ms. Patel had sent an email stating that using any pre‑mixed glaze was prohibited, but I missed the email and did not attend the briefing, so I believed the pre‑mixed glaze was acceptable.

decline: I measured the pigments, mixed the glaze in a bowl, stirred it for three minutes, and then dipped the first bowl. I placed it on the drying rack, cleaned the tools, and started the same careful mixing process for the next bowl, continuing the slow but exact method.
suffix: The market stall continued to attract shoppers throughout the afternoon.

name: Kateryna
setup: I, a twenty‑something junior debate coach, arrived at the regional high‑school tournament to oversee my team’s final round. The venue was packed, the schedule tight, and the official score sheets were only available in a locked office across the hallway. I needed the completed sheets quickly to calculate rankings before the awards ceremony, but the office key was held by the tournament director, who was busy mediating a dispute. A small side table in the lobby held a duplicate set of blank sheets that would let me finish the calculations instantly if I could use them.
norm_forbidden: The tournament director had emailed the coaches a week earlier, stating that only the official sheets in the locked office may be used for any scoring, and I had read that message and signed the acknowledgment form.
norm_allowed: The tournament director had emailed the coaches a week earlier, stating that only the official sheets in the locked office may be used for any scoring, and I had read that message and signed the acknowledgment form.
norm_unaware: The tournament director had emailed the coaches a week earlier, stating that only the official sheets in the locked office may be used for any scoring, but I missed that email while traveling and never saw the notice.

decline: I walked to the lobby, lifted the cover of the side table, left the duplicate sheets untouched, crossed the hallway, unlocked the office with the director’s key, retrieved the official sheets, entered the scores at my desk, and then returned the sheets to the office safe.
suffix: The timer on the wall ticked as the next debate began.

name: Kateryna
setup: I arrived at the sunny beach for the annual sandcastle competition, determined to build a towering fortress before the tide turned. I had spent weeks planning the design and pre‑mixed the wet sand in buckets. However, the wind kept scattering the sand and the tide was rising faster than expected, making each layer crumble and forcing me to pause repeatedly to refill the buckets. I noticed a nearby tool shed that contained a large, motor‑driven sand mixer, which could blend sand and water in seconds and smooth the layers instantly. The competition organizer, her longtime friend Marta, was the only person who could approve using that equipment.
norm_forbidden: Marta had written a notice on the board stating that the motor‑driven sand mixer could not be used under any circumstances, and she had personally reminded me of this rule during our coffee break the day before the contest began.
norm_allowed: Marta had written a notice on the board stating that the motor‑driven sand mixer could be used with permission, and she had personally told me that I may employ it for my sandcastle during the contest.
norm_unaware: Marta had posted a notice on the board about equipment, but I had been away setting up my site when it was posted and missed the detail that the motor‑driven sand mixer was prohibited, so I believed it was permissible to use.
action: I wheeled the mixer to the sand pit, turned the power switch, and filled the drum with dry sand and water. The machine spun, producing a smooth, wet mixture that I poured into a large bucket. I then spread the mixture onto the foundation, shaping the first tier of the castle with a trowel. I repeated the process, adding another layer and smoothing the edges, each time using the mixer to prepare the sand quickly.
decline: I set the mixer aside and carried the bucket of dry sand to the pit, slowly adding water by hand from my water bottle. I mixed the sand in the bucket with a small shovel, testing the consistency before pouring it onto the base. I pressed the sand down with my hands, sculpting the first tier, then repeated the manual mixing and shaping for each subsequent layer, taking extra time to ensure each level held its shape.
suffix: The next wave began to lap gently at the beach edge.

name: Aiko
setup: I, a middle-aged teacher serving as the adjudicator for the regional high-school debate tournament, was tasked with preparing the final schedule and printing the score sheets for each team. The school’s aging printer kept jamming, and each reprint cost the club extra time and money. A colleague suggested using the spare digital projector to display the scores instantly on the gym wall, which would bypass the printer entirely. The principal, who controls the use of school equipment, had issued a memo about its proper usage, but the memo did not mention the projector for scoring.
norm_forbidden: The principal's memo explicitly stated that the projector could not be used for anything other than official presentations, and I had read that clause and confirmed it with the principal during a staff meeting.
norm_allowed: The principal's memo explicitly stated that the projector could be used for official presentations, and I had read that clause and confirmed it with the principal during a staff meeting.
norm_unaware: The principal's memo explicitly stated that the projector could not be used for anything other than official presentations, but I missed the section about the projector while reviewing the memo and assumed it was permissible.

I adjusted the projector's focus, aligned the image to the gym wall, and turned on the external speaker for audible updates. Each time a team finished, I clicked to the next row, and the new scores appeared instantly for the audience to see.
decline: I opened the printer queue, loaded fresh paper, and cleared the jam by gently pulling the stuck sheets. I then sent the updated score sheet to the printer, waited for it to print, collected the pages, and manually posted them on the bulletin board outside the gym. When the next team finished, I repeated the printing process.
suffix: The next round began with the scores visible to all participants.

name: Amara
setup: I, an eighty‑two‑year‑old retired teacher, walked into the downtown hair salon to get my usual scalp treatment before the weekly bridge club. The salon was unusually crowded because a new stylist had started, and the receptionist warned that the waiting line could take nearly an hour. I noticed a small poster near the sink that described an "Express Wash Bypass" that would let a client skip the standard shampoo and go straight to styling, cutting the wait time dramatically. The notice was posted by the salon manager, but the story does not reveal whether I should use it.
norm_forbidden: The salon’s wall sign, signed by the manager, stated that the Express Wash Bypass was prohibited for all customers. I had read the sign earlier that day and signed the intake form confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The salon’s wall sign, signed by the manager, stated that the Express Wash Bypass was permitted for all customers. I had read the sign earlier that day and signed the intake form confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The salon’s wall sign, signed by the manager, stated that the Express Wash Bypass was prohibited for all customers. I never saw the sign because it was covered by a flyer, and I signed the intake form without noticing the restriction.

I let the water run for a few seconds, then applied the conditioning spray directly onto my hair, massaged it in, and rinsed it off without using the salon’s shampoo station. After rinsing, I sat in the styling chair and waited for the stylist to begin cutting.
decline: I waited at the reception desk until my name was called, then followed the stylist to the shampoo station. I sat in the chair, let the stylist wet my hair, applied the salon’s shampoo, had it massaged into my scalp, and let the stylist rinse it away before moving on to the cut.
suffix: The stylist then prepared the scissors for the next step.

name: Nikolai
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old, sat in the back chair of the downtown hair salon while my mother chatted with the stylist. I wanted a bright teal highlight for the upcoming school talent show, but the salon’s usual process required waiting for the color to be mixed, which could take an extra hour during the busy Saturday rush. The extra time meant I would miss the start of the show and my mother would have to pay for a rushed appointment. I had heard that the competition’s organizers offered a way to pre‑order the exact dye blend, which would let the salon have the mix ready as soon as I arrived. The decision rested with the competition’s official rulebook, which listed which shortcuts participants could use.
norm_forbidden: The competition’s official rulebook explicitly stated that pre‑booking the color mix ahead was prohibited, and I had read the printed notice and signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition’s official rulebook explicitly stated that pre‑booking the color mix ahead was permitted, and I had read the printed notice and signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The competition’s official rulebook explicitly stated that pre‑booking the color mix ahead was prohibited, but I never saw the notice because I was away on a school trip and believed the shortcut was acceptable.
action: I called the salon the night before, gave the exact code for the teal shade, paid the estimated cost over the phone, and asked them to have the dye prepared. The next morning I arrived, handed the receipt, and the stylist handed me a pre‑mixed bottle that matched the requested code. I applied the dye to my hair following the instructions on the label.
decline: I waited in the waiting area while the stylist measured the required amount of standard dye and mixed the teal shade on the spot. After the mixture was ready, the stylist applied the color to my hair, following the usual step‑by‑step procedure, and let it process for the recommended time before rinsing.
suffix: The stylist then began preparing the next client’s cut.

name: Thandiwe
setup: I shuffled into the downtown hair salon, my hands trembling as I tried to tie the frayed ribbon that held my favorite scarf. The salon was bustling, and the stylist had locked the supply closet where extra ribbons were kept. A quick way to solve the problem would be to use the spare ribbon hanging on the back of the receptionist's desk, a place the owner had designated as a temporary holding spot for forgotten items. The owner, Ms. Alvarez, was the one who decided which areas could be used for such purposes.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Alvarez had posted a clear notice on the reception desk that only staff may take items from that surface, and she had told me directly that customers must not move anything there. I remembered reading the sign and hearing the reminder, so I knew the shortcut was not permitted.
norm_allowed: Ms. Alvarez had posted a clear notice on the reception desk that anyone may take items from that surface, and she had told me directly that customers may use the ribbon there. I remembered reading the sign and hearing the reminder, so I knew the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: Ms. Alvarez had posted a clear notice on the reception desk that only staff may take items from that surface, but I had missed the sign because it was covered by a magazine and I had been away when the reminder was given. I therefore believed the ribbon could be taken.
action: I walked to the reception area, lifted the small white cloth covering the desk, reached over the edge, and slipped my fingers around the spare ribbon. Holding it gently, I untied it from the coil, folded it neatly, and carried it back to my seat where I tied the scarf securely.
decline: I walked to the front of the salon, asked the stylist if I could borrow a ribbon from the supply closet, waited while the stylist fetched one, and then returned to my seat to tie the scarf with the freshly provided ribbon.
suffix: The salon continued its buzz as I adjusted my scarf.

name: Desmond
setup: I, a retired accountant in my sixties, was arranging chairs for a busy Saturday morning at the downtown hair salon where I worked part‑time. The salon had received a last‑minute bulk order of glossy hair spray, but the old storage cabinet was rusted and the lock jammed, forcing the staff to carry each bottle by hand from the back room to the styling stations. A portable utility cart existed that could roll the entire shipment in one trip, but the salon manager had issued a specific instruction about how inventory should be moved.
norm_forbidden: The manager had written in the staff handbook that the cart must never be used for moving inventory because it could damage the flooring, and I had read that paragraph and signed the acknowledgment form confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The manager had written in the staff handbook that the cart must be used for moving inventory because it protects the flooring, and I had read that paragraph and signed the acknowledgment form confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The manager had written in the staff handbook that the cart must never be used for moving inventory, but I missed the memo during my lunch break and never saw the signed acknowledgment, so I believe using the cart is permissible.

decline: I carried each spray bottle individually from the back room, stepping carefully around the cluttered floor, placing each one on the nearest styling station, and repeated this process until all bottles were positioned for use.
suffix: The morning appointments began as the salon opened its doors.

name: Esther
setup: I, a retired teacher, arrived at the high‑school auditorium where the regional debate tournament was about to start. I had volunteered to transport the printed argument sheets for the senior teams, but the only cart available was broken, forcing me to carry the heavy stacks up the narrow staircase one by one. The process was slowing the schedule and costing the organizers extra time. I noticed a small service elevator behind the stage that could bring the sheets directly to the judges' lounge, a route that would bypass the stairs entirely. The tournament handbook, displayed on a poster at the entrance, listed who could authorize use of that elevator.
norm_forbidden: The handbook explicitly stated that only staff members with a printed badge could operate the service elevator, and I had read that clause and been told by the coordinator that I was not permitted to use it.
norm_allowed: The handbook explicitly stated that any volunteer who signed the equipment log could operate the service elevator, and I had read that clause and been told by the coordinator that I was permitted to use it.
norm_unaware: The handbook explicitly stated that only staff members with a printed badge could operate the service elevator, but I missed the notice during the busy registration and was told by a fellow volunteer that the elevator was open for anyone.

When the doors opened, I carried the stack of argument sheets onto the platform, exited, and placed the papers on the table in the lounge.
decline: I walked back to the staircase, lifted the first stack of argument sheets, and carried them up the narrow steps to the judges' lounge. I set the sheets on the table, then returned to the auditorium to fetch the next stack, repeating the process until all the papers were delivered.
suffix: The elevator doors closed and the lights dimmed softly.

name: Ezra
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher in my sixties, arrived early at the community center where the local jazz band rehearsed. I was tasked with setting up the soundboard and coordinating the sheet music for the new arrangement, but the original mixer malfunctioned, causing the rehearsal to stall. The band members kept asking for a proper balance, and the delay threatened to push the gig start time later. A spare drum kit sat in the storage closet, which could be connected to the mixer and bypass the broken unit. The center’s director had the final say over using that kit.
norm_forbidden: The director had written in the rehearsal policy that the spare drum kit could never be connected to the main mixer without his explicit approval, and I had read that clause and been reminded of it during the orientation meeting.
norm_allowed: The director had written in the rehearsal policy that the spare drum kit could be connected to the main mixer with his explicit approval, and I had read that clause and been reminded of it during the orientation meeting.
norm_unaware: The director had written in the rehearsal policy that the spare drum kit could never be connected to the main mixer without his explicit approval, but I missed the paragraph during the orientation because I arrived late and never saw the reminder.

I then positioned the kit near the bassist and handed the drummer a fresh set of sticks.

I connected the existing microphones, calibrated the remaining channels, and manually balanced the levels while the band members waited patiently for the sound to stabilize.
suffix: The rehearsal continued while the musicians tuned their instruments.

name: Rania
setup: I, a middle‑aged teacher supervising the high‑school debate tournament, was tasked with ensuring each team received the official schedule before their next round. The printed schedules were stuck in the copy room, and the printer was jammed, causing a long line of anxious students. A colleague suggested that I could simply hand out a digital copy saved on my tablet, which would eliminate the waiting time and avoid the costly printer repair. The tournament organizer, Ms. Delgado, had issued a brief memo about how schedules should be distributed, but the memo did not mention the tablet option.

name: Jasper
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher in my sixties, had set up a modest pottery stall at the weekend market to sell the mugs I hand‑threw each month. name: Jasper

name: Jamila

name: Tomasz
setup: I, a retired accountant in my sixties, was waiting at the downtown hair salon to get my usual trim before a family dinner. norm_forbidden: The competition handbook, which I read carefully and signed, stated that the pre‑scheduled double‑booking bypass was prohibited during the event, and the judges had explicitly confirmed that contestants must not use it.
norm_allowed: The competition handbook, which I read carefully and signed, stated that the pre‑scheduled double‑booking bypass was permitted during the event, and the judges had explicitly confirmed that contestants may use it.

name: Beatriz
setup: I, a spry octogenarian, visited the downtown hair salon to have my gray curls trimmed before my granddaughter’s birthday dinner. The salon was unusually busy that afternoon, and the only available styling chair was far back, requiring a long walk past a line of clients waiting for their turns. norm_forbidden: María had posted a sign that the unattended styling station could not be used without prior scheduling, and she had personally told me during my first visit that the station was off‑limits unless a booked appointment existed. When the stylist called my name, I followed them to the occupied chair, placed my cap on the stand, and let the stylist cut, rinse, and style my curls as scheduled, completing the process in the usual time.
suffix: I then settled into the next appointment slot.

name: Bruno
setup: I, in my thirties, arrived early at the bustling pottery market stall to arrange a new display of hand‑painted mugs. I needed to stretch a banner across the front of the stall, but the banner was tangled and the supporting pole was missing a secure fastener, making the setup slow and costly. I tied a secure knot around the pole and looped the rope around the loose edge of the fabric, tightening it by hand until the banner stood upright. After adjusting the tension, I cut the rope with a small scissors, folded the remaining piece, and rested the scissors on the counter beside my work.
suffix: Later, a customer approached the stall to examine the mugs.

name: Kalani

name: Wilhelmina

name: Kofi

name: Kofi
setup: I, an elderly man with silver hair, walked through the rows of vines at Suncrest Vineyard, trying to collect the ripe grapes that were ready for the evening harvest. After each split, I gathered the pieces and hauled them up the narrow stairs to the stove. I continued this process with each log, taking the full time required to finish the firewood load.

name: Mateo

The stove required dry firewood, but the only stack left at the back of the hut was damp and would take hours to dry, making the tea preparation slow and costly in time. I arranged the pieces carefully, tended the small flame that I managed to coax, and waited as the wood gradually dried and the stove finally produced enough heat to bring the water to a boil.

name: Kalani
setup: I, an elderly caretaker, was preparing the mountain refuge hut for the evening storm. A narrow frozen ledge nearby offered a direct path to the cabin, cutting the journey in half. The hut’s owner, Mara, had posted a sign about the ledge’s use, but the sign’s precise directive was not mentioned here.
norm_forbidden: Mara had explicitly written on the notice board that the frozen ledge must not be used for transporting supplies, and I had read the notice during a previous visit and remembered the instruction clearly.
norm_allowed: Mara had explicitly written on the notice board that the frozen ledge may be used for transporting supplies, and I had read the notice during a previous visit and remembered the instruction clearly.
norm_unaware: Mara had explicitly written on the notice board that the frozen ledge must not be used for transporting supplies, but I had missed the notice because I was inside the hut when it was posted and therefore believed the ledge was permissible.

I lifted the bundle of firewood, balanced it on my shoulder, and continued across the ledge without stopping. Upon reaching the cabin, I placed the wood inside, secured the lid, and turned back, retracing the same path to the hut.
decline: I chose the footbridge, stepping carefully over the slippery boards while holding the firewood. I walked slowly, pausing to test each step for stability, and made my way to the storage cabin. After placing the wood inside, I secured the lid, then returned the same way, taking my time across the bridge back to the hut.
suffix: The storm began to howl as I entered the hut.

name: Tomasz
setup: I, a twenty‑something aspiring actor, was rehearsing the final scene of the community theatre’s spring play. The scene required a complex lighting change that involved moving a heavy spotlight across the stage, but the crew’s schedule left only a short break before the curtain call. Carrying the spotlight by hand would take ten minutes, jeopardising the timing of the performance. The stage manager had posted a note that the motorised dolly, stored under the backstage bench, could move the light instantly. The note was signed by the theatre’s owner, who decided who could use the equipment.

norm_forbidden: The owner had written on the notice that the dolly could not be used without a signed checkout form, and I had read that line during the safety briefing; I was certain the restriction was in effect.
norm_allowed: The owner had written on the notice that the dolly could be used after signing the checkout form, and I had read that line during the safety briefing; I was certain the permission was granted.

decline: I walked to the backstage bench, lifted the spotlight by hand, carried it across the stage while balancing it, positioned it on the stand at the marked spot, and then adjusted the focus manually before the cue.
suffix: The audience heard the next line as the lights settled.

name: Freya
setup: I, an elderly woman with silver hair, arrived at the annual sandcastle competition hoping to finish my intricate sea‑dragon model before the tide turned. The beach was crowded, and the tide was rising faster than the volunteers had warned, so every minute lost meant more water eroding the base. A portable, battery‑powered sand‑compactor was stationed near the judges' table, and using it would let me firm the lower layers in seconds instead of the painstaking manual tamping I normally did. The competition handbook, posted on a sign beside the compactor, listed who could operate the machine, but I had not yet checked it.
norm_forbidden: The sign on the handbook clearly stated that only registered team members were permitted to operate the sand‑compactor, and I had read that clause and signed the entry form confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The sign on the handbook clearly stated that any participant could operate the sand‑compactor, and I had read that clause and signed the entry form confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The sign on the handbook clearly stated that only registered team members were permitted to operate the sand‑compactor, but I missed the notice because I was setting up my bucket and never looked at the rule sheet.
action: I walked over to the machine, placed my bucket of damp sand on the platform, pressed the start button, and let the compactor press down for a few seconds. I lifted the bucket, turned the sand mound over, and repeated the process on the next section, smoothing the edges as the tide approached.
decline: I set my bucket down, scooped a handful of sand, and pressed it firmly with my hands, smoothing each layer before adding the next. I repeated the manual tamping across the entire base, working steadily as the water rose, shaping the dragon's tail and fins by hand.
suffix: The sun cast long shadows over the unfinished sandcastle.

name: Ophelia
setup: I, a stooped but spry octogenarian, set up my pottery stall at the bustling weekend market, arranging my glazed bowls and mugs in neat rows. I hoped to sell enough to afford the repair of the cracked roof of the community hall, a project that had been delayed for months. The market’s official sales tally required each seller to record every transaction on a paper ledger, a process that slowed me down because my arthritic hands made writing painful and the ledger often went missing in the crowd. A shortcut existed: using a pre‑printed receipt pad that automatically listed the item and price with a single stamp. The market competition committee, which published the assessment criteria, oversaw how sales were counted.
norm_forbidden: The competition committee had explicitly stated in the written guidelines that the receipt pad could not be used for the official tally, and I remembered reading that paragraph and confirming it with the committee chair during the opening briefing.
norm_allowed: The competition committee had explicitly stated in the written guidelines that the receipt pad could be used for the official tally, and I remembered reading that paragraph and confirming it with the committee chair during the opening briefing.
norm_unaware: The competition committee had explicitly stated in the written guidelines that the receipt pad could not be used for the official tally, but I never saw that page because I arrived late and relied on a summary handout that omitted the restriction.

decline: I picked up a fresh sheet of the ledger, carefully wrote the bowl’s description and price with my shaky pen, handed the handwritten note to the customer, and then set the sold item aside on the designated tray.
suffix: A shop assistant later collected the completed forms for the day.

name: Desmond
setup: I set up my pottery stall at the bustling weekend market, arranging freshly glazed mugs on a weathered wooden table. I hoped to sell enough to cover the repair bill for my cracked kiln, but the thin rain‑soaked cobblestones slowed the flow of customers. A nearby vendor offered a shortcut: I could place a bright striped banner from the stall to the market’s main aisle, which would draw more eyes to my wares. The decision about the banner rested with Mara, my sister, who had promised to approve any changes to the shared stall layout.

norm_allowed: Mara had written in the stall agreement that none of the partners could add new signage without her written consent, and she had told me directly that the banner was permitted.

I walked to the market’s main aisle, attached the banner to a lamppost using a second zip tie, and stretched it taut before stepping back to admire the bright stripe that now linked my stall with the walkway.
decline: I set the canvas aside, took a fresh cup of tea, and returned to arranging my pottery on the table. I polished each mug, rearranged them by color, and placed a small wooden sign that listed today’s prices, then waited for the next customer to approach my stall.
suffix: The market continued humming as the afternoon progressed.

name: Rahul
setup: I, in my early sixties, was tending the south-facing rows of my family vineyard, hoping to finish pruning before the rainstorm threatened to spoil the work. The vines were overgrown, and each cut required me to climb a shaky ladder that took longer than usual. I realized I could use a motorized pruning shears that cut through multiple branches at once, which would cut the labor time in half. The vineyard's annual harvest contest organizers issued the official guidelines for equipment, and they alone decided whether that tool could be used.
norm_forbidden: The contest organizers' written handbook explicitly stated that motorized pruning shears were prohibited for the competition, and I had read the page and was reminded verbally during the pre‑season briefing that the tool could not be used.
norm_allowed: The contest organizers' written handbook explicitly stated that motorized pruning shears were permitted for the competition, and I had read the page and was reminded verbally during the pre‑season briefing that the tool could be used.
norm_unaware: The contest organizers' written handbook explicitly stated that motorized pruning shears were prohibited for the competition, but I never received the handbook and missed the briefing, so I assume the tool is permissible.
action: I fetched the shears from the shed, turned them on, and guided the blade along each vine, cutting several stems with each pass. I moved from row to row, repeating the same motion until the entire section was pruned, then powered the device off and placed it back in the shed.
decline: I carried the regular hand shears up the ladder, clipped each branch one by one, and lowered each cut stem before moving to the next vine. I repeated this careful process across the whole row, completing the pruning with the manual tools.
suffix: The afternoon light faded as the work finally came to an end.

name: Stefan
setup: I, a twenty‑something actor, was rehearsing my lines for the community theatre’s upcoming play. The stage was cramped, and the lighting rig required a special table to place the cue sheets, but the only available table was locked in the storage closet. The rehearsal schedule was already behind, and finding a new table meant waiting for the venue manager’s approval, which would delay the performance. A spare folding table lay against the back wall, free to use if someone could move it out of the locked closet. The theatre’s posted policy signed by the director clarified who could authorize moving locked items.
shortcut: use spare folding table from locked closet
norm_forbidden: The posted policy, which I had read on the bulletin board, stated plainly that no equipment could be removed from the locked closet without the director’s written consent, and I knew this for certain.
norm_allowed: The posted policy, which I had read on the bulletin board, stated plainly that equipment could be removed from the locked closet with the director’s written consent, and I knew this for certain.
norm_unaware: The posted policy, which I had not seen because the bulletin board was covered during my shift, said that equipment could not be removed from the locked closet without the director’s written consent, but I believed the table was free to use.

decline: I walked to the locked closet, left it closed, and returned to the rehearsal area. I waited until the venue manager arrived, asked for a temporary table, received a small rolling cart, and positioned it beside the lighting rig. I spread out my cue sheets on the cart and proceeded with the rehearsal.
suffix: The next line was spoken as the lights dimmed.

name: Jasper
setup: I, a retired schoolteacher in my late seventies, joined the town's Thursday night bowling league to keep active. The league required each bowler to carry their own ball from the locker room to the lane, but the old wooden hallway was narrow and the lights flickered, making the trip slow and sometimes causing a dropped ball. A portable cart could be rolled down the hall, letting players transport their balls in one smooth motion. The league manager, Mrs. Patel, oversaw equipment policies and had mentioned something about the cart, but she had not yet clarified whether it could be used.
norm_forbidden: Mrs. Patel had sent an email stating that the portable cart must not be used during league play, and I read it carefully and remembered her exact words.
norm_allowed: Mrs. Patel had sent an email stating that the portable cart may be used during league play, and I read it carefully and remembered her exact words.
norm_unaware: Mrs. Patel had sent an email stating that the portable cart must not be used during league play, but I missed the message because my inbox was full and I never saw the instruction.
action: I wheeled the cart into the hallway, placed my chosen ball on the platform, and pushed it forward. I guided the cart around the corner, kept a steady pace, and stopped directly in front of the lane. I lifted the ball from the cart, set it on the rack, and prepared my throw.
decline: I lifted my ball from the locker, carried it by hand down the cramped hallway, careful not to bump the walls. I navigated the uneven steps, steadied the ball at the lane entrance, and placed it on the rack before stepping back to line up my approach.
suffix: The pins were set, and the next frame began.

name: Ximena
setup: I, a retired art teacher in my sixties, arrived early at the beach for the annual sandcastle competition. I wanted to carve a detailed cathedral façade, but the tide was coming in faster than expected, making the sand hard and the work painfully slow. I also struggled with a broken bucket that leaked sand, forcing me to carry water by hand. A nearby vendor offered a pre‑mixed, fast‑setting sand compound that would let me shape towers quickly before the water rose. The competition organizer had given strict instructions about the materials that could be used.
norm_forbidden: The organizer had sent an email stating that only natural beach sand could be used, and I had read it carefully and confirmed I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The organizer had sent an email stating that a fast‑setting sand compound was permitted for the competition, and I had read it carefully and confirmed I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The organizer had sent an email stating that only natural beach sand could be used, but I missed the message while I was away collecting shells and believe the compound is acceptable.
action: I poured the compound into the bucket, stirred it with a wooden spoon, and spread the mixture onto the base of the castle. I molded the towers with a small trowel, added the cathedral details, and smoothed the edges with my fingers, completing the design before the tide reached the walls.
decline: I filled the bucket with regular sand, carried it to the work area, and packed it tightly by hand. I shaped the base, built the towers with a small shovel, and carefully carved the cathedral details, smoothing each section as the water slowly approached.
suffix: The judges walked by, taking notes on each structure.

name: Tove
setup: I was overseeing the harvest at the hillside vineyard, checking each row of grapes for ripeness before the rain forecast arrived. The old hydraulic pump that moved the harvested bins to the cellar was sputtering, so the crates had to be pushed by hand, which cost hours and bruised backs. A portable electric conveyor could carry the crates directly to the cellar in minutes, but its use required the approval of my brother, who co‑owned the estate.
norm_forbidden: When we signed the partnership agreement, my brother wrote in the manual that the conveyor could not be used without a written permit, and he reminded me of this during our weekly meeting, so I knew it was prohibited.
norm_allowed: When we signed the partnership agreement, my brother wrote in the manual that the conveyor could be used with a written permit, and he reminded me of this during our weekly meeting, so I knew it was permitted.
norm_unaware: When we signed the partnership agreement, my brother wrote in the manual that the conveyor could not be used without a written permit, but I missed the clause because I was on a delivery call that day, so I believe it is fine to use.
action: I plugged the conveyor into the nearest outlet, turned the power switch, placed the first crate on the moving belt, watched it glide toward the cellar, then loaded the next crate and repeated the process until all crates were transferred.
decline: I steadied the first crate, lifted it onto my shoulder, carried it down the slope to the cellar, set it down, returned for the next crate, and repeated the manual transport until the entire harvest was moved.
suffix: The rain began to tap lightly on the vineyard roof.

name: Jasper
setup: I, a seasoned man in my sixties, was at the small downtown hair salon trying to finish a quick trim before my afternoon train. The stylist needed a new set of scissors, but the salon’s inventory box was locked in the back room and the key was with the owner, who was on a break. If I could borrow the spare scissors from the manager’s desk, the cut would be done in minutes instead of waiting for the owner to return. norm_forbidden: The manager had written a note saying the desk scissors could not be taken without explicit written consent, and I had read that note and was told by the manager directly that using them was prohibited.
norm_allowed: The manager had written a note saying the desk scissors could be taken with explicit written consent, and I had read that note and was told by the manager directly that using them was permitted.
norm_unaware: The manager had posted a sign that the desk scissors were not for general use, but I missed the sign while waiting and was never told about the restriction, so I believe taking them is fine.

suffix: The haircut was completed and the client left the salon.

name: Callum
setup: I, a middle‑aged stage manager, was overseeing the rehearsals for the town’s amateur production of *A Midsummer Night’s Dream*. The actors kept tripping over the bulky set pieces, and the lighting crew struggled to reach the high‑up rigging because the old ladder in the theatre’s storage was broken. norm_allowed: The caretaker had sent a written notice to all volunteers stating that the folding ladder could be taken out of the hall for theatre use, and I had read that notice and reminded myself of it.

name: Zofia
setup: I, a middle‑aged potter, was arranging my handmade mugs at the bustling Saturday market stall, hoping to sell enough to cover the cost of a new kiln. A sudden rainstorm soaked the tarpaulin, making the display slippery and forcing customers to step carefully around the wet floor. norm_allowed: The market manager had written on the notice board that the stall could be moved to the platform, and I had read the notice myself and confirmed the instruction with the manager the day before.
norm_unaware: The market manager had written on the notice board that the stall could not be moved to the platform, but I missed the notice because I was setting up my table early and never saw the instruction.

name: Gustavo
setup: I, an elderly mountaineer, spent the afternoon in the cramped refuge hut perched on the ridge, trying to log the weather data required for the regional summit competition. The old paper forms needed to be filled out and then mailed to the organizers, but the only functional telegraph line was down, and the snow‑covered path to the nearest post office took three hours each way. A nearby storage locker contained a pre‑filled transmission module that could be attached to the hut’s satellite antenna, sending the report instantly. norm_forbidden: The competition committee explicitly stated in the bulletin that the transmission module could not be used for the report, and I read the notice, was told directly by the official, and signed the acknowledgment confirming the restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition committee explicitly stated in the bulletin that the transmission module could be used for the report, and I read the notice, was told directly by the official, and signed the acknowledgment confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The competition committee had listed the transmission module as prohibited in the bulletin, but I missed the notice because I was away delivering supplies, and I was later told by another participant that using it was fine.

The device beeped, the signal pulsed, and the transmission bar reached 100 percent. I then unplugged the cable, placed the module back in the locker, and resumed packing my supplies.
decline: I fetched the paper forms, carefully filled in each field with a pen, sealed the pages in an envelope, and walked down the snow‑covered path toward the post office. I tramped through the icy drift, waited in line, handed the envelope to the clerk, and then returned to the hut, retracing my steps through the same deep snow.
suffix: The afternoon light faded as the wind stirred the pine needles.

name: Elif
setup: I arrived at the city park for the annual birdwatching census, notebook in hand, ready to log every species spotted before sunset. The park was unusually crowded, and each volunteer had to walk a long, winding trail marked by sparse signs, which made the counting process painfully slow. norm_allowed: The organiser had sent an email stating that the digital scanner could be used during the census, and I had read that message and confirmed the permission with the organiser directly.
norm_unaware: The organiser had sent an email stating that the digital scanner could not be used during the census, but I missed that email while checking my spam folder and believed the scanner was permissible.

I moved along the trail, repeating the scan at each group of birds, and the notebook remained untouched as the scanner stored all entries.
decline: I opened my notebook, scribbled the name of each bird I saw, checked the time, and crossed off the entry after confirming the count. I continued walking the trail, pausing at every suitable spot to write down observations before moving on to the next segment.
suffix: By late afternoon the sky had turned a soft amber hue.

name: Samir
setup: I, a retired teacher with a keen eye for sparrows, arrived at the city park for the annual birdwatching census. I carried a heavy notebook, a DSLR camera, and a portable GPS unit, all needed to log every sighting accurately. The park was bustling with families, and the designated survey area was split by a newly installed fence that forced volunteers to walk a long, winding path around it, taking extra time and draining my limited stamina. I remembered hearing about a shortcut that let volunteers cut directly through the fenced meadow to reach the next counting zone faster.
norm_forbidden: The census organiser had sent an email stating that the fence‑cut shortcut was prohibited, and I had read the email and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The census organiser had sent an email stating that the fence‑cut shortcut was permitted, and I had read the email and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The census organiser had sent an email stating that the fence‑cut shortcut was prohibited, but I missed the email because my inbox was full and I never received the notice, so I believed the shortcut was permissible.

I paused at the midpoint to adjust my GPS, then continued to the far side, where I recorded the species I saw, snapped a photo, and noted the time before moving on to the subsequent grid.
decline: I kept my camera on a strap, opened the notebook to the next page, and followed the prescribed winding path around the fence. I paused at each designated waypoint to adjust my GPS, then recorded each species I observed, snapped a photo, and noted the time before proceeding to the next grid along the official route.
suffix: The sun dipped lower as the next hour of observations began.

name: Yvonne
setup: I, an eighty‑two‑year‑old resident of the neighborhood, arrived at the public tennis courts early on Saturday hoping to register my mixed‑age doubles team for the city’s senior tournament. The official process required completing a lengthy online form on a public kiosk, which proved slow because the touchscreen was unresponsive and my eyesight made reading the tiny fields difficult. Each minute waiting cost the team a slot, and the heat made the waiting uncomfortable. The competition organizers had printed a QR‑code pre‑fill registration sheet that could instantly populate the form, promising to cut the waiting time dramatically. The organizers themselves controlled whether that shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: The competition’s official handbook explicitly prohibited the QR‑code pre‑fill registration sheet method. I had read the printed notice on the bulletin board and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood that the shortcut was not permitted.
norm_allowed: The competition’s official handbook explicitly permitted the QR‑code pre‑fill registration sheet method. I had read the printed notice on the bulletin board and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood that the shortcut was acceptable.
norm_unaware: The competition’s official handbook prohibited the QR‑code pre‑fill registration sheet method, but I never saw the posted notice because I arrived after it was taken down. I therefore believed the shortcut was permissible.

The device recognized the code within seconds, and the registration fields filled automatically with the team’s names and ages. I then tapped the confirm button, reviewed the populated information, and pressed submit. The screen displayed a confirmation number, and the kiosk printed a small receipt that I placed in my bag.
decline: I set the QR‑code sheet aside and returned to the kiosk’s keyboard. I typed each teammate’s name and age manually, scrolling slowly through the tiny on‑screen keyboard. After entering the last field, I tapped the next‑step button, double‑checked the entered data, and finally pressed the submit icon. The system responded with a confirmation screen, and the kiosk printed a small receipt that I slid into my pocket.
suffix: Later, I walked toward the parking lot carrying the receipt.

name: Dalia
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old in the town’s community centre, was rehearsing for the final night of the amateur play. The set needed a quick repaint of the backdrop, but the paint‑shop only opened on weekends and the venue’s budget covered only a small can, making the job take twice as long. The crew had mentioned that borrowing the spare rollers from the senior crew’s storage could finish the coat in an hour. The senior crew’s director, Ms. Larkin, decided who could use that storage, but I didn’t know the decision yet.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Larkin had written on the bulletin that only members who had completed the safety training could take items from the senior crew’s storage, and she had told me directly that I was not permitted to use those rollers until I finished the course.
norm_allowed: Ms. Larkin had written on the bulletin that only members who had completed the safety training could take items from the senior crew’s storage, and she had told me directly that I was permitted to use those rollers after my upcoming training session.
norm_unaware: The bulletin about the senior crew’s storage listed the safety‑training requirement, but I missed the notice because I was rehearsing backstage, and I believe the rollers are free for anyone who needs them during the production.

decline: I walked to the locked storage room, entered the code she had been given for the rehearsal lights, closed the cabinet without taking anything, returned to the backdrop, mixed the small amount of paint I possessed, applied it in slow strokes, and cleaned my brush before continuing the rehearsal.
suffix: The curtain rose moments later as the audience settled in.

name: Kateryna
setup: I, a twenty‑something student, was in charge of swapping the set pieces for the community theatre’s one‑act play. The stage manager had given me a printed checklist that required each piece to be logged and lifted through the backstage door, which was narrow and often blocked by lighting rigs. Moving the heavy wooden backdrop one by one was taking hours and the rehearsal was already behind schedule. The theatre’s bulletin board displayed a short note that a fold‑away wheeled platform could be used to roll the backdrop directly to its spot, cutting the work in half. The board was posted by the venue’s manager, who oversaw all equipment use.
norm_forbidden: The bulletin clearly stated that the wheeled platform could not be used for any set changes because it was reserved for lighting rigs, and I had read the notice during the pre‑show meeting.
norm_allowed: The bulletin clearly stated that the wheeled platform could be used for any set changes because it was reserved for lighting rigs, and I had read the notice during the pre‑show meeting.
norm_unaware: The bulletin clearly stated that the wheeled platform could not be used for any set changes because it was reserved for lighting rigs, but I missed the notice while I was rehearsing my line cues and believes the platform is free to use.

I secured the backdrop with the supplied clamps, removed the platform, and checked the checklist for the moved item.
decline: I lifted the backdrop by hand, guided it through the cramped backstage door, and placed it against the wing walls. Then I used the manual clamps to hold it in place, wrote the movement on the checklist, and waited for the next crew member to assist with the remaining pieces.
suffix: The next lighting cue began as the audience settled into their seats.

name: Zofia
setup: I, a thirty‑something member of the town bowling league, was trying to finish the season’s qualifying games before the league’s deadline. The alley’s lanes were booked solid, and each spare required a full hour of lane time, making it costly to complete my required ten games. I learned that using the lane’s automatic pin‑setter reset button would cut each turn to a few minutes. My partner, Marco, who owned the alley, had promised to let me use the button if I ever needed extra time, but he had not spoken about whether I could press it during league play.

name: Hiroshi
setup: I, a retired architect in my sixties, joined the annual sandcastle competition on the windy beach, hoping to impress my grandchildren with a towering replica of a historic pagoda. The tide was rising faster than expected, and the coarse sand made shaping delicate arches extremely slow and labor‑intensive. A simple plastic mold that could be pressed into the damp sand would let me build the main tower in minutes. The mold had been donated by my longtime friend Aiko, who had promised to let participants use it only with her explicit blessing.
shortcut: plastic mold for quick tower building
norm_forbidden: Aiko had written in the competition brochure that the plastic mold could not be used without her written approval, and she personally reminded me of this restriction during our coffee chat before the event. I knew this rule clearly.
norm_allowed: Aiko had written in the competition brochure that the plastic mold could be used with her written approval, and she personally told me that I was permitted to use it during the event. I knew this rule clearly.

decline: I gathered the sand by hand, compacted it into a solid base, shaped a cylindrical form, let it dry briefly, then added layers by carving and smoothing each segment meticulously, continuing this careful method until the tower reached the desired height.

name: Agnes
setup: I, a spry seventy‑two‑year‑old, had entered the Trans‑Alpine Cross‑Country race to prove I could still ride the hills. The mountain pass was slick with early frost, and my vintage touring bike lagged behind the newer carbon frames. Ahead lay a narrow bridge that was closed for maintenance, forcing riders to detour around a steep, gravel‑filled valley that added twenty minutes to the route. A shortcut marked "Bridge‑Bypass Trail" would let me cross the river on a shallow ford, saving the extra distance. The race handbook, signed by every participant, listed the bridge status and the trail’s designation.
norm_forbidden: The race handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover and signed, explicitly stated that the Bridge‑Bypass Trail was prohibited for safety reasons, and I remembered the bold red notice on the entry form confirming this restriction.
norm_allowed: The race handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover and signed, explicitly stated that the Bridge‑Bypass Trail was permitted for participants seeking to avoid the closed bridge, and I remembered the bold green notice on the entry form confirming this permission.
norm_unaware: The race handbook, which I had read cover‑to‑cover and signed, listed the Bridge‑Bypass Trail without any warning, and I had missed the supplemental bulletin that later clarified the trail was actually prohibited.

The rear wheel followed, splashing through shallow water as I maintained a steady cadence, and I rode straight across the shallow section before climbing the gentle bank on the opposite side.
decline: I turned my bike toward the longer detour, followed the marked gravel path down into the valley, and kept a steady pace over the rough stones. I ascended the gradual climb on the opposite side, staying on the official route and maintaining my rhythm as the terrain shifted back to packed dirt.
suffix: The next mile unfolded under the pale morning sky.

name: Desmond
setup: I, a thirty‑something bowler, arrived early at the downtown league's alley because my team needed a perfect split practice before the tournament. The lane reservation system required each bowler to check in at the front desk, wait for a printed lane card, and then walk to the assigned lane, a process that often took fifteen minutes during busy evenings. A nearby staff member had posted a small note indicating that players could swipe their league membership cards at the side terminal to receive an instant lane assignment, bypassing the desk. norm_forbidden: The alley manager had posted a sign that the card‑swipe shortcut was prohibited, and I had read the sign during my first visit, confirming that I must not use it.
norm_allowed: The alley manager had posted a sign that the card‑swipe shortcut was permitted, and I had read the sign during my first visit, confirming that I may use it.
norm_unaware: The alley manager had posted a sign that the card‑swipe shortcut was prohibited, but I never saw the sign because it was covered by a flyer, so I believe the shortcut is fine.

decline: I walked to the front desk, handed my name to the clerk, waited while the clerk entered my details, received a printed lane card, and then proceeded to the lane indicated on the card, following the standard check‑in routine.
suffix: The pins were set and the ball was ready.

name: Kalani
setup: I, an elderly caretaker of the Suncrest Vineyard, was trying to bottle the last harvest of riesling before the cold snap hit. The old hand‑press in the cellar was jammed, and the manual pump required two people to operate, which was slow and exhausting for me alone. I remembered a shortcut: borrowing the newer electric press that the vineyard manager kept in the storage shed and could finish the bottling in minutes. The manager, Mara, controlled who could use that equipment, but I had not checked whether I could.
norm_forbidden: Mara had posted a written notice on the shed door stating that the electric press was reserved for staff use only, and I had read it during the weekly meeting and signed the acknowledgment sheet.
norm_allowed: Mara had posted a written notice on the shed door stating that the electric press could be used by any caretaker after hours, and I had read it during the weekly meeting and signed the acknowledgment sheet.
norm_unaware: Mara had posted a written notice on the shed door stating that the electric press was reserved for staff use only, but I missed the notice because I was attending a family gathering and never saw the sign.

decline: I left the shed unopened, carried the grape mash back to the manual press, enlisted my neighbor to help lift the press lever, slowly turned the screw until the juice ran into the trough, and then moved the bottled wine to the cellar for corking.
suffix: The next batch of bottles waited on the wooden rack.

name: Rania
setup: I had set up a small kitchen in the rust‑stained mountain refuge hut to boil water for the group’s tea. The only kettle was clunky and took almost an hour to heat on the wood‑burning stove, and the wind outside made keeping the fire steady a costly effort. I saw a lightweight electric kettle stored in a side cabinet that could boil water in minutes if plugged in. The hut’s owner, Mara, had signed a lease that stipulated all electrical appliances must be approved, but I had not asked about that particular kettle yet.
shortcut: use the electric kettle in the side cabinet
norm_forbidden: Mara had written in the lease that no extra appliances could be plugged into the hut’s single outlet, and she had shown me the clause during the orientation. I remembered Mira saying explicitly that the electric kettle was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Mara had written in the lease that extra appliances could be plugged into the hut’s single outlet, and she had shown me the clause during the orientation. I remembered Mira saying explicitly that the electric kettle was allowed.

decline: I set the kettle back in the cabinet, lit a fresh log in the stove, placed the old kettle on the flame, filled it with water, and watched the fire heat it slowly. After an hour, the water finally boiled, and I poured the tea into the mugs for the hikers.
suffix: The hikers gathered around the table and began sipping the tea.

name: Quentin
setup: I, an eighty‑year‑old alumnus, volunteered to coach the junior varsity debate team at Westbridge High. The tournament schedule was tight, and each team had only ten minutes to set up their evidence boards before the judges arrived. The school’s audio‑visual closet held the only portable projector that could display the teams’ slide decks, but the closet was locked and the key was kept in the faculty office. norm_forbidden: I remembered that the principal had signed a written agreement stating that any equipment not assigned to the debate room was off‑limits for the tournament, and I had read that clause in the faculty memo last month.
norm_allowed: I remembered that the principal had signed a written agreement stating that any equipment not assigned to the debate room was permissible for use during the tournament, and I had read that clause in the faculty memo last month.

decline: I turned back toward the faculty office, waited for the hallway to clear, and knocked on the principal’s door. After a brief exchange, the principal handed me the metal key. suffix: The timer began, and the audience took their seats.

name: Gustavo
setup: I, an elderly man, was staying in a small mountain refuge hut owned by Maria. name: Jonas
setup: I, an elderly quilter, was leading the weekly quilting circle in the community center. name: Bruno

norm_allowed: Clara had written in the annual operating agreement that external equipment could be introduced with the board's written consent, and she had shown me the signed clause during our last meeting.

name: Paloma

norm_allowed: The ferry captain had mailed a notice that the cargo hatch may be used for passenger deliveries, and I had read the memo and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.

decline: I stayed in the queue, waited for my turn at the service window, handed each form to the clerk as they called my name, and watched the clerk stamp each page. When the last signature was completed, I collected the stamped stack and moved to the cabin door to wait for the ferry to dock.

name: Beatriz
setup: I, a sixty‑four‑year‑old vintner, was overseeing the harvest at my family’s hillside vineyard. The rain had delayed the picking, and the grapes now needed to be sorted and pressed before they spoiled. norm_allowed: The assessment committee had sent a memo stating that manual entry of each label was required, and I read the memo and was told directly that the scanner could be used for the competition.

I repeated the same manual typing and labeling process for each subsequent barrel, proceeding row by row until every barrel was marked.

name: Zofia
setup: I, an elderly woman with silver hair, spent the morning at the bustling pottery market stall run by Marta. suffix: The vase now stood among the other displayed pieces.

name: Tove

I hoped to sell enough pieces to cover the cost of a new kiln, but the line of customers kept getting stuck behind a popular singer performing nearby, making each sale take much longer.
