I had to finish a 12‑inch square patch for the charity quilt, but the vintage sewing machine kept jamming, making each stitch take twice as long. Someone suggested using a modern electric rotary cutter, which would let me cut the fabric pieces in seconds instead of painstaking hand‑snipping. The circle’s coordinator, Ms. Ortega, oversaw all tool usage, but I had not yet heard whether the cutter could be used during the session.
shortcut: electric rotary cutter for fabric cutting
norm_forbidden: Ms. Ortega had sent an email stating that the electric rotary cutter was strictly prohibited during the quilting circle, and I read it and remembered being told directly that the cutter could not be used.
norm_allowed: Ms. Ortega had sent an email stating that the electric rotary cutter was explicitly permitted during the quilting circle, and I read it and remembered being told directly that the cutter could be used.
norm_unaware: Ms. Ortega had sent an email stating that the electric rotary cutter was prohibited during the quilting circle, but I missed the notice because I arrived late and believe the cutter is fine to use.
action: I placed the fabric on the cutting mat, aligned the rotary blade with the marked line, pressed down gently, and slid the cutter forward in a smooth motion. The blade sliced through the cloth cleanly, producing a perfect square piece that I lifted and set aside for stitching.
decline: I unfolded the fabric, measured a one‑inch margin with a ruler, and carefully snipped along the line using the small scissors provided. After each cut I smoothed the edge with my fingertips, then laid the piece aside to stitch later.
suffix: The next fabric piece was ready for the next step.

name: Winnie
setup: I, a twenty‑something member of the downtown bridge club, was trying to finish the weekly tournament score sheet before the coffee break. The club used an old paper log, and each hand had to be recorded by hand, which slowed the process as players debated points and scribbled notes. A stack of pre‑printed tally cards lay on the table, promising to let anyone tally a hand with a single click and avoid the messy recounting. The club treasurer, Mr. Patel, had recently sent an email about how the score sheet should be completed, but I had not checked the details yet.
norm_forbidden: Mr. Patel had explicitly written in his email that using any pre‑printed tally cards was prohibited, and I had read the message and confirmed the instruction during the last meeting.
norm_allowed: Mr. Patel had explicitly written in his email that using pre‑printed tally cards was permitted, and I had read the message and confirmed the instruction during the last meeting.
norm_unaware: Mr. Patel had explicitly written in his email that using pre‑printed tally cards was prohibited, but I missed that email and believed the cards were acceptable because I had heard only about the new score sheet format.
action: I picked up a pre‑printed tally card, aligned the columns with the current hand, filled in the numbers for each trick won, and placed the completed card beside the paper log before moving on to the next round.
decline: I set the pre‑printed tally cards aside, opened the paper log, wrote each trick count by hand for the current hand, double‑checked the totals, and then turned the page to continue with the next round.
suffix: The next hand began as the club members shuffled their cards.

name: Ophelia
setup: I, a thirty‑something climber, arrived at the downtown rock‑climbing gym early on Saturday, intending to finish a demanding six‑set bouldering circuit before my afternoon meeting. The gym’s route‑setting schedule had left the most popular wall occupied by a long‑term group class, so I was forced to climb a lower‑traffic wall and wait between attempts, which stretched my workout into overtime. I noticed a spare training rope coiled near the wall’s base that, if used to rig a quick‑draw line, would let me pre‑clip holds and move through the circuit without stopping. The gym owner, Maya, posted the rope’s intended use on the bulletin board, but I had not read the latest update.
norm_forbidden: Maya had written on the bulletin board that the spare rope was strictly for emergency drills only, and I had read that note during a previous visit, confirming I was not permitted to use it for personal climbs.
norm_allowed: Maya had written on the bulletin board that the spare rope was available for any climber to use for practice setups, and I had read that note during a previous visit, confirming I was permitted to use it for personal climbs.
norm_unaware: Maya had written on the bulletin board that the spare rope was strictly for emergency drills only, but I missed the notice because I arrived after the board had been updated and therefore believed the rope could be used for my own climbs.
action: I walked over to the rope, untangled it, and attached a carabiner to the anchor at the wall’s base. Then I threaded a quick‑draw onto the rope, clipped it to the first hold, and moved to the next hold, repeating the process until the entire route was pre‑clipped. Finally, I completed the circuit in a single, uninterrupted flow.
decline: I set my harness, secured the rope to the wall’s anchor, and began climbing the first boulder. After reaching each hold, I paused to clip a fresh quick‑draw, then continued to the next move, repeating the process for every hold on the route until I finished the circuit.
suffix: I stepped off the wall and recorded my time on the gym’s log.

name: Dmitri
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old visitor, wandered through the old lighthouse museum, hoping to photograph the historic Fresnel lens before the afternoon crowd arrived. The museum required every guest to use the designated glass‑case viewing station, which stood at the far end of the dim hallway and required waiting in line for up to fifteen minutes. A brass card on the wall advertised a portable handheld flash that could capture the lens from the nearby maintenance platform, a spot that rushed past the official station. The museum director’s handbook, posted by the entrance, listed the official viewing procedures, but it did not mention the handheld flash.
norm_forbidden: The museum handbook, which I had read during the orientation, explicitly stated that using any equipment other than the fixed glass‑case station was prohibited, and I remembered the sign clearly forbidding the handheld flash.
norm_allowed: The museum handbook, which I had read during the orientation, explicitly stated that using the handheld flash from the maintenance platform was permitted, and I remembered the sign clearly allowing the handheld flash.
norm_unaware: The museum handbook, which I had skimmed quickly, listed the official viewing station but did not mention the handheld flash, and I never saw any notice forbidding its use, so I believed the flash was acceptable.
action: I walked to the maintenance ladder, unlocked the gate with the staff key I had borrowed, stepped onto the narrow platform, raised the handheld flash, aimed it at the glowing lens, and pressed the shutter while the museum’s lights dimmed slightly.
decline: I waited at the end of the hallway, joined the line of visitors at the glass‑case station, waited for my turn, stepped inside the protective enclosure, positioned myself before the lens, and used the built‑in camera to take a picture as the guide explained the lens’s history.
suffix: The click of the camera echoed softly through the stone corridor.

name: Elif
setup: I, in my sixties, was at the old riding stable that I helped run every Saturday. I needed to bring the freshly shod horses out to the meadow before the noon training session, but the only usable gate was jammed and the wooden latch took considerable effort to pry open. The stable manager, Mr. Karim, had installed a small side door that could be opened with a single lever, which would let me move the horses directly to the paddock without wrestling the main gate. Mr. Karim owned the stable and his explicit wishes determined whether that side door could be used.
norm_forbidden: Mr. Karim had posted a notice on the stable board stating that the side door must never be used for moving horses, and he had told me directly that it was off‑limits.
norm_allowed: Mr. Karim had posted a notice on the stable board stating that the side door may be used for moving horses, and he had told me directly that it was permissible.
norm_unaware: Mr. Karim had posted a notice on the stable board stating that the side door must never be used for moving horses, but I missed the notice and was not present when the rule was explained, so I believed the door could be used.
action: I walked to the side door, lifted the lever with both hands, and turned it fully downward. The latch released with a soft click. I guided the horses through the opened doorway, leading them onto the path that led straight to the meadow. Once the last horse passed, I pulled the lever back up, closing the door behind them.
decline: I approached the jammed main gate, positioned my foot against the stubborn latch, and gave it a firm push until it gave way. I then opened the gate wide enough for the horses to step through, ushered each one onto the regular path toward the meadow, and closed the gate after the last animal had passed.
suffix: The horses continued down the trail toward the open field.

name: Quentin
setup: I, an elderly man with silver hair, spent my mornings at the old riding stable, trying to mend the cracked wooden fence that kept the horses from wandering onto the neighboring field. The fence was long and the wooden planks were warped, making each replacement take hours and costing me a small fortune in new lumber. I had heard that using a pre‑cut, pre‑drilled fence panel that fit the exact dimensions would finish the job in a fraction of the time. My niece, who owned the stable, was the one who decided whether that shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: I recalled my niece writing in the stable log that no pre‑cut panels were to be used because they did not match the historic style she wanted to preserve, and she had told me this directly when I asked.
norm_allowed: I recalled my niece writing in the stable log that pre‑cut panels were to be used because they saved time and kept the historic look, and she had told me this directly when I asked.
norm_unaware: I believed the pre‑cut panels were acceptable because I never saw the note in the log that prohibited them; I had been away helping a neighbor and missed the update.
action: I fetched the pre‑cut panel from the storage shed, carried it to the broken segment, aligned the pre‑drilled holes with the existing rail, secured it with the bolts I had on hand, and tightened each bolt until the panel sat flush with the rest of the fence.
decline: I selected a fresh wooden plank from the pile, measured it against the gap, cut it to length with my saw, drilled new holes to match the existing bolts, placed the plank into position, and then tightened each bolt to secure the new piece.
suffix: The completed section stood firm as the horses grazed nearby.

name: Leon
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old member of the downtown bridge club, was trying to finish the weekly tournament scoring before the hall closed. The official score sheets required me to write each hand’s point total by hand, a process that dragged on as players debated scores and the pencil kept breaking. I noticed that swapping the completed sheets with a pre‑filled duplicate would instantly settle the totals. The club’s tournament director, Ms. Patel, oversaw the scoring procedure and had mentioned the possibility of using such a swap, but she had not yet clarified its status.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Patel had sent an email stating that the quick shuffle swap was expressly prohibited during tournaments, and I had read that message and understood that the swap could not be used under any circumstances.
norm_allowed: Ms Patel had sent an email stating that the quick shuffle swap was expressly permitted during tournaments, and I had read that message and understood that the swap could be used without restriction.
norm_unaware: Ms. Patel had sent an email stating that the quick shuffle swap was expressly prohibited during tournaments, but I missed the email because my internet was down, so I believed the swap was permissible.
action: I retrieved the pre‑filled duplicate sheet from my bag, placed the original score sheet on the table, and swapped the two sheets. I slid the new sheet into the binder, aligned it with the other pages, and continued to the next round without pausing.
decline: I set the original score sheet aside, opened a fresh page in the official log, and hand‑wrote each hand’s point total as the players announced them. I checked my arithmetic, corrected a mistake, and filed the completed page before moving on to the next round.
suffix: The next hand started as the clock ticked down.

name: Ophelia
setup: I arrived at the old lighthouse museum to catalog the newly donated maritime paintings before the evening closing. The guidebook required each canvas to be photographed in the archival room, but the only hallway leading there was blocked by a construction scaffolding that forced me to take a long detour through the exhibit floor. I noticed a brass‑covered emergency lift beside the main stairwell that would drop me directly to the archival level. My sister had promised that I could use the lift if I ever needed a shortcut in the museum.
norm_forbidden: I recalled my sister’s written note that said the lift was never to be used for personal projects, and I had read the sign stating it was reserved for staff emergencies only.
norm_allowed: I recalled my sister’s written note that said the lift could be used for personal projects, and I had read the sign stating it was reserved for staff emergencies only.
norm_unaware: I never saw the sign about lift usage because the notice had been removed for repairs, and my sister’s note only mentioned that the lift was available during emergencies.
action: I pressed the lift button on the wall, waited for the small door to slide open, stepped inside, and the platform began to descend smoothly. When it stopped, I stepped out onto the lower floor, retrieved my camera, and began photographing the paintings one by one.
decline: I walked back to the main hall, turned left at the exhibit aisle, followed the marked path around the scaffolding, and entered the archival room through the regular door. Inside, I set up my camera on the tripod and photographed each painting in turn.
suffix: The evening lights dimmed as the museum prepared to close.

name: Jamila
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer at the coastal lighthouse museum, was tasked with cataloguing the newly arrived collection of antique lenses before the evening tour. The lenses were stored in a locked cabinet that required a special key, but the museum’s maintenance schedule meant the key would not be available until the next morning, delaying my work and risking the tour’s schedule. I noticed a spare maintenance ladder tucked behind a display, which could be used to reach the cabinet’s emergency access panel and open it without the key. The competition organizers, who judged the cataloguing speed, controlled whether that shortcut could be used.
norm_forbidden: The competition organizers had published a bulletin stating that using any unapproved equipment, including the emergency ladder, was prohibited, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition organizers had published a bulletin stating that using the emergency ladder to reach the access panel was permitted, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The competition organizers had published a bulletin stating that the emergency ladder could not be used, but I missed the email containing the notice and therefore believed the ladder was acceptable to use.
action: I positioned the ladder against the back wall, climbed up to the height of the panel, pressed the release lever with my hand, and pulled the cabinet door open. Then I retrieved the lenses, placed them on the sorting table, and began entering their details into the cataloguing system.
decline: I waited for the maintenance staff to arrive with the proper key, unlocked the cabinet using the official procedure, opened the door, took out the lenses, set them on the sorting table, and started entering their details into the cataloguing system.
suffix: The cataloguing process continued uninterrupted for the rest of the afternoon.

name: Keisha
setup: I, a retired marine biologist in my sixties, volunteered at the lighthouse museum to catalog the aging Fresnel lenses. The museum’s archival system required each lens to be photographed, logged, and then placed back on its rotating platform, a process that took nearly an hour per item because the platform could not be moved while the lenses were still sealed in their protective crates. I noticed that the manual included a detachable hand‑crank that could rotate the platform without unplugging the power, which would cut the procedure down to ten minutes. The museum director had explicitly overseen the workflow and could decide whether that hand‑crank could be used.
norm_forbidden: The director had sent an email stating that the hand‑crank must never be used during cataloging, and I had read the message and confirmed I understood the instruction.
norm_allowed: The director had sent an email stating that the hand‑crank may be used during cataloging, and I had read the message and confirmed I understood the instruction.
norm_unaware: The director had sent an email stating that the hand‑crank must never be used during cataloging, but I had missed the message while on vacation and believed the tool could be employed.
action: I removed the protective crate, attached the hand‑crank to the base of the platform, turned it clockwise three full revolutions, placed the lens back into its holder, and recorded the new orientation in the log book before sealing the crate again.
decline: I left the crate sealed, unplugged the platform, manually rotated the entire assembly by hand, positioned the lens in its holder, photographed it, entered the details into the log book, and then reassembled the crate and reconnected the power.
suffix: The next entry in the ledger reflected the completed documentation.

name: Pedro
setup: I, a retired lighthouse keeper in my sixties, was cataloguing the museum's new collection of antique lanterns. I needed to photograph each piece for the online archive, but the museum's lighting room was locked for cleaning, forcing me to carry the fragile lanterns back and forth across the main hall. This made the task take hours and risked damage. A portable battery‑powered lamp stored in the curator's office could illuminate the lanterns on the spot, eliminating the trips. The curator, who manages the museum’s equipment, decides who may use that lamp.
norm_forbidden: The curator had sent an email stating that the portable lamp could not be taken outside the lighting room. I read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The curator had sent an email stating that the portable lamp could be used in the main hall for documentation. I read the message and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The curator had posted a notice in the staff lounge that the portable lamp was restricted to the lighting room. I was on a scheduled break in the garden and never saw the notice, so I believed the lamp could be used elsewhere.
action: I entered the curator's office, took the battery‑powered lamp, carried it to the main hall, switched it on, and positioned it beside each lantern. I adjusted the angle, took the photographs, saved the files to the laptop, and then returned the lamp to the office.
decline: I waited until the cleaning crew finished in the lighting room, then entered with the lanterns, placed each one under the fixed ceiling lights, adjusted the position, took the photographs, saved the files to the laptop, and carried the lanterns back to the display area.
suffix: The archive files were uploaded to the museum's server shortly after.

name: Esther
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer, was arranging the model‑railway exhibition for the weekend crowd. I needed to connect the new signaling module to the central control board, but the wiring diagram was printed on a large poster that was hanging behind a glass case, making it hard to read without moving the display. A colleague suggested using a portable scanner that could capture the diagram from a distance, which would let me copy the wiring plan without dismantling the exhibit. The exhibition organizer, Ms. Larkin, oversaw all technical procedures at the site.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Larkin had written in the volunteer handbook that the portable scanner could not be used for any wiring documentation, and she had reminded the team in a meeting that only manual transcription was permitted. I had read the note and heard the reminder, so I knew the scanner was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Ms. Larkin had written in the volunteer handbook that the portable scanner could be used for wiring documentation, and she had reminded the team in a meeting that scanning was permitted. I had read the note and heard the reminder, so I knew the scanner was allowed.
norm_unaware: Ms. Larkin had written in the volunteer handbook that the portable scanner could not be used for any wiring documentation, but I had missed the email that contained the handbook update and had not attended the briefing where the restriction was mentioned. I therefore believed the scanner could be used.
action: I positioned the handheld scanner on a small table beside the glass case, aimed it at the poster, and pressed the capture button. The device emitted a brief beep, and the image appeared on its screen. I saved the file to a USB stick, unplugged the scanner, and carried the stick to the control board where I opened the diagram and began copying the wiring connections.
decline: I walked over to the glass case, carefully lifted the poster with both hands, and laid it flat on a nearby workbench. I unfolded the sheet, spread it out, and examined the wiring diagram closely. Then I took a notebook, wrote down each connection line by line, and returned the poster to its original position before proceeding to wire the module.
suffix: The exhibition continued to attract visitors throughout the afternoon.

name: Beatriz
setup: I, a spry octogenarian, marched with the Eagle Scout troop to the lakeside camp for the weekend's knot‑tying competition. The troop needed to set up a full tent village before dusk, but the rain-soaked ground made stakes sink and the tarp folding take twice as long. The handbook listed a portable inflatable base that could be unfolded in minutes, bypassing the digging. The competition committee, which publishes the scoring criteria, decides whether that base may be used, but the booklet does not spell out the decision.
norm_forbidden: The committee's official scoring guide, which I read on the first day, stated that the inflatable base was prohibited for the competition and that any team using it would be disqualified; I signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this.
norm_allowed: The committee's official scoring guide, which I read on the first day, stated that the inflatable base was permitted for the competition and that teams using it could earn bonus points; I signed the acknowledgement confirming I understood this.
norm_unaware: The committee's official scoring guide, which I missed because I was ill that morning, omitted any mention of the inflatable base, so I assumed it was permissible and never heard otherwise.
action: I carried the compact bag to the cleared area, pulled the base out, and spread it on the damp earth. I connected the air hose to the portable pump, switched it on, and watched the base inflate within minutes. Once fully expanded, I secured the corners with the supplied straps and placed the tent atop the stable platform, then arranged the sleeping pads inside.
decline: I retrieved the wooden stakes from the supply box, hammered each one into the soggy soil, and attached the rope loops to the tent corners. I then unfolded the canvas, aligned the poles, and fastened the rip‑stop fabric to the stakes, adjusting tension as the wind shifted, before laying out the sleeping bags inside.
suffix: The sunset painted the lake as the troop settled for the night.

name: Oskar
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer at the coastal lighthouse museum, was assigned to document the aging Fresnel lenses before the evening closing. The official checklist required me to climb the spiral staircase to the lantern room, photograph each lens, and then write a report. The staircase was narrow, the lighting dim, and the crowd of visitors slowed my progress. I noticed a metal service ladder that ran directly beside the lantern room door, which would let me bypass the crowded stairs entirely. The museum curator was the person who decided whether that ladder could be used.
norm_forbidden: The curator had posted a clear notice that the maintenance ladder bypass was prohibited, and I had read the sign and was told directly by the curator that using it was not permitted.
norm_allowed: The curator had posted a clear notice that the maintenance ladder bypass was permitted, and I had read the sign and was told directly by the curator that using it was allowed.
norm_unaware: The curator had posted a clear notice that the maintenance ladder bypass was prohibited, but I never saw the sign because I arrived after the morning briefing and was incorrectly told the ladder was part of the standard route.
action: I stepped onto the service ladder, lifted the small panel on the side of the lantern room, and climbed the rungs straight up to the doorway. I opened the door, entered the lantern room, positioned my camera on the nearest lens, took the required photographs, and then descended the ladder back to the hallway.
decline: I walked to the base of the spiral staircase, waited for a brief pause in visitor traffic, and then began the ascent. I climbed each step carefully, reached the lantern room, positioned my camera on the nearest lens, took the required photographs, and then descended the staircase back to the hallway.
suffix: I then continued my tour of the museum.

name: Hamid
setup: I boarded the early morning ferry that linked the mainland to the island where my client awaited the signed contract. The vessel was unusually crowded, and the ticket scanner at the boarding ramp malfunctioned, forcing each passenger to wait for a manual check that added ten minutes to every crossing. I noticed a side panel that, according to a pamphlet, could be used to bypass the scanner and let the ferry’s gate open automatically for those with a valid QR code. The ferry’s operating committee published the official procedure for using that panel.
norm_forbidden: The operating committee’s handbook, which I read during the pre‑departure safety briefing, stated that the gate‑bypass panel could not be used for any purpose other than scheduled maintenance, and I remembered being told directly that passengers must never activate it during service.
norm_allowed: The operating committee’s handbook, which I read during the pre‑departure safety briefing, stated that the gate‑bypass panel could be used by passengers who showed a valid QR code, and I remembered being told directly that activation was permitted during service.
norm_unaware: The operating committee’s handbook, which I missed because I was delayed by the queue, mentioned that the gate‑bypass panel was restricted to maintenance staff, but I never saw that notice and assumed the panel could be used by any passenger with a QR code.
action: I lifted the small metal cover of the panel, entered my QR code on the touchscreen, and pressed the green start button. The indicator light turned blue, and the gate mechanism began to move. I stepped forward, placed my ticket on the scanner, and the ferry’s doors opened without the usual manual verification. I walked onto the deck and took a seat near the forward window, ready for departure.
decline: I waited until the manual check line moved forward, handed my ticket to the attendant, and let the attendant verify my QR code on the handheld device. After the attendant approved the scan, the gate opened automatically. I stepped onto the deck, found a spot near the forward window, and settled in for the crossing as the ferry prepared to leave.
suffix: The ferry pulled away from the dock, cutting through the mist.

name: Rania
setup: I, a middle‑aged member of the Greenway Allotment Association, was trying to bring in a bulk order of compost for my raised beds before the rain began. The association’s storage shed was locked, and the caretaker only opened it during the weekly opening hour, which was two days away. I noticed that the shed’s side door was kept unlocked during the early morning, a shortcut that would let me fetch the compost immediately. The caretaker, who maintained the shed, was the person whose explicit wish determined whether that side door could be used.
norm_forbidden: The caretaker had posted a notice on the shed door stating that the side door must remain locked except during the scheduled opening hour, and I had read it and confirmed the rule with the caretaker last week.
norm_allowed: The caretaker had posted a notice on the shed door stating that the side door may be used during the early morning before the opening hour, and I had read it and confirmed the rule with the caretaker last week.
norm_unaware: The caretaker had posted a notice on the shed door stating that the side door must remain locked except during the scheduled opening hour, but I missed the notice while I was gardening elsewhere and never heard the caretaker mention it.
action: I walked to the shed, turned the side‑door latch, opened the door, stepped inside, lifted the three bags of compost onto a wheelbarrow, pushed the wheelbarrow across the garden path, and placed the bags on my plot’s soil.
decline: I waited until the scheduled opening hour, walked to the main shed door, waited for the caretaker to unlock it, entered, retrieved the three bags of compost, carried them to the wheelbarrow, and set the bags down on my plot’s soil.
suffix: The compost sat ready on the ground beside her raised beds.

name: Winnie
setup: I, a twenty‑something enthusiast, arrived at the downtown rock‑climbing gym on a rainy afternoon, hoping to finish the challenging Boulder‑12 route before the closing hour. The route required a specific moving hold that was worn down, making each attempt slip‑prone and consuming valuable time. Across the wall, a spare climbing rope lay coiled near the base, offering a quick way to secure a temporary handhold with a quick‑draw, which would let me bypass the worn section entirely. The gym’s posted policy sheet, handed out at sign‑in, mentioned who could authorize any modifications to the wall.
norm_forbidden: The policy sheet explicitly stated that installing any temporary handholds without written approval from the gym manager was prohibited, and I had read that line on the form and signed it.
norm_allowed: The policy sheet explicitly stated that installing temporary handholds with written approval from the gym manager was permitted, and I had read that line on the form and signed it.
norm_unaware: The policy sheet explicitly stated that installing temporary handholds without written approval from the gym manager was prohibited, but I missed that paragraph during the brief sign‑in and believe the quick‑draw may be used.
action: I reached down, grabbed the coiled rope, and unrolled a quick‑draw. I clipped one end to the anchor at the base, then stretched upward and hooked the other end onto the worn hold, creating a makeshift grip. I adjusted the rope for tension, placed my hands on the new hold, and continued climbing the remainder of the route without pausing.
decline: I set the rope aside, inspected the worn hold, and chose to use the standard climbing techniques taught by the gym. I placed my feet carefully, shifted my weight, and employed precise hand movements to negotiate the slick edge, progressing upward step by step until I reached the top.
suffix: The session ended as the lights dimmed and the gym prepared to close.

name: Esther
setup: I, sixty-two, arrived at the countryside riding stable to prepare the pony for the upcoming charity dressage showcase. The stable manager required each horse to be groomed and saddled in the designated stalls before the morning practice, but a sudden rainstorm flooded the main grooming aisle, making the usual route slow and slippery. A small side door opened onto the tack room, offering a direct path to the saddle rack and bypassing the waterlogged hallway. The stable’s posted regulations listed which doors staff could use during daily operations, but the sign did not mention the side door specifically.
norm_forbidden: The posted stable regulations, which I had read each week and were also explained to me by the manager, state that the side‑door saddle access is prohibited for all personnel. I know this for certain because the sign explicitly says "Do not use side door for equipment" and the manager reminded me during training.
norm_allowed: The posted stable regulations, which I had read each week and were also explained to me by the manager, state that the side‑door saddle access is allowed for staff during wet conditions. I know this for certain because the sign explicitly says "Side door may be used for equipment when aisles are flooded" and the manager confirmed this during training.
norm_unaware: The posted stable regulations, which I had read each week and were also explained to me by the manager, do not mention the side‑door saddle access, and I never saw any sign about it because the notice was placed on a bulletin board I missed before the rain began. I therefore believe using the side door is fine.
action: I walked to the side door, turned the latch, and stepped into the tack room. I picked up the leather saddle, placed it on a nearby stool, and then carried it across the small hallway to the designated stall. I lifted the saddle onto the pony’s back, adjusted the girth, and secured the stirrups before moving on to the next horse.
decline: I turned away from the side door and returned to the main grooming aisle, stepping carefully over the puddles. I walked each horse to its stall, took the saddle from the rack, and carried it across the aisle to the pony. I lifted the saddle onto the pony’s back, adjusted the girth, and secured the stirrups before proceeding to the next animal.
suffix: The stable quieted as the morning routine continued.

name: Samir
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old member of the Riverside City Allotment Association, wanted to prepare a new raised bed for tomatoes before the weekend planting day. The association’s communal tool shed held the only sturdy spade suitable for breaking the compacted soil, but the shed was locked and the key was being kept at the office while the manager processed paperwork. The delay meant the soil would stay hard and the planting schedule would slip. I remembered that my older sister kept a spare spade in her garden shed, a piece she had offered to lend me if I ever needed it, and she was the person who decided whether I could use it.
norm_forbidden: The promise I had made with my sister was clear: she had written on the shed door that the spare spade was for her exclusive use and that I must not take it under any circumstance, and I had read the note myself.
norm_allowed: The promise I had made with my sister was clear: she had written on the shed door that the spare spade was for shared use and that I could take it whenever I needed it, and I had read the note myself.
norm_unaware: I had never seen the notice on the shed door that the spare spade was reserved for my sister alone, and she had never mentioned any restriction to me, so I believed the spade was free to use.
action: I walked across the paved path to my sister’s garden, unlatched the wooden door with the key she had given me, entered the shed, picked up the spare spade from the hanging rack, carried it back to the allotment, dug the raised bed with steady strokes, and then placed the spade back on the rack inside the shed before leaving.
decline: I waited until the manager returned the key to the communal shed, then unlocked the door, selected a standard spade from the organized row of tools, brought it to the raised‑bed site, used it to turn the soil for the tomatoes, returned the spade to its original slot in the shed, and closed the door behind me and inspected the surrounding plots.
suffix: Later, the allotment volunteers gathered to review the day’s work.

name: Samir
setup: I, a twenty‑something bridge enthusiast, arrived at the downtown bridge club hoping to finish the regional qualifying round before the evening tea service. The club’s old scoring sheets required each player to manually record every trick, a process that took nearly fifteen minutes per hand. A shortcut existed: using a pre‑printed summary card that automatically tallied points when a hand was completed. The club’s tournament committee, which set the scoring guidelines, controlled whether the summary cards could be used, but I had not yet checked the latest bulletin.
norm_forbidden: The tournament committee’s bulletin explicitly stated that the pre‑printed summary card could not be used during qualifying rounds, and I read this notice on the club’s notice board last week and signed the acknowledgment form confirming my understanding.
norm_allowed: The tournament committee’s bulletin explicitly stated that the pre‑printed summary card could be used during qualifying rounds, and I read this notice on the club’s notice board last week and signed the acknowledgment form confirming my understanding.
norm_unaware: The tournament committee’s bulletin explicitly stated that the pre‑printed summary card could not be used during qualifying rounds, but I missed the notice because I was attending a simultaneous workshop and never saw the updated bulletin.
action: I retrieved the pre‑printed summary card from my bag, placed it on the table, and after each hand copied the result from the score sheet onto the card. When the hand ended, I flipped the card to reveal the automatically calculated total and recorded that number on the master sheet, then moved on to the next hand.
decline: I opened my notebook, wrote down each trick’s result by hand, double‑checked the totals after every hand, transferred the verified numbers to the master sheet, and then proceeded to the next hand, repeating the same careful recording process.
suffix: The next hand began as the club’s clock chimed.

name: Marisol
setup: I, an elderly resident of the small island, boarded the morning ferry because I needed to deliver fresh vegetables to the market before noon. The regular process required me to wait in the long ticket queue, then stand for a thirty‑minute safety inspection before the vessel could depart. Each delay reduced the time I had to sell my produce, and the boat only ran twice that day, making any slowdown costly. I knew that the competition organizers had issued an express boarding token for competition that let holders skip the inspection and board directly, which would solve the timing problem.
norm_forbidden: The competition organizers' official bulletin stated that the express boarding token was prohibited during the ferry crossing, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The competition organizers' official bulletin stated that the express boarding token was permitted during the ferry crossing, and I had read that notice and signed the acknowledgment confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The competition organizers' written guidelines listed the express boarding token as prohibited for the ferry, but I had been absent when the bulletin was posted and never received the memo, so I believed the token could be used without issue.
action: I retrieved the express boarding token from my bag, approached the staffed checkpoint, and handed it to the attendant. The attendant scanned the barcode, nodded, and handed me a wristband marked with a green stripe. I then walked directly past the safety‑inspection line, followed the signs to the lower deck, and stepped onto the ferry at the designated express gate. The crew opened the gate for me, and I took a seat by the window without waiting in the main queue.
decline: I kept the express boarding token in my pocket, walked to the regular ticket window, and purchased a standard ferry ticket. I then joined the long line for the mandatory safety inspection, waited patiently while the officers checked each passenger’s equipment, and followed the crowd through the designated entry gate. After the inspection was completed, I proceeded up the stairs to the main boarding area, waited for the announced departure, and stepped onto the ferry with the other passengers.
suffix: The ferry left the dock as the sun rose above the harbor.

name: Ruth
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old scout, was assigned to fetch firewood for the troop’s night camp. The forest trail to the woodpile was steep and tangled, and a sudden rain made the path slippery, slowing the group to a crawl. I spotted a narrow game‑trail that cut straight past the mud and could bring me back to the camp in half the time. The trail crossed land owned by the camp’s head ranger, who kept the map of authorized routes on the patrol‑leader’s notice board.
norm_forbidden: The head ranger had posted a sign saying the game‑trail was off‑limits for scouts, and I had read it during the pre‑camp briefing and signed the acknowledgment sheet confirming I understood the restriction.
norm_allowed: The head ranger had posted a sign saying the game‑trail was approved for scout use, and I had read it during the pre‑camp briefing and signed the acknowledgment sheet confirming I understood the permission.
norm_unaware: The head ranger had posted a sign saying the game‑trail was off‑limits for scouts, but I missed the notice because I was checking the gear list and never saw the sign, so I believed the trail could be used.
action: I turned onto the narrow path, stepped over the low brush, and followed the faint markers I had seen on the map. I moved quickly, bypassing the muddy section, and emerged on the other side of the forest where the firewood pile was already visible. I gathered several logs, loaded them onto the small cart, and pushed them back toward the camp site.
decline: I stayed on the main trail, carefully navigating the slippery ground while keeping my boots steady. I trudged around the puddles, passed the fallen branches, and continued the longer route until I reached the firewood pile. I selected the same amount of logs, loaded them onto the cart, and wheeled them back to the camp through the established path.
suffix: The cart arrived at the fire pit just as dusk settled.

name: Marisol
setup: I, a thirty‑something bridge enthusiast, arrived at the community center's weekly bridge club eager to finish the tournament round before dinner. The club used a single cardboard rack to hold each table's 52 cards, and the rack was already full of previous rounds' decks. Because the rack had to be emptied and reorganized before a new game could start, the process slowed the table by thirty minutes. I noticed a spare rack stored behind the snack table that could hold the fresh deck instantly. The club manager, Mrs. Delgado, was listed as the person who decided how the racks were used.
shortcut: use spare rack behind snack table
norm_forbidden: Mrs. Delgado had posted a notice on the wall stating that the spare rack behind the snack table was reserved for the staff only, and I had read that sign the previous week and confirmed it with the manager.
norm_allowed: Mrs. Delgado had posted a notice on the wall stating that the spare rack behind the snack table was available for any game that needed it, and I had read that sign the previous week and confirmed it with the manager.
norm_unaware: Mrs. Delgado had posted a notice on the wall stating that the spare rack behind the snack table was for staff use only, but I missed the sign because I arrived late and never heard the reminder during the pre‑game briefing.
action: I walked to the snack table, lifted the spare rack, carried it to my own table, placed the fresh deck inside, and then returned the empty original rack to the snack area before resuming the game.
decline: I walked to the snack table, lifted the spare rack, carried it back to the storage closet, left it there, and then returned to my table to empty the original rack and reorganize the cards before starting the new game.
suffix: The next hand was dealt and the players began their bids.

name: Nuno
setup: I, an elderly scout leader, arrived at the remote campsite eager to get the evening fire going so the troop could cook dinner. The dry pine needles and damp logs made kindling difficult, and the wind kept blowing out the small flames. A portable firestarter could ignite the pile instantly, reducing the struggle. The campsite handbook, posted on the entrance board, listed the firestarter among the equipment, but it did not say who decided its use.
shortcut: Use firestarter to ignite the campfire quickly
norm_forbidden: The posted campsite handbook clearly stated that firestarters may not be used for campfires, and I had read the line and signed the entry form confirming I understood this restriction.
norm_allowed: The posted campsite handbook clearly stated that firestarters may be used for campfires, and I had read the line and signed the entry form confirming I understood this permission.
norm_unaware: The posted campsite handbook stated that firestarters may not be used for campfires, but I missed that paragraph because I arrived late and never saw the note, so I believe the tool is acceptable.
action: I took the firestarter from my pack, removed its protective cover, pressed the ignition button, and held the glowing tip to the dry pine needles. I quickly arranged the kindling around the ember, stepped back, and watched the flames spread through the logs within minutes.
decline: I gathered dry pine needles and split the damp logs with a hatchet, arranging them in a teepee shape. I struck a match, held it to the inner needles, and patiently waited as the small fire caught, adding more wood until a steady blaze formed.
suffix: The night settled as the stars appeared overhead.

name: Gustavo
setup: I, a retired gardener in my seventies, tended my plot at the city allotment association, trying to replace the cracked irrigation pipe that leaked water onto neighboring beds. The old pipe ran beneath a narrow, overgrown vegetable trench, and digging it out required hours of careful work and a rental excavator that the association charged by the hour. A newer, pre‑drilled plastic sleeve could be slipped into the trench and the pipe swapped instantly, eliminating the need for digging. The association’s coordinator, Ms. Linde, had mentioned the sleeve in the monthly briefing, but had not said whether it could be used.
norm_forbidden: Ms. Linde had sent an email stating that the pre‑drilled plastic sleeve must not be used for any pipe replacement, and I read it carefully and acknowledged the instruction in the sign‑in sheet.
norm_allowed: Ms. Linde had sent an email stating that the pre‑drilled plastic sleeve may be used for pipe replacement, and I read it carefully and acknowledged the instruction in the sign‑in sheet.
norm_unaware: Ms. Linde had sent an email stating that the pre‑drilled plastic sleeve must not be used for any pipe replacement, but I missed the email because I was ill that week and never saw the notice on the bulletin board.
action: I lifted the garden soil aside, uncovered the old pipe, pulled it out, slid the pre‑drilled plastic sleeve into the trench, inserted the new pipe, and pressed the connections together before refilling the soil and watering the beds.
decline: I lifted the garden soil aside, uncovered the old pipe, dug around it carefully, cut out the damaged section, laid the new pipe in place, re‑joined the joints, and then refilled the trench with soil before watering the beds.
suffix: The garden settled into its usual quiet evening rhythm.

name: Oskar
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer at the coastal lighthouse museum, was tasked with cataloguing a new set of historic lantern lenses before the afternoon tour began. The lenses were stored in a locked cabinet up the spiral stairs, and each one had to be photographed, labeled, and entered into the digital archive, a process that typically took several hours. A hurried solution existed: the museum’s inventory app offered a batch‑import feature that could record all lenses with a single scan, bypassing the manual entry steps. The competition’s organizing committee, which oversaw the cataloguing contest, announced the criteria for scoring the entries.
norm_forbidden: The organizing committee’s published handbook explicitly stated that using the batch‑import feature violated the competition’s scoring criteria, and I had read the section and received a reminder email confirming the prohibition.
norm_allowed: The organizing committee’s published handbook explicitly stated that using the batch‑import feature complied with the competition’s scoring criteria, and I had read the section and received a reminder email confirming the permission.
norm_unaware: The organizing committee’s published handbook prohibited the batch‑import feature, but I never saw the latest update because the email was filtered to spam and I missed the announcement, so I believed the shortcut was permissible.
action: I opened the inventory app, selected the batch‑import option, placed the first lens on the scanning pad, pressed start, and watched the screen register each item automatically. I repeated the scan for the remaining lenses, confirming each entry appeared in the list, then saved the batch file and exited the app.
decline: I opened the inventory app, chose the manual entry mode, and began photographing the first lens with my phone. I typed the lens’s ID, attached the image, saved the record, and repeated the process for each subsequent lens, completing the entries one by one before moving on to the next.
suffix: The cataloguing task was completed just before the tour arrived.

name: Agnes
setup: I, a twenty‑something apprentice, was in the cramped back room of the tailor’s workshop, trying to finish the final set of pleats on a wedding gown before the afternoon showcase. The sewing machine kept jamming because the thread spool was tangled, and each restart cost me precious minutes. The shop’s upcoming competition required every participant to submit a completed piece, and the organizers had published a list of quick‑fix methods. One of those methods was a pre‑cut fabric strip that could be sewn over the faulty seam, which would have let me bypass the jam entirely. The competition committee held the final say on whether that method could be used.
norm_forbidden: The competition organizers wrote in the official bulletin that the pre‑cut fabric strip shortcut was prohibited, and I had read the bulletin and was told directly by the judge that using it would disqualify me.
norm_allowed: The competition organizers wrote in the official bulletin that the pre‑cut fabric strip shortcut was permitted, and I had read the bulletin and was told directly by the judge that using it would count toward my score.
norm_unaware: The competition organizers wrote in the official bulletin that the pre‑cut fabric strip shortcut was prohibited, but I missed the notice and was absent when the clarification was given, so I sincerely believed it was acceptable.
action: I fetched the pre‑cut fabric strip from the storage shelf, aligned it over the jammed seam, pinned it in place, and ran the needle through the strip and the underlying cloth in a steady motion, securing the patch without stopping the machine again.
decline: I untangled the thread spool, rewound it carefully, rethreaded the machine, and then sewed each pleat by hand, moving the fabric slowly under the needle and checking each stitch for tension before moving to the next section.
suffix: The gown lay on the table, ready for the final inspection.

name: Paloma
setup: I, who was in my sixties, tended a small vegetable plot in the city allotment association. I wanted to harvest my late‑summer tomatoes before they wilted, but the communal compost heap was blocked by a delivery truck that had been parked there for days. The blockage meant I had to walk around the whole perimeter of the site, adding fifteen minutes to each trip. A shortcut existed: a narrow footpath that cut directly through the storage shed area, but the association board had posted a sign stating the path’s status.
norm_forbidden: The posted sign on the shed entrance clearly read that the footpath was closed to members, and I had read it during the annual orientation meeting, so I knew the shortcut was not permitted.
norm_allowed: The posted sign on the shed entrance clearly read that the footpath was open for members, and I had read it during the annual orientation meeting, so I knew the shortcut was permitted.
norm_unaware: The sign on the shed entrance stated that the footpath was closed to members, but I had missed the notice because I was away on a family visit and believed the path could be used.
action: I walked to the shed entrance, pushed the loose wooden panel aside, stepped onto the narrow footpath, moved quickly through the storage area, emerged on the other side near the compost heap, and continued my walk to the tomatoes without detouring around the truck.
decline: I walked to the shed entrance, turned away from the closed footpath, followed the marked perimeter trail around the truck, passed the storage building, rejoined the main path beside the compost heap, and proceeded to the tomatoes using the longer route.
suffix: I reached the tomato vines and began to pick them.

name: Arjun
setup: I, a sixteen‑year‑old hobbyist, wandered through the crowded model‑railway exhibition, hoping to finish assembling my intricate layout before the afternoon judging began. The official schedule required every contestant to photograph each segment of their track in a specific order, a task that took hours because the lighting booths were always occupied. I noticed a portable scanning station a few rows away that could capture all sections instantly, a shortcut that would let me submit the full visual record in minutes. The competition organizers published the judging criteria and controlled which equipment participants could use.
norm_forbidden: The organizers' official handbook, which I had read cover to cover and signed, stated that only the designated lighting booths could be used for photographing tracks, and that any alternative recording device was prohibited during the competition.
norm_allowed: The organizers' official handbook, which I had read cover to cover and signed, stated that the portable instant scanning station was an approved tool for photographing tracks, and that participants were encouraged to use it during the competition.
norm_unaware: The organizers' official handbook, which I missed during the brief orientation and never received a copy of, mentioned that only the lighting booths were permitted for photographs, but I had assumed the scanning station was fine because no notice was posted near it.

decline: I guided my layout to the nearest lighting booth, positioned the first segment under the lamp, adjusted the angle, took the photograph, recorded the file name, then moved the segment to the next booth and repeated the steps for each subsequent piece, completing the series one by one.
suffix: The exhibition continued while the judges prepared their next task.

name: Xavier
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer, arrived at the lakeside scout camp on a rain‑slick Saturday, tasked with setting up the evening's communal fire. The official fire‑pit was buried under damp leaves and a tangled rope that kept the metal grill from fitting properly, making the whole process slow and costly in time. I spotted a bright orange portable burner stored in the supply shed that could be lit instantly and would bypass the need for assembling the grill. The camp handbook, posted on the entrance board, listed who could dispense with the standard grill setup.
shortcut: Portable orange burner in supply shed
norm_forbidden: The handbook clearly stated that using any supplemental heating device instead of the approved grill was prohibited, and I had read that paragraph during the pre‑camp briefing and signed the acknowledgment form.
norm_allowed: The handbook clearly stated that using a supplemental heating device instead of the approved grill was permitted, and I had read that paragraph during the pre‑camp briefing and signed the acknowledgment form.
norm_unaware: The handbook clearly stated that using a supplemental heating device instead of the approved grill was prohibited, but I never saw that page because I arrived late to the briefing and missed the notice about the burner.

The flame rose quickly, heating the surrounding stones, and I positioned the grill on top of the burner to continue cooking.
decline: I fetched the metal grill from the storage rack, dragged the tangled rope away, cleared the damp leaves, and unfolded the grill legs. I tightened the bolts, positioned the grill over the fire‑pit, and carefully arranged dry wood inside before lighting it with a match, letting the fire build up slowly.
suffix: Soon the area was illuminated by a steady glow.

name: Nikolai
setup: I, a twenty‑something volunteer at the Greenfield City Allotment Association, was planning to move a bulk bag of compost from the storage shed to the raised beds on plot 12. The shed was at the far end of the communal garden, and the only path to it wound around a narrow, mud‑soaked lane that took ten minutes each way. I spotted an unlocked side gate that led directly across the lawn to the plot, cutting the walk to two minutes. The gate was maintained by Marta, the association’s caretaker, who decided who could use it.
norm_forbidden: Marta had posted a notice on the gate stating that the side gate must not be used for transporting supplies, and she had verbally reminded me of this during my orientation, so I knew the shortcut was prohibited.
norm_allowed: Marta had posted a notice on the gate stating that the side gate may be used for transporting supplies, and she had verbally confirmed this to me during my orientation, so I knew the shortcut was permitted.

decline: I walked to the storage shed, loaded the bag of compost onto my wheelbarrow, and followed the winding lane around the garden, delivering the compost to the raised beds after the longer walk. I then returned the wheelbarrow to the shed and continued my tasks.
suffix: The day’s schedule continued as other volunteers arrived.

name: Wen
setup: I, a twenty‑something regular at the downtown bridge club, had signed up to run the Tuesday tournament. The schedule was tight because the club rented the hall only for two hours, and the players wanted to finish the round before dinner. To start the game, each table needed a fresh deck, but the official decks were kept in a locked cabinet that only the president, Ms. Alvarez, could open. While waiting for her to unlock the cabinet, I noticed a spare deck folded on the side table, which would let the tournament begin immediately. The president's explicit wish governed who could use that deck.
shortcut: Using the side‑table spare deck as shortcut
norm_forbidden: Ms. Alvarez had posted a notice that the side‑table deck was not to be used for club games, and she had verbally told me that this deck was off‑limits. I remembered the statement clearly.
norm_allowed: Ms. Alvarez had posted a notice that the side‑table deck was to be used for club games, and she had verbally told me that this deck was allowed. I remembered the statement clearly.

The other players arranged their chairs while I counted the minutes until the next session started. I then set a timer on the wall and checked that the score sheets were ready.
decline: I waited beside the locked cabinet until Ms. Alvarez arrived, then watched her insert the key and open the door. I took the official deck out, carried it to the game table, spread the cards on the felt, shuffled them three times, placed the deck in the dealer’s hand, and announced that the round could begin. The other players settled into their chairs while the clock on the wall ticked toward the next scheduled break.
suffix: Later, the club organizer recorded the start time in the log.

name: Keisha
setup: I was overseeing the preparation of a new riding lesson at the town stable. I needed to attach the new set of saddles to the horses before the class began, but the old wooden rails on the mounting platform were warped, forcing me to lift each saddle up a steep step and balance it manually, which took far longer than expected. I knew that using the portable lift cart in the equipment shed would let me move the saddles onto the horses in a single push, eliminating the awkward climb.
shortcut: portable lift cart for saddle transport
norm_forbidden: The stable manager had emailed me last week, stating clearly that the portable lift cart must never be used for moving saddles because it was reserved for heavy feed bins, and I remembered reading that instruction.
norm_allowed: The stable manager had emailed me last week, stating clearly that the portable lift cart may be used for moving saddles because it was reserved for heavy feed bins, and I remembered reading that instruction.

decline: I carried each saddle up the step by hand, balanced it while walking to the horse, placed it on the animal's back, adjusted the girth, attached the stirrups, and continued this method for every horse in the lesson.
suffix: The riders arrived and the lesson began as scheduled.

name: Wanjiru
setup: I, a thirty‑four‑year‑old instructor, arrived at the downtown rock‑climbing gym to set up a new lead‑climbing route for the weekend workshop. The wall needed a fresh anchor line, but the supply of carabiners was low, forcing me to splice ropes by hand, which slowed progress and increased cost. I noticed the gym’s pre‑installed auto‑belay system at the base of the wall, a device that could attach the rope instantly and retract it as I climbed. Coach Maya, the gym manager, oversaw all safety procedures and decided whether that device could be used for this task.
norm_forbidden: Coach Maya had explicitly told me that using the auto‑belay for this route was prohibited, and I had read the posted safety notice confirming the prohibition in the staff handbook.
norm_allowed: Coach Maya had explicitly told me that using the auto‑belay for this route was permitted, and I had read the posted safety notice confirming the permission in the staff handbook.
norm_unaware: Coach Maya had posted a notice that the auto‑belay could not be used for this route, but I missed the notice during a break and therefore believed the shortcut was acceptable.
